display.story_text:
Thurman "Tops" Whitsitt has cut hair in Warren County for three decades, and he saved a chair for Hen Lofland. The Newark librarian is not sitting down. She just watched her quarterback throw five touchdown passes.

Delaware (3-4) at Western Kentucky (3-4), Tuesday at 7:00 p.m. ET on CBSSN at Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium in Bowling Green. It's a Conference USA game. DraftKings has Western Kentucky Hilltoppers −1.5 with a total of 55.5. My card: Western Kentucky Hilltoppers −1.5, Over 55.5, and a final of Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 30, Delaware Blue Hens 27.

Hen speaks for Delaware, and she has a new entry for the card catalog. "Nick Minicucci is back on the shelf where he belongs. He went 20 of 29 for 225 yards and five touchdown passes in a 61-38 win over Missouri State, and Jo Silver ran for 101."

Tops speaks for Western Kentucky, and he keeps sweeping while he talks. "Hen, darlin', we've won two straight in this league. We beat Missouri State 34-13 and went to Huntsville and won 16-3. And Jaylen Lewis has 56 tackles. That man never misses a customer."

The honest part: Delaware scores 28.3 a game, WKU allows 30.6. But WKU gave up 49, 70 and 38 at Nevada, Georgia and Indiana, then 13 and 3 in its last two.

Why Western Kentucky? Home field, a defense that has found itself, and a Delaware ground game that runs for 3.6 yards a carry. In The Trenches is on the Hilltoppers for exactly that reason. The market agrees: DraftKings opened WKU at +1.5, and now WKU lays the 1.5. My final has WKU by three, clear of the 1.5.

The worry is the Hilltopper quarterback room. Rodney Tisdale Jr. leads in passing with 857 yards, but Brock Glenn threw the most passes in each of the last two games, and he went 14 of 30 at Sam Houston. If WKU stalls and Minicucci gets hot again, a field goal decides it.

Why the Over? Delaware has scored 61 and 30 in its last two games, and the Blue Hens' defense gives up 28.4 a game. Missouri State put 38 on it last week. My 30-27 adds up to 57, a point and a half over 55.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up is the loudest Hilltopper fan here, with WKU 31-26 and the Over. The Formula has WKU 28-27, a one-point win, so it takes Delaware +1.5 and the Under. Follow The Money and In The Trenches both like WKU, and both say Under. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up started it: "The Formula, you've got the Hilltoppers winning and you're taking the points? That's paying for the haircut and skipping the trim."

The Formula didn't flinch: "One point is one point. Ask Delaware about 33-30 at Middle Tennessee."

Follow The Money chimed in: "I'm with you on the side, Next Man Up. On the total, you're on your own."

Bottom of the card: a home team that has won two straight in the league, last season's 27-24 win in this series, and a road offense that has to throw. Tops gets his chair back. Give me the Hilltoppers and the Over.

Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 30, Delaware Blue Hens 27. Western Kentucky Hilltoppers cover the 1.5. Over 55.5.

Tuesday Night on the Hill: Minicucci's Five-Touchdown Night Meets a Hilltopper Defense That Found Its Footing

Delaware (3-4, 1-2 CUSA) at Western Kentucky (3-4, 2-1 CUSA). Tuesday, Oct. 27, 7 p.m. ET, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green, Ky., CBS Sports Network.

Your hosts are Thurman "Tops" Whitsitt, a Warren County barber with three decades of Hilltopper stories, and Hen Lofland, the Newark librarian who loves the wing-T.

Tops: Go Tops! Have a seat, Hen. The first cut is free, and the conversation is better than the haircut.

Hen: I brought my library card and a bookmark. I'll be taking notes.

Players to watch

Delaware quarterback Nick Minicucci is 79 of 132 for 1,063 yards, 10 touchdowns and four interceptions. Jo Silver leads the Blue Hens with 331 rushing yards and two touchdowns, and wide receiver Sean Wilson has 31 catches for 408 yards and three scores. On defense, linebacker Blake Matthews has 4.5 sacks and linebacker Gavin Moul leads the team with 46 tackles.

Western Kentucky's passing leader is Rodney Tisdale Jr., 80 of 119 for 857 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions. Brock Glenn threw the most passes in each of the last two games, and both were wins. Ajay Allen leads the rushers with 346 yards and four touchdowns, and wide receiver Jonathan Stafford Jr. has 41 catches for 369 yards. Defensive back Jaylen Lewis leads the Hilltoppers with 56 tackles, and linebacker Westen Ard has 2.5 sacks.

Tops: Forty-one catches. Jonathan Stafford Jr. has more regulars than my shop.

What happened last week

Delaware beat Missouri State 61-38 on Oct. 20 for its first Conference USA win of the season. Minicucci went 20 of 29 for 225 yards and five touchdown passes. Silver ran 13 times for 101 yards and a score, and Wilson caught six passes for 69 yards.

Hen: Sixty-one points. I had to cross-reference the scoreboard twice.

Western Kentucky had an open week after a 16-3 win at Sam Houston on Oct. 14. Glenn went 14 of 30 for 127 yards and a touchdown and also carried 22 times for 54 yards. The week before that, the Hilltoppers beat Missouri State 34-13 at home.

Tops: Two straight league wins. In the shop, we call that a good week for business.

Injuries and availability

Conference USA has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either team, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Neither school's box scores mark a starting quarterback. Minicucci threw the most passes for Delaware last week, and Glenn did for Western Kentucky in each of its last two games.

What the coaches are up to

Tyson Helton leads Western Kentucky, and CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Nov. 27, 2018. His teams went 9-5, 9-5, 8-5, 8-6 and 9-4 from 2021 through 2025. This year's group took its lumps early at Nevada, Georgia and Indiana, then allowed just 13 and 3 points in its last two games.

Ryan Carty is in his fifth season at Delaware. He led the Blue Hens' move to FBS and Conference USA, and Delaware is the 2025 68 Ventures Bowl champion. His offense scores 28.3 points a game.

Tops: Coach Helton has been in Bowling Green long enough to have a standing appointment.

Hen: Coach Carty brought a whole program up a level. That deserves its own shelf.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is Minicucci and Wilson against Lewis and the Hilltopper secondary. Lewis leads both rosters in tackles. On the other side, Matthews and his 4.5 sacks will test whichever Western Kentucky quarterback takes the snaps. The Blue Hens run for 3.6 yards a carry, so the big guys up front for WKU can make life hard if they win early.

What's happening on campus

Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium was built in 1968 and lists a capacity of 22,113. The fight song is "Stand Up and Cheer!" and the band is the Big Red Marching Band. And if you visit, ask somebody about Big Red, the mascot Hilltopper fans love to show off first.

Anything else fun and true

These two met last season, and Western Kentucky won 27-24, so Delaware arrives with a three-point memory. The Blue Hens claim six national titles, from 1946 to 2003, and produced quarterbacks Rich Gannon and Joe Flacco.

Hen: Six national titles, catalogued, alphabetized and dusted weekly.

Tops: And we've got Big Red. Pull up a chair, Hen. The game's about to start, and the coffee's on me.

My call: Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 30, Delaware Blue Hens 27.

display.story_text:
Lem Coxwell teaches history in Walker County, and he says every Texas tale has a turn. Clementine Bilyeu guides float trips in the Ozarks, and she says the river decides where you land.

Sam Houston (1-6) at Missouri State (2-5), Tuesday at 8:00 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at Robert W. Plaster Stadium in Springfield. It's a Conference USA game, and these two haven't met in the regular season since at least 2016. DraftKings has Missouri State Bears −6 with a total of 52.5. My card: Sam Houston Bearkats +6, Over 52.5, and a final of Missouri State Bears 29, Sam Houston Bearkats 25.

Clementine speaks for Missouri State, and she leads with her paddle. "Lem, honey, Isaiah Myers caught 11 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns last week. He has 796 yards and seven scores on the year. When the current's this strong, you hold on."

Lem speaks for Sam Houston, and he opens his grade book. "Ma'am, Landyn Locke has 1,653 passing yards and 12 touchdowns. Tim Burns Jr. caught four for 117 last week. We lost 24-21 at Troy, 23-17 to Tulsa and 30-24 to New Mexico State. Every chapter came down to the last page."

That's the Bearkat case in one breath: 1-6, but three of those losses came by six points or fewer.

Why Sam Houston? Missouri State hasn't earned this many. The Bears allow 34.9 points a game. They just gave up 61 at Delaware, and Western Kentucky beat them 34-13 a week before WKU beat Sam Houston 16-3. My final has Missouri State by four, which keeps the Bearkats inside the 6.

The risk is the Sam Houston offense. The Bearkats score 20.1 points a game, managed 3 against Liberty and 3 against Western Kentucky, and run for 2.9 yards a carry. If Locke can't find Burns, a four-point game turns into ten in a hurry.

Why the Over? This is the Missouri State defense, which has allowed 30 or more in five of seven games, against a Sam Houston quarterback who just threw for 235. Henry Belin IV has thrown the most passes for the Bears in each of the last two games, and he threw for 337 at Delaware. My 29-25 adds up to 54, a point and a half over 52.5.

Now the room, and everybody who takes a side takes Sam Houston. The Formula has Missouri State 27-25 and likes the Bearkats with the Under. Next Man Up has Missouri State 30-25, also takes Sam Houston +6, and goes Over with me. Follow The Money skips the side and likes the Over. In The Trenches sits this one out, and Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up started it: "The Formula, two points? You think this is a library?"

The Formula shrugged: "Two points or five, it's still Sam Houston plus six. We agree on the part that matters."

Follow The Money smiled: "Then I'll take the part you're arguing about. Over."

Bottom of the card: a road team that loses close, a home defense that gives up a lot, and six points in a game my final calls by four. Clementine gets her current. Lem gets his turn. I'll take the points.

Missouri State Bears 29, Sam Houston Bearkats 25. Sam Houston Bearkats cover the 6. Over 52.5.

Tuesday Night in Springfield: Isaiah Myers and the Bears Host a Bearkat Team That Keeps Coming Back

Sam Houston (1-6, 0-3 CUSA) at Missouri State (2-5, 1-2 CUSA). Tuesday, Oct. 27, 7 p.m. CT (8 p.m. ET), Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield, Mo., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Clementine Bilyeu, the Missouri State float-trip guide from the Ozarks, and Lem Coxwell, a Walker County history teacher and Texas folklore collector.

Clementine: Howdy from the Ozarks! Lem, you're on my river tonight. Life jackets are by the door.

Lem: Evenin', ma'am. Pull up a stump. Tonight's chapter is called "The Long Road North."

Players to watch

Missouri State wide receiver Isaiah Myers is the headliner: 38 catches for 796 yards and seven touchdowns. Henry Belin IV has thrown the most passes for the Bears in each of the last two games and is 73 of 108 for 887 yards, six touchdowns and four interceptions. Ramone Green Jr. leads the rushers with 246 yards and two scores. Linebacker Jared Lloyd leads the team with 80 tackles, and defensive end Josh Lukusa has 1.5 sacks.

Sam Houston quarterback Landyn Locke is 147 of 236 for 1,653 yards, 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. Wide receiver Tim Burns Jr. has 15 catches for 329 yards and three scores, more than 20 yards a catch. Alton McCaskill leads the rushers with 220 yards. Linebacker Dean Ford leads the Bearkats with 44 tackles, and linebacker Elijah Groves has 2.5 sacks.

Clementine: Eighty tackles. Jared Lloyd shows up to every float on time and carries everybody's cooler.

What happened last week

Missouri State lost 61-38 at Delaware on Oct. 20, but Myers had a night to remember: 11 catches for 242 yards and two touchdowns. Belin went 26 of 35 for 337 yards and two scores, and Connor Lair ran 15 times for 85 yards and two touchdowns.

Clementine: Two hundred forty-two yards. I had to check the river gauge twice.

Sam Houston lost 30-24 to New Mexico State on Oct. 21 in Huntsville. Locke went 18 of 31 for 235 yards and a touchdown, Burns caught four passes for 117 yards and a score, and MJ Dowdy ran one in.

Lem: Six points short. Every Texas tale has a turn, and ours is coming.

Injuries and availability

Conference USA has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either team, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Box scores don't mark starters, but Belin threw the most passes for Missouri State in each of its last two games, and Locke has done it in every Sam Houston game this season.

What the coaches are up to

Casey Woods is in his first season at Missouri State after serving as SMU's offensive coordinator. His Bears beat Kennesaw State 24-21 on Oct. 14 for their first FBS win under him, and the offense has scored 38 or more twice this season.

Phil Longo is in his second season at Sam Houston. He was named the program's 16th head coach in December 2024, and he's an air raid coach who previously ran offenses at Wisconsin, North Carolina and Ole Miss. Locke has thrown for at least 300 yards three times this year.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is Myers against a Sam Houston defense that allows 25.3 points a game. On the other side, Locke and Burns face a Missouri State defense that allows 34.9 points a game. Both teams struggle to run it: Sam Houston gains 2.9 yards a carry and Missouri State 3.9, so the big guys up front on both sides have plenty to prove.

Clementine: When the river's low, you paddle harder. Isaiah's our paddle.

What's happening on campus

Tuesday brings a fresh matchup to Springfield: these two have no regular-season meetings from 2016 through 2025. Missouri State became a full FBS member in 2026, and this is its first FBS season.

Anything else fun and true

Missouri State first fielded a football team in 1909 and was known as Southwest Missouri State until 2005. Sam Houston's close calls this year include a 24-21 loss at Troy in the opener and a 23-17 loss to Tulsa, and its lone win was a 59-0 shutout of Nicholls. Both teams also share a common opponent: Western Kentucky beat Missouri State 34-13 and Sam Houston 16-3.

Clementine: Pack a snack, Lem. It's going to be a fun float.

Lem: Ma'am, I brought a whole history book. Let's write a new page.

My call: Missouri State Bears 29, Sam Houston Bearkats 25.

display.story_text:
Opal Stonebriar has a pan of biscuits warming in Murfreesboro and a fresh page open in Grandmama's ledger. Ximena Holcombe-Reyes has a laptop, a bug list and one commit message she keeps pushing: we lose close, and close is the whole story.

Kennesaw State (1-6) at Middle Tennessee (4-3), Wednesday at 7:00 p.m. ET on CBSSN at Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium in Murfreesboro. It's a Conference USA game. DraftKings has Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders −2.5 with a total of 50.5. My card: Kennesaw State Owls +2.5, Under 50.5, and a final of Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 24, Kennesaw State Owls 23.

Opal speaks for Middle Tennessee. "Sugar, we have won two in a row, 33-30 over Delaware and 26-23 at FIU, and Terrence Brown ran for 158 yards in Miami. Roman Gagliano has 12 touchdown passes and two interceptions. Grandmama would call that a tidy book."

Ximena speaks for Kennesaw State. "Tidy, sure. Check the version history. Last September we beat you 24-16. This year we lost 17-14 at Arkansas State, 27-26 to Jacksonville State and 24-21 at Missouri State. Teams like yours do not blow us out. They beat us by a whisker."

Here is the part that matters. Every one of Middle Tennessee's wins over an FBS team came by seven points or fewer: 27-20 over Nevada, 33-30 over Delaware, 26-23 at FIU. This home team wins by a field goal, not a landslide.

Why Kennesaw State? Because 2.5 points is real breathing room in a game built to be decided late. Three of the Owls' losses came by three points or fewer, and Rickie Collins carries the offense with 1,426 passing yards plus five rushing touchdowns. My final has the Blue Raiders by one, so the Owls stay inside the number.

The worry is last Thursday. Collins threw two interceptions in a 34-6 loss to Liberty, and Jerry Mack went to Landon Varnes late in the fourth quarter. In The Trenches also points out that Middle Tennessee runs for 5.1 yards a carry against a defense that allows 4.3. If the Owls turn it over early, the Blue Raiders pull away.

Why the Over/Under? Neither offense scares anyone. Kennesaw State scores 20.0 a game and Middle Tennessee 23.3. The last two meetings finished 14-5 and 24-16. DraftKings had this total at 48.5 on Monday, and the climb to 50.5 only hands the Under more room. My 24-23 adds up to 47, three and a half under the over/under 50.5.

Now the room. The Formula has Middle Tennessee 24-23, my exact final, with Kennesaw State and the Under. Next Man Up has the Blue Raiders 23-22, same side, same Under. In The Trenches likes Middle Tennessee. Follow The Money skips the side and likes the Over. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

In The Trenches: "Two of you have Middle Tennessee winning and you both take Kennesaw State? Somebody check the scoreboard."

The Formula: "One point is not two and a half. That is the whole job."

Follow The Money: "And I am the only one in here who thinks anybody scores. Cozy."

Bottom of the card: a home team that wins close against a road team that loses close. Opal keeps the biscuits. Ximena keeps the points.

Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 24, Kennesaw State Owls 23. Kennesaw State Owls cover the 2.5. Under 50.5.

Wednesday Night at Floyd: Gagliano's Blue Raiders Try to Make It Three Straight Against a Kennesaw State Team That Plays Everyone Close

Kennesaw State (1-6, 0-3 CUSA) at Middle Tennessee (4-3, 2-1 CUSA). Wednesday, Oct. 28, 7 p.m. ET, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro, Tenn., CBS Sports Network.

Your hosts are Opal Stonebriar, a Murfreesboro biscuit baker who keeps Grandmama's ledger of every Blue Raiders game, and Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, a Marietta coder who has cheered Kennesaw State since version 1.0.

Opal: Come on in, sugar. The biscuits are warm.

Ximena: I brought my laptop. I'm logging every snap.

Players to watch

Middle Tennessee quarterback Roman Gagliano is 126 of 215 for 1,404 yards, 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Antonio Martin leads the rushers with 480 yards, and wide receiver Cam'ron Lacy has 41 catches for 437 yards and four scores. Linebacker Korey Smith leads the defense with 66 tackles.

Kennesaw State's Rickie Collins does a little of everything. He is 144 of 210 for 1,426 yards with four touchdowns, and he is also the Owls' leading rusher with 295 yards and five touchdowns. Wide receiver Brayden Munroe has 22 catches for 352 yards. Linebacker Tywon Christopher leads the team with 54 tackles, and defensive lineman Ugonna Nwoha has three sacks.

Ximena: Collins is basically the whole app. Passing module, running module, all of it.

What happened last week

Middle Tennessee won 26-23 at FIU on Oct. 20. Gagliano went 16 of 27 for 200 yards and a touchdown, and Terrence Brown ran 18 times for 158 yards and a score. Lacy caught six passes for 68 yards. That came a week after a 33-30 home win over Delaware.

Opal: One hundred fifty-eight yards for Terrence Brown. Grandmama underlined that one twice.

Kennesaw State lost 34-6 to Liberty on Oct. 22. Collins went 15 of 26 for 124 yards, and Munroe caught three passes for 53 yards. Linebacker Baron Hopson made a season-high 12 tackles. Late in the fourth quarter, coach Jerry Mack gave Landon Varnes some snaps at quarterback.

Ximena: Not our best build. Patch notes are coming.

Injuries and availability

Conference USA has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Neither school's box scores mark a starter. Gagliano has thrown the most passes for Middle Tennessee in every game this season, and Collins has done the same for Kennesaw State.

What the coaches are up to

Derek Mason is in his third season at Middle Tennessee, after coaching Vanderbilt from 2014 to 2020. His Blue Raiders went 3-9 in both 2024 and 2025, so four wins already tops last season. Three of those wins came by seven points or fewer.

Jerry Mack is in his second season at Kennesaw State. He went 31-15 as head coach at North Carolina Central and later worked at Rice. His Owls are the defending Conference USA champions, and three of their six losses this year came by three points or fewer.

Opal: Coach Mason has us winning the close ones. Grandmama always said a win by three still goes in the ledger.

Player storylines

Gagliano has been steady all season. He threw two touchdown passes in each of the first four games and three against Delaware.

In the Owls' 27-26 loss to Jacksonville State on Oct. 7, he threw for 293 yards. Hopson was a big part of last year's title team, with 138 tackles.

Ximena: Hopson tackles like he's closing tickets. Twelve last week, and he wants more.

What's happening on campus

Middle Tennessee is calling this one Halloween at Floyd, a few days before the real thing. For Kennesaw State, it's a short week and only the second trip to Murfreesboro in program history.

Opal: Halloween at Floyd! I'm dressing as a biscuit, and I'm not sorry.

Ximena: I'm coming as a semicolon. Nobody will get it.

Anything else fun and true

These two have split their last two meetings, both low scoring. Middle Tennessee won 14-5 in 2024, and Kennesaw State won 24-16 last September in Kennesaw. Both teams have also played Jacksonville State close this year: the Gamecocks beat Middle Tennessee 23-13 and Kennesaw State 27-26.

Opal: Fourteen to five. Grandmama wrote that one in pencil because she couldn't believe it.

Ximena: One to one in the version history. Tonight is the tiebreaker commit.

Opal: Biscuits for both sidelines, sugar. But I know which side gets the honey.

Ximena: Fair. Let's go, Owls.

My call: Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 24, Kennesaw State Owls 23.

display.fanatic_story:
Wednesday Night in Las Cruces: Unbeaten-in-League Jax State Comes Off the Bye to Face James Jones and the Aggie Ground Game

Jacksonville State (5-2, 3-0 CUSA) at New Mexico State (3-4, 2-1 CUSA). Wednesday, Oct. 28, 8 p.m. ET, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces, N.M., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Burl Ashcraft-Neeley, a Calhoun County barbecue pitmaster who has never lived more than ten miles from campus, and Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, a chile farmer's daughter from Las Cruces who grades every play on a chile-pepper scale.

Burl: Low and slow wins the fourth quarter! I brought brisket for the whole press box.

Esperanza: ¡Bienvenidos, Burl! I brought green chile. We'll see whose cooler empties first.

Players to watch

Jacksonville State runs through quarterback Caden Creel. He is 129 of 192 for 1,637 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions, and he is also the team's leading rusher with 500 yards and four scores. Wide receiver Deondre Johnson has 22 catches for 431 yards and three touchdowns. Safety Caleb Nix leads the defense with 43 tackles and two interceptions, and defensive lineman Tae Floyd has two sacks.

New Mexico State's headliner is running back James Jones, a Delaware State transfer who leads Conference USA with 777 rushing yards on 119 carries. Defensive end Gabe Peterson has 5.5 sacks, safety Nick Session leads the team with 52 tackles, and wide receiver TK King has 23 catches for 307 yards and three scores.

Esperanza: Seven hundred seventy-seven yards. That's Hatch hot, Burl.

What happened last week

New Mexico State won 30-24 at Sam Houston on Oct. 21. Jones ran 27 times for 178 yards and a touchdown, Adam Damante went 19 of 29 for 160 yards and two touchdowns, and AJ Williams III caught two of them.

Jacksonville State had an open week. Its last game was a 27-24 home win over FIU on Oct. 13. Creel went 16 of 22 for 214 yards and two touchdowns and ran 19 times for 95 yards, and Johnson caught four passes for 93 yards and a score.

Burl: An open week is not a day off, friends. It's a deep breath and a clean grill.

Injuries and availability

Conference USA has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Neither school's box scores mark a starter. Creel has thrown the most passes for Jacksonville State in every game, and Damante has done it for New Mexico State in each of the last four games.

What the coaches are up to

Jacksonville State's head coach is in his second season with the Gamecocks. His first team went 9-5, and this one is 3-0 in league play. During the bye he said the focus was fundamentals and doing your job "for six seconds at a time."

Tony Sanchez is an NMSU alum and former Aggie wide receiver who coached UNLV from 2014 to 2019. The Jax State coach says the two are friends, and he called the Aggies' ground game "the best running attack that we played against."

Esperanza: When the other coach says it, Burl, it's not bragging. It's a weather report.

Player storylines

The big matchup is Jones against the Jacksonville State front. The Gamecocks hold opponents to 4.2 yards a carry, and the Aggies run for 4.6. On the other side, the Aggie defense allows just 3.3 yards a carry, and Peterson has been chasing quarterbacks all season.

Creel has had a busy year. He threw five touchdown passes against Eastern Kentucky and 311 yards at Kennesaw State. The Gamecocks have won three straight close ones: 31-27, 27-26 and 27-24.

Burl: Three close wins in a row. That's slow-smoked football, and I like it tender.

What's happening on campus

This is the longest Conference USA road trip of the season for Jacksonville State, a long way from AmFirst Stadium and the Marching Southerners. Out in Las Cruces, the Organ Mountains will be watching over Aggie Memorial Stadium.

Esperanza: Welcome to the desert, Burl. Leave the humidity at home.

Burl: I brought the smoker. That's all the humidity I need.

Anything else fun and true

The series is tied 1-1. New Mexico State won 20-17 in 2023, and Jacksonville State won 54-13 at home in 2024 behind five rushing touchdowns. Both teams have played FIU this year: the Gamecocks won 27-24, and the Aggies lost 22-3.

Esperanza: One win each. Wednesday settles the chile cook-off.

Burl: Brisket versus green chile. Friends, nobody loses that kind of cook-off.

My call: Jacksonville State Gamecocks 27, New Mexico State Aggies 26.

Grady Mayhew-Ochoa has his headphones on in Denton, and the North Texas offense is still playing in 7/8 time. Kaia Brightwater drove in from Boca Raton with a swell report, a tempo offense and one honest admission: the Florida Atlantic defense has been flat water on the road.

Florida Atlantic (5-2) at North Texas (5-2), Thursday at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN at DATCU Stadium in Denton. It's an American game. DraftKings has North Texas Mean Green −13.5 with a total of 77.5. Grady: Mean Green, baby! Welcome to Denton, Kaia. Our offense plays in 7/8 time.

Kaia: Surf's up on tempo, babe. We brought our own rhythm.

Players to watch

North Texas quarterback Tayven Jackson is 160 of 221 for 2,173 yards, 18 touchdowns and five interceptions. Running back Jahiem White has 861 yards and 11 touchdowns on 116 carries, and wide receiver Justin Stevenson has 41 catches for 662 yards and seven scores. Kaia: Fifty-one to forty-nine. Perfect swell day, and my heart rate is still recovering.

Zach Kittley is in his second season at Florida Atlantic. He was named the Hagerty Family Head Football Coach on Dec. 2, 2024. His Owls throw it all over the yard and score 37.3 points a game.

North Texas has won the last three meetings: 41-38 in 2018, 45-28 in 2022 and 41-37 in 2024. Florida Atlantic won both games in 2017, 69-31 and 41-17. Big scores are a tradition in this series. Both teams also came into this week at 5-2.

Grady: Sixty-nine points in 2017. That's a seven-minute guitar solo.

Kaia: And we'd love an encore, babe.

Grady: Not in my house. Mean Green, baby.

Goose Crowder is nursing a shoulder, and Coach Parker is still working out a quarterback plan. But Donnie Smith has six sacks, and we gave you all you wanted in 2023, 16-14."

Here is the part that matters. James Madison will play this one without George Pettaway, its leading rusher with 824 yards and eight touchdowns, per the Daily News-Record. The Dukes are also coming off a 34-31 overtime loss at App State, while Troy is on a short week.

Why Troy? Because 21 points is a lot to ask of a home team missing its lead back. The Dukes beat Old Dominion 46-20 and Marshall 45-17, but they also won 20-13 over Liberty and 27-24 at Georgia Southern. Troy's defense allows 24.9 a game, and Smith can make Coleman uncomfortable. My final has the Dukes by 20, a point inside the number.

Title Game Rematch on a Thursday: Troy Visits James Madison in Harrisonburg

Troy (3-4, 1-2 Sun Belt) at James Madison (7-1, 4-1 Sun Belt). Thursday, Oct. 29, 7:30 p.m. ET, Bridgeforth Stadium, Harrisonburg, Va., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Marlo Pickens, a former Troy snapper from a Wiregrass peanut farm who never met a peanut pun he didn't like, and Lila Shenandoah, a former JMU cheer captain who turns every stat into a chant.

Marlo: Lila, I brought boiled peanuts for the whole Shenandoah Valley. Salted, Cajun or plain.

Lila: Purple reign, y'all! Give me a T, give me an R, give me a warm welcome for our guests!

Players to watch

James Madison quarterback Camden Coleman is 131 of 212 for 1,567 yards, 14 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Wide receiver Corey Scott leads the Dukes with 24 catches for 371 yards and four scores. On defense, linebacker Nakian Jackson has 59 tackles and linebacker JT Hooten has three sacks.

For Troy, quarterback Goose Crowder is 102 of 183 for 1,162 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. Running back Gavin Griffin has 398 rushing yards, and wide receiver TK Keyes has 13 catches for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Defensive back Donnie Smith has six sacks, and linebacker Keno Jones leads the team with 52 tackles.

Marlo: Six sacks from a defensive back. That boy gets to the quarterback like a squirrel gets to a peanut.

What happened last week

James Madison lost 34-31 in overtime at App State on Oct. 22, its first loss of the season. Coleman went 22 of 39 for 232 yards and a touchdown, and Braeden Wisloski caught two passes for 84 yards and a score.

Troy lost 21-14 to UL Monroe at home on Oct. 24. The Trojans led 14-3 with less than three minutes to play before the Warhawks rallied in the final minutes. Jordan Lovett ran 17 times for 70 yards.

Lila: Give me a deep breath! Both teams want to turn the page.

Injuries and availability

The Sun Belt has not posted an availability report for this game. James Madison running back George Pettaway, the team's leading rusher with 824 yards and eight touchdowns, is out with a lower-body injury, according to the Daily News-Record. Nick Herman and Seth Cromwell are the next backs up. Troy quarterback Goose Crowder has been dealing with a shoulder injury, and coach Gerad Parker had not settled on a quarterback plan early in the week, according to AL.com. Tucker Kilcrease played after Crowder came out against UL Monroe. Watch the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Billy Napier is in his first season at James Madison. He went 40-12 at Louisiana from 2018 to 2021 and then coached Florida from 2022 to 2025. His Dukes score 41.4 points a game and allow 18.2.

Gerad Parker is in his third season at Troy. He was hired on Dec. 18, 2023. His team has a short week and a long trip after a tough Saturday.

Marlo: Coach Parker will have those boys ready. A short week is like a short peanut row. You just hoe faster.

Player storylines

The Troy quarterback room is the big question. Whoever plays will face a James Madison defense that allows just 18.2 points a game. On the other side, the Dukes have to replace Pettaway's carries, and Smith will be hunting Coleman all night.

Coleman has been careful with the football. Two interceptions in 212 attempts is a fine way to keep a team in every game.

Lila: Give me a T, give me an O! Turnover margin, y'all!

What's happening on campus

Bridgeforth Stadium seats 24,877, and the Dukes have won 11 straight games there. It is a Thursday night in the Shenandoah Valley two days before Halloween, so the night already feels like a party.

Marlo: If anybody shows up dressed as a peanut, Lila, it's me. Nobody's surprised.

Lila: Give me a P, give me an E, give me a costume contest!

Anything else fun and true

This is the fifth all-time meeting, and James Madison leads 3-1, including 2-0 at home. The teams met twice in the FCS playoffs, in 1994 and 1999. James Madison won the 2025 Sun Belt Championship Game 31-14 over Troy and went on to the College Football Playoff. In 2023, the Dukes won 16-14.

Marlo: Sixteen to fourteen in 2023. We were right there, Lila. That's not peanuts.

Lila: Give me a handshake, Marlo. See you Thursday.

My call: James Madison Dukes 38, Troy Trojans 18.

Friday Night in the Queen City: Tulane Visits a Charlotte Team Fresh Off Its First Win

Tulane (3-4, 1-2 American) at Charlotte (1-6, 1-2 American). Friday, Oct. 30, 7 p.m. ET (6 p.m. Central), Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte, N.C., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Twan Ducros-Labat, an Uptown Tulane fan who believes every game is a brass-band parade, and Priya Halloran, an uptown Charlotte bank risk analyst who prices every drive like a loan.

Twan: Darlin', I brought beignets for the whole section. Roll Wave!

Priya: Price that drive, Twan. Today the beignets are on the house, and the interest rate is friendly.

Players to watch

Charlotte quarterback Conner Harrell went 23 of 31 for 281 yards and two touchdowns at Temple and ran for two more scores. Running back Henry Rutledge leads the team with 331 rushing yards, and wide receiver Jaden Barnes leads the receivers with 40 catches for 396 yards. On defense, linebacker Gavin Willis has 53 tackles and DJ Burgess has two sacks.

For Tulane, freshman quarterback Trace Johnson has thrown the most passes in each of the last two games. Running back Johnnie Daniels has 394 yards and four touchdowns on 66 carries, and wide receiver Destyn Hill has 26 catches for 339 yards. Linebacker Dickson Agu leads the team with 64 tackles, and defensive lineman Ed Smith IV has three sacks.

Twan: Sixty-four tackles from Agu. That man shows up to every parade.

What happened last week

Charlotte had the week off after beating Temple 38-31 on Oct. 17 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. It was the 49ers' first win of the season and the first American Conference win for coach Tim Albin. Rutledge ran for a career-high 123 yards, Derrick Eley caught six passes for 96 yards, and Aiden Bui, kicking for the first time in his career, hit a 47-yard field goal in the final two minutes.

Tulane lost 42-19 to UTSA at home on Oct. 24. Johnson went 24 of 44 for 265 yards, and Daniels ran eight times for 104 yards and a touchdown.

Priya: A stand at the two-yard mark, four stops in a row, before halftime at Temple. I'd frame that drive and hang it in the lobby.

Injuries and availability

The American has not posted an availability report for this game. Tulane tackle Ryan Mickow, who was hurt against UTSA, will be unavailable Friday, according to nola.com. Sophomore Reese Baker has moved between tackle and guard and has been the one constant among the big guys up front. No injury news has surfaced for either starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Will Hall is in his first season at Tulane. He was hired on Dec. 8, 2025. After the UTSA game he said, "I'm glad it's a short week. We know we've got to play better." He also called Charlotte "explosive on offense."

Tim Albin is in his second season at Charlotte. He went 30-12 in his last three years at Ohio before taking over the 49ers.

Twan: Coach Hall wants a clean game. No fumbles, no fuss, just a good parade.

Player storylines

Harrell made his second start of the season at Temple after dealing with injuries, and he looked sharp, with four different receivers going over 50 yards. Tulane's freshman quarterback, meanwhile, threw for nearly 200 yards in the first half against UTSA. "Trace was very poised," Hill said.

Tulane's Jah'rie Garner, who chases quarterbacks for a living, is staying humble. "I see them as a faceless opponent," he said. "In this league you can beat anybody."

Priya: Two quarterbacks, both trending up. That's a healthy portfolio.

What's happening on campus

Jerry Richardson Stadium opened in 2013 and has a listed capacity of 15,300. The Pride of Niner Nation Marching Band will be there, and if you visit, ask somebody about the 49ers name, which dates to the school's founding in 1946.

Twan: Fifteen thousand three hundred? That's a cozy block party. I love it.

Anything else fun and true

Tulane won the last two meetings, 34-3 in 2024 and 27-0 in 2025. The Temple win was the 49th in Charlotte program history, so the next one will be No. 50. Tulane's three wins this season came over South Alabama, Southern Miss and Memphis.

Priya: Win No. 50 would be a milestone worth framing, Twan.

Twan: Then we'll both bring the brass band, darlin'. Roll Wave!

My call: Tulane Green Wave 31, Charlotte 49ers 19.

Twan Ducros-Labat has the trombone back in its case after a rough Saturday Uptown, and he is ready to play it again in North Carolina. Priya Halloran is in the stands in Charlotte with a spreadsheet, and she has finally priced a drive that paid off.

Tulane (3-4) at Charlotte (1-6), Friday at 7:00 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at Jerry Richardson Stadium in Charlotte. It's an American game. DraftKings has Tulane Green Wave −10 with a total of 46.5. My card: Tulane Green Wave −10, Over 46.5, and a final of Tulane Green Wave 31, Charlotte 49ers 19.

Priya speaks for Charlotte. "Price that drive! Conner Harrell went 23 of 31 for 281 yards at Temple, threw two touchdowns and ran for two more. Henry Rutledge ran for 123. We won 38-31, and we've had two weeks to enjoy it."

Twan speaks for Tulane. "Darlin', six turnovers against UTSA. That's not us. Trace Johnson was sharp for most of that night before it got away, and we beat Charlotte 34-3 and 27-0 the last two years. Roll Wave!"

Here is the part that matters. Charlotte allows 40.6 points a game, last in the American. Before Temple, the 49ers gave up 41 to Ole Miss, 34 to Louisiana, 59 to Memphis and 50 to North Texas, and never scored more than 10 in those games.

Why Tulane? Because the 49ers have trouble running the ball, and that is where In The Trenches finds its read. Charlotte gains 3.9 yards a carry against a Tulane defense that allows 4.8, and that gap points to the Green Wave. Without a ground game, Harrell has to carry everything. My final has Tulane by 12, clear of the 10.

The worry is real. Tulane is on a short week, starting tackle Ryan Mickow is out per nola.com, and the line will be reshuffled again. All three Tulane wins were decided in the final minutes. Follow The Money likes Charlotte, because Action Network's opening number was Tulane −13.5 and it has fallen to 10.

Why the Over/Under? Charlotte games have finished 43-41, 41-9, 26-21, 34-7, 59-8, 50-10 and 38-31. This defense gives up points to everyone, and Tulane scored 31 on Memphis. Action Network opened the total at 45.5 and it has ticked up to 46.5. My 31-19 adds up to 50, three and a half over the over/under 46.5.

Now the room. The Formula has Tulane 33-20 and likes the Green Wave and the Over. Next Man Up has Tulane 28-17, on our side but under the total. Follow The Money likes Charlotte and the Over. In The Trenches likes Tulane and reads the side only. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up: "Forty-five points. A freshman quarterback on a short week does not light up a scoreboard."

The Formula: "He does against a defense allowing forty."

Follow The Money: "Three and a half points of movement toward Charlotte. Somebody saw Temple."

Bottom of the card: Tulane is the better team on both sides of the ball, and Charlotte has not shown it can stop anybody for four quarters. Priya prices one more good drive. Twan gets the parade.

Tulane Green Wave 31, Charlotte 49ers 19. Tulane Green Wave cover the 10. Over 46.5.

Baylor fired Dave Aranda after a 25-24 loss at Kansas, and now interim coach Joe Klanderman takes the Bears to Orlando on a Friday night. Maggie Whitlock packed her toolbox for a full remodel. Knox Brevard-Stiles is still riding the high from a double-overtime win over No. 2 BYU.

Baylor (4-3) at UCF (4-3), Friday at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN at the Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando. It's a Big 12 game. DraftKings has UCF Knights −1.5 with a total of 47.5. My card: UCF Knights −1.5, Over 47.5, and a final of UCF Knights 27, Baylor Bears 25.

Knox speaks for UCF. "Ride check: Keyone Jenkins went 25 of 41 for 293 yards and three touchdowns in the overtime win over BYU, and Coach Frost says he's the hot hand. Duke Watson has 577 rushing yards. Keep your arms inside the car, Maggie."

Maggie speaks for Baylor. "Sugar, we're under new management, but the foundation is still good. Coach Klanderman built this defense, and we allow 16.1 points a game. Gavin Freeman has 58 catches for 678 yards. And we beat you 30-3 last year."

Here is the part that matters. Baylor has lost two straight, 17-6 to TCU and 25-24 at Kansas, where three of its field-goal tries were blocked. A midseason coaching change can light a team up or knock it flat, and this is a second straight road trip.

Why UCF? Because the Knights have found a quarterback. Jenkins has 11 touchdown passes and only three interceptions, and he threw four touchdown passes at Oklahoma State before beating BYU. Baylor's run game gets 3.8 yards a carry against a UCF defense that allows 3.2, and DJ Lagway has to carry the offense. My final has UCF by two, just enough.

The worry is that Baylor defense. Klanderman knows it best, and the Bears held six straight opponents to 19 or fewer before Kansas. If Lagway plays like he did at Arizona State, 306 yards and four touchdowns, Baylor wins this outright. The Formula has Baylor by one.

Why the Over/Under? UCF lost 42-28 at Oklahoma State and beat BYU 39-31. Baylor scored 55 at Arizona State. DraftKings had this total at 48.5 on Monday and it has dipped to 47.5, the wrong direction with a hot home quarterback. My 27-25 adds up to 52, four and a half over the over/under 47.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up has UCF 29-23 and likes the Knights and the Over. The Formula has Baylor 26-25, takes Baylor and likes the Over. Follow The Money stays off the side and likes the Under after the total fell. In The Trenches sees the run gaps cancel and has no pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

The Formula: "Twenty-six to twenty-five. A coin flip with a Baylor sticker on it."

Next Man Up: "Coin flip in Orlando lands on the Knights."

Follow The Money: "The total slipped two points. Somebody respects the defenses."

Bottom of the card: a home team that just found its quarterback against a road team that just lost its coach. Knox says the ride is open. Maggie says her renovation is still in progress.

UCF Knights 27, Baylor Bears 25. UCF Knights cover the 1.5. Over 47.5.

Space Game Friday at the Bounce House: Baylor Brings an Interim Coach to Orlando

Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) at UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12). Friday, Oct. 30, 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 p.m. Central), Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, ESPN.

Your hosts are Maggie Whitlock, a Waco interior designer who renovates roster weaknesses live on air, and Knox Brevard-Stiles, a UCF roller-coaster devotee who runs a Ride Check before every big game.

Knox: Ride check, Maggie! Lap bar down, arms inside, and welcome to the annual Space Game.

Maggie: Sugar, I brought my tape measure and a hard hat. It's been a big week of remodeling in Waco.

Players to watch

UCF quarterback Keyone Jenkins is 108 of 159 for 1,099 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions, and he has run for four more scores. Running back Duke Watson has 577 yards on 85 carries, and wide receiver Josh Derry leads the team with 34 catches for 358 yards. Linebacker Tackett Curtis has 42 tackles, and Isaiah Nixon has 2.5 sacks.

Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway is 113 of 217 for 1,352 yards, nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has 58 catches for 678 yards and ranks third in the nation in receptions per game. Linebacker Travion Barnes has 51 tackles, and defensive end Garrick Ponder has four sacks.

Maggie: Freeman is the load-bearing wall in this house. Don't touch him.

What happened last week

UCF beat No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime at home. Jenkins went 25 of 41 for 293 yards and three touchdowns, ran for another score, and found Derry on the first play of overtime. Tyren Hornes caught six passes for 137 yards.

Baylor lost 25-24 at Kansas. A 45-yard field goal try with 22 seconds left was blocked, the third Baylor field goal try the Jayhawks blocked that day. Freeman caught nine passes for 123 yards.

Knox: Thirty-nine to thirty-one over the No. 2 team in the country. My hands are still up in the air.

Injuries and availability

The Big 12 has not posted an availability report for this game. UCF coach Scott Frost said Jenkins will start again. Alonza Barnett III, who hurt his hamstring in Week 2, is making progress, and Frost said, "I think he probably could play," though he was not sure Barnett was fully healthy yet. No injury news has surfaced for Baylor's starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Baylor parted ways with seventh-year coach Dave Aranda after the Kansas game. Athletic director Doug McNamee called Aranda "a genuine and honorable person" who "deeply cares for his players." Joe Klanderman, the first-year defensive coordinator, is the interim head coach for the rest of the season. He won four national titles at North Dakota State and led the defense at Kansas State before coming to Waco.

Scott Frost is in his second year of his second stint at UCF. He led the Knights in 2016 and 2017, and his 2017 team went 13-0.

Maggie: New management, same foundation. Coach Klanderman built this defense.

Player storylines

Jenkins has been the steady hand while Barnett heals. After the BYU win, Jenkins said, "It's still his team. Still his starting job." That is a great teammate talking.

Baylor's defense ranks third in the nation in sacks and fifth in tackles for loss per game. Watson and the big guys up front for UCF will need a strong night.

Knox: Jenkins giving his teammate the credit? That's a first-class ride, Maggie. Pure class.

What's happening on campus

Friday is UCF's annual Space Game, one of the fun themed nights on the schedule. Mike Monaco, Jordan Rodgers and Dana Boyle have the call on ESPN.

Maggie: A space theme? I'm repainting the den in galaxy blue the minute I get home.

Anything else fun and true

Baylor leads the series 2-1. UCF won the first meeting, 52-42 in the 2013 Fiesta Bowl. In 2023 in Orlando, Baylor came back from 35-7 down in the third quarter to win 36-35, the biggest comeback in Bears history, and in 2025 Baylor won 30-3 in Waco. After this one, Baylor goes home for Homecoming against Iowa State on Nov. 7.

Knox: A 28-point comeback in our house? That one still makes my stomach drop like the big hill.

Maggie: Then buckle up, Knox. We like a late build.

My call: UCF Knights 27, Baylor Bears 25.

Kent State flies across the country for a 7:30 p.m. Pacific kickoff, and Ozzie Brannigan has already decided the jet lag will be a problem. Mateo Villaseñor is in Sacramento with a fresh recipe and a defense that finally showed some flavor at Ball State.

Kent State (3-5) at Sacramento State (1-7), Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at Hornet Stadium in Sacramento. It's a MAC game and the first meeting between these schools. DraftKings has Kent State Golden Flashes −10 with a total of 46.5. My card: Sacramento State Hornets +10, Over 46.5, and a final of Kent State Golden Flashes 27, Sacramento State Hornets 22.

Ozzie speaks for Kent State. "Dru DeShields threw four touchdown passes and ran for another against Akron. We won 35-20. I expected to lose. Now I expect the plane to be late. Wayne Harris caught nine balls for 156 yards and three scores, and I'm suspicious of that too."

Mateo speaks for Sacramento State. "Plate it up, Ozzie. We led Ball State twice in the first half. Boogsie Silvera picked off two passes, and our special teams are a five-course meal. Matt Coleman has 39 catches for 492 yards."

Here is the part that matters. Before Akron, Kent State scored 0, 3, 10, 7 and 2 points in its five losses. The Flashes run for 3.0 yards a carry. A team that scores 14.9 points a game has no business laying 10 on the road.

Why Sacramento State? Because 10 points is a lot of cushion for a home team with a punter who flips the field and a kicker who just hit from 47. Kent State's defensive coordinator, Cherokee Valeria, coached Sacramento State's defensive backs for six seasons, so this is no mystery to either side. My final has Kent State by five, well inside the 10.

The worry is the Hornets' offense. Sacramento State has not run for a touchdown in six games and is minus-9 in turnover margin. It lost 48-7 to Ohio and 49-3 at Fresno State. If DeShields carries the Akron game into this one, the Flashes pull away.

Why the Over/Under? These offenses are poor, but these defenses are worse. Kent State allows 30.5 points a game and Sacramento State allows 32.9. Kent State's last game finished 35-20 and Sacramento State's finished 34-17. The total has ticked up a point, and Follow The Money likes that move. My 27-22 adds up to 49, two and a half over the over/under 46.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up has Kent State 25-24, takes Sacramento State and likes it, and goes Over. The Formula has Kent State 28-19, also on the Hornets, and the Over. Follow The Money stays off the side and likes the Over. In The Trenches sees the run gaps cancel and has no pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up: "Twenty-five to twenty-four. One point. Bring the fireworks."

The Formula: "Nine points. Still inside the 10."

Follow The Money: "The total moved up. Somebody stayed up late for this one."

Bottom of the card: two struggling teams on a Friday night, and the home team gets 10 points. Ozzie expects the worst. Mateo just wants the plate to look good.

Kent State Golden Flashes 27, Sacramento State Hornets 22. Sacramento State Hornets cover the 10. Over 46.5.

Fireworks Friday in Sacramento: Kent State Makes Its First Trip to Hornet Stadium

Kent State (3-5, 2-2 MAC) at Sacramento State (1-7, 0-5 MAC). Friday, Oct. 30, 10:30 p.m. ET (7:30 p.m. Pacific), Hornet Stadium, Sacramento, Calif., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Ozzie Brannigan, a Kent State pessimist who grades uniforms and fourth-down decisions, and Mateo Villaseñor, a Sacramento State fan and farm-to-fork chef who explains defense like a recipe.

Mateo: Welcome to Sacramento, Ozzie! Farm-to-fork capital, Friday night lights and postgame fireworks.

Ozzie: I expected fireworks. I always expect fireworks. I just don't expect them to be for us.

Players to watch

Kent State quarterback Dru DeShields is 124 of 218 for 1,439 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions, and he has run for a team-high four scores. Wide receiver Wayne Harris has 40 catches for 552 yards and four touchdowns, and running back Brandon White leads the rushers with 235 yards. Linebacker Hayden Dawahare leads the defense with 43 tackles and four sacks.

Sacramento State quarterback Jackson Sharman is 123 of 218 for 1,257 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions. Wide receiver Matt Coleman has 39 catches for 492 yards and five scores, fourth in the MAC in receiving yards. Running back Isaiah Ene has 303 yards. Safety Boogsie Silvera leads the team with 61 tackles.

Mateo: Look at that, Ozzie. Our quarterbacks have the same attempts, the same touchdowns and the same interceptions. That's a matched pair of plates.

What happened last week

Kent State beat Akron 35-20 at home to keep the Wagon Wheel. After a 7-7 halftime tie, DeShields threw four touchdown passes and ran for another, and Harris caught nine passes for 156 yards and three scores.

Sacramento State lost 34-17 at Ball State, but the Hornets led twice in the first half. Sharman threw two touchdown passes, Jace Wilson caught a 55-yard score, and Silvera picked off two passes and made 11 tackles.

Ozzie: Four touchdown passes. I'm happy. I'm also nervous that I'm happy.

Injuries and availability

The MAC has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Sacramento State has used seven different starting groups on offense this year, and Silvera is the only Hornets defender to start all eight games.

What the coaches are up to

Mark Carney is in his second season as Kent State's head coach and is 8-12. Kent State removed his interim tag on Oct. 30, 2025, so Friday is one year to the day. His assistant head coach and defensive coordinator, Cherokee Valeria, coached Sacramento State's defensive backs from 2019 to 2024 and was part of three Big Sky championships.

Alonzo Carter is a first-time head coach. Sacramento State hired him on Dec. 15, 2025, and he's leading the Hornets through their first FBS season.

Bodie speaks for Texas Tech. He tips his hat, studies the sky and says, "Wind." Inez keeps staring, so he adds a little more. "J'Koby Williams. 619 yards. A.J. Holmes Jr. 6.5 sacks. Austin Romaine. 53 tackles. Cincinnati was one bad night."

Why Texas Tech? Home field and a run game. Tech gains 5.0 yards a carry and gives up just 3.5. Arizona's offense is Fifita's arm, and that arm now has to work in front of a Lubbock crowd that watched its team lose 37-24 last week. The market has drifted toward Arizona: DraftKings had Tech −4.5 on Monday, and now it's 3.5. My final has Tech by four, so I'll take the cheaper price.

Saturday Noon in Lubbock: Fifita's Wildcats Bring the Desert to a Red Raider Team Looking to Bounce Back

No. 22 Arizona (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) at No. 13 Texas Tech (6-1, 3-1 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, Texas, ESPN.

Your hosts are Inez Paloverde, an Arizona fan and desert-sunrise optimist who will defend this team to the last saguaro, and Bodie Ratliff, a Texas Tech bareback rider who answers most questions in one word.

Inez: Hi, hi, hi, Bodie! Happy Halloween! I brought you a cactus. It's a dry hype, get it?

Bodie: Thanks.

Inez: That's it? I fly all the way to Lubbock and I get one word?

Bodie: Windy.

Players to watch

Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita is 167 of 225 for 2,064 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. Wide receiver Isaiah Mizell leads the Wildcats with 27 catches for 493 yards and five touchdowns. Kedrick Reescano leads the rushers with 303 yards and five scores. On defense, linebacker Chase Kennedy has four sacks and linebacker Taye Brown leads the team with 42 tackles.

Texas Tech quarterback Will Hammond is 139 of 205 for 1,561 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions. Running back J'Koby Williams is the workhorse, with 619 yards and five touchdowns on 86 carries. Wide receiver Kenny Johnson has 31 catches for 499 yards. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. leads the team with 6.5 sacks, and linebacker Austin Romaine leads with 53 tackles.

Inez: Eighteen touchdown passes! Noah throws the ball the way the sun comes up over the Catalinas. Every single day, and beautifully.

Bodie: Sunburn.

What happened last week

Arizona rolled past Iowa State 39-3 at home on Oct. 24. Fifita went 27 of 34 for 308 yards and two touchdowns, Mizell caught eight passes for 134 yards and a score, and Quincy Craig ran nine times for 51 yards and a touchdown. The Wildcat defense allowed just one field goal.

Texas Tech had its first loss of the season, 37-24 at Cincinnati on Oct. 24. Hammond went 24 of 37 for 227 yards, Williams ran 12 times for 81 yards, and Johnson caught seven passes for 81 yards.

Bodie: Lesson.

Inez: That was almost a sentence, Bodie. I'm so proud of you.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and the teams' box scores don't mark starters. Fifita has thrown the most passes for Arizona in all seven games, and Hammond has done the same for Texas Tech, so check the teams' pregame notes on Saturday morning.

What the coaches are up to

Joey McGuire was hired at Texas Tech on Nov. 8, 2021. Last season was the best in school history: the Red Raiders went 12-2, beat BYU 34-7 to win the Big 12 championship and made their first College Football Playoff. It was the program's first outright conference title since 1955. This year's team is built on the ground and on defense, and it allows 20.4 points a game.

Brent Brennan was hired at Arizona on Jan. 16, 2024. He went 4-8 in his first season, then turned it around with a 9-4 year in 2025 that ended in the Holiday Bowl. His 2026 Wildcats score 36.1 points a game and allow just 16.7.

Inez: Coach Brennan took a seedling and grew a whole desert garden. Bear Down!

Bodie: Respect.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is Fifita against a Texas Tech defense that has 6.5 sacks from Holmes alone. If the Red Raider big guys up front can get to Fifita, they can slow the Arizona passing game. On the other side, Williams and the Tech ground game face an Arizona defense that held Cincinnati to 7 points and Iowa State to 3. Whichever running game finds room first could decide the afternoon.

Bodie: Trenches.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Lubbock, and the noon kickoff means plenty of time for costumes after the final whistle. Expect plenty of "Guns Up" signs from the Red Raider faithful.

Anything else fun and true

Arizona's rallying cry, "Bear Down," goes back to October 1926 and John "Button" Salmon, the student-body president and the Wildcats' quarterback. Before he died after a car accident, he asked coach J.F. "Pop" McKale to tell the team to "bear down," and it has been the school's motto ever since. These two have split their last two meetings: Arizona won 28-14 in 2019, and Texas Tech won 28-22 in 2024.

Inez: Bear Down, friends! And Happy Halloween to everybody in Lubbock.

Bodie: Guns up.

Inez: Two words! It's a Halloween miracle.

My call: Texas Tech Red Raiders 29, Arizona Wildcats 25.

Ruff Pegram has his grill lit in the same Carter-Finley lot, and he's reading the thermometer like a scouting report. Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch arrives from Berkeley with a picket sign that says "RUN IT ON SECOND DOWN, PLEASE (RESPECTFULLY)."

California (3-5) at NC State (3-4), Saturday at 12:00 p.m. ET on ACC Network at Carter-Finley Stadium in Raleigh. It's an ACC game, and the Wolfpack has lost two straight. DraftKings has NC State Wolfpack −7 with a total of 56.5. My card: NC State Wolfpack −7, Over 56.5, and a final of NC State Wolfpack 36, California Golden Bears 24.

Quentin speaks for Cal, and he's already organizing. "Comrades, Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele went 27 of 37 for 265 yards at SMU. Chase Hendricks has 54 catches. The revolution will be thrown, not run."

Ruff speaks for NC State, and he points a spatula at the sign. "Quentin, buddy, the revolution gave up 59 points last week. CJ Bailey has 1,763 passing yards and 11 touchdowns, and Keenan Jackson has six touchdown catches. We lost 31-28 at Stanford by a field goal. Saturday's a sear."

Why NC State? Because Cal can't stop anybody right now. The Bears allow 31.6 points a game, and they gave up 41 to Wake Forest and 59 at SMU in the last two weeks. Their run defense gives up 5.2 yards a carry, and NC State gains 4.4. On the other side, Cal runs for 3.1 yards a carry, so the Bears have to throw into a home crowd that's hungry after two losses. My final has NC State by a dozen, well clear of the 7.

The worry is the NC State defense. It allows 28.1 points a game, and Wake Forest put 38 on it in Raleigh. Last time these two met, in 2024, NC State won 24-23. If Sagapolutele gets hot the way he did against Wagner, this turns into a one-score game late.

Why the Over? NC State scores 32.3 points a game, and Cal's defense has been giving up more than that. The Wolfpack offense scored 31 against Louisville and 28 at Stanford, and Cal has scored 20 or more in six of its eight games. My 36-24 adds up to 60, three and a half points over 56.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up is the loudest howl in the parking lot, NC State 38-23 and the Over. The Formula agrees on both, NC State 33-25. Follow The Money saw the market come down toward Cal, so it takes California +7 and skips the total. In The Trenches sits this one out, and Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up started it: "Two of us have the Wolfpack by more than a touchdown, Follow The Money. You're picketing with Quentin?"

Follow The Money held its sign high: "A move is a move. I follow it."

The Formula had the last word: "Then follow it to the scoreboard. Cal gave up 59 last week."

Bottom of the card: a home team that wants a sear after two losses, a Cal defense that has bled points for two weeks, and a total two scores in the room clear. Ruff gets his howl. Give me the Wolfpack and the Over.

Halloween Noon in Raleigh: The Wolfpack Fires Up the Grill as Cal Comes East With a Sign for Every Occasion

California (3-5, 2-3 ACC) at NC State (3-4, 1-3 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh, N.C., ACC Network.

Your hosts are Rutherford "Ruff" Pegram, a Wake County engineer who grills in the same Carter-Finley lot every home game, and Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch, a Berkeley philosophy Ph.D. student with a picket sign for every bad play call.

Ruff: Welcome to Raleigh, Quentin! Grill's at 450. That's a sear. Wolfpack, howl!

Quentin: Greetings, comrade. I brought a new sign for the occasion. It says "TRICK PLAYS ARE A HUMAN RIGHT."

Players to watch

Cal quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is 149 of 219 for 1,555 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. Jackson Brousseau threw the most passes in three straight games in October, and Sagapolutele was back on top at SMU. Wide receiver Chase Hendricks leads the Bears with 54 catches for 498 yards and three scores. Adam Mohammed leads the rushers with 336 yards. On defense, defensive back Isaiah Crosby has 46 tackles and linebacker JD McKinley has three sacks.

NC State quarterback CJ Bailey is 143 of 219 for 1,763 yards, 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, and he has thrown the most passes in every Wolfpack game this season. Wide receiver Keenan Jackson has 30 catches for 456 yards and six touchdowns. Jayden Scott leads the rushers with 358 yards and four scores. Linebacker Popo Aguirre leads the team with 60 tackles, and linebacker Elijah Satchell has four sacks.

Ruff: Sixty tackles. Popo Aguirre is the kind of linebacker who flips burgers, cleans the grill and still helps you pack the cooler.

What happened last week

Cal lost 59-20 at SMU on Oct. 24. Sagapolutele went 27 of 37 for 265 yards and a touchdown, and Hendricks caught seven passes for 83 yards and a score.

Quentin: I have filed a formal grievance with the scoreboard.

NC State lost 31-28 at Stanford on Oct. 23. Bailey went 17 of 30 for 256 yards and two touchdowns and was also the team's leading rusher, with 59 yards on nine carries. Deandre Desinor caught three passes for 79 yards and a touchdown.

Ruff: Three points. That one stayed on the grill a little too long.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and neither school's box scores mark starters. Bailey has thrown the most passes for NC State in all seven games, and Sagapolutele did for Cal last week, so watch the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

NC State has new leadership this week. The school relieved Dave Doeren of his duties after the loss at Stanford, ending a run that began in 2013, and running backs coach and special teams coordinator Todd Goebbel will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the season. Saturday is his first game in charge, and he has promised a team that will be "hard, tough and together." This year's offense scores 32.3 points a game, including a 73-0 win over Richmond and a 31-28 win over Louisville.

Tosh Lupoi was named the 35th head coach in Cal history on Dec. 4, 2025, replacing Justin Wilcox. His first Cal team picked up ACC wins over Syracuse and Virginia Tech, both by one score.

Quentin: Coach Lupoi is building something, comrade. Respectfully, but firmly.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is Bailey and Jackson against a Cal defense that allows 31.6 points a game. Jackson has six touchdown catches, the most of anyone on either roster. On the other side, Hendricks has caught 54 passes, and the Bears like to throw it to him early and often. Cal gains 3.1 yards a carry, so the Wolfpack big guys up front will try to make the Bears one-dimensional.

What's happening on campus

Carter-Finley Stadium has been NC State's home since 1966, and it's the largest college football stadium in North Carolina. In 2010 the school brought back a live mascot, a Tamaskan dog named Tuffy, and a Halloween noon kickoff means Tuffy may see a few costumes in the stands.

Anything else fun and true

NC State was a founding member of the ACC in 1953 and has won seven conference championships. Cal fans have their own claim to fame: The Play, from the 1982 Big Game against Stanford, when the Bears returned the final kickoff through five laterals and Kevin Moen scored as the Stanford band wandered onto the field. Cal won 25-20. These two met in 2024, and NC State won 24-23, so there's some history here, too.

Quentin: Five laterals, Ruff. That's democracy in action.

Ruff: Then let's have a fair election. Grab a plate, Quentin. The game's about to start, and grace comes before brisket.

My call: NC State Wolfpack 36, California Golden Bears 24.

Halloween Noon in the Loud House: No. 19 SMU Heads North to Meet a Syracuse Team That Loves Overtime

No. 19 SMU (6-1, 4-1 ACC) at Syracuse (3-4, 1-4 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse, N.Y., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Tatum Delacroix-Price, a Highland Park boutique owner who grades opponents' sideline outfits, and Nico Calabrese, a Syracuse fan from the Salt City who has survived more lake-effect winters than he can count.

Nico: Tatum! Welcome to the Salt City. Grab a salt potato. You're gonna need the energy.

Tatum: Nico, darling, I packed three coats and my biggest sunglasses. Indoors. It's a whole look.

Players to watch

SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings has thrown the most passes in all seven Mustang games. He's 156 of 215 for 2,062 yards, 19 touchdowns and five interceptions, and he threw for 430 yards in the opener at Florida State. Running back Kendrick Raphael has 641 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. Yamir Knight leads the receivers with 38 catches for 443 yards. On defense, end Marques White has 5.5 sacks, and linebacker Alexander Kilgore leads the team with 39 tackles.

Syracuse wide receiver Umari Hatcher is the name to know. He has 54 catches for 887 yards and eight touchdowns. Steve Angeli leads the Orange with 987 passing yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions. Tylik Hill has 461 rushing yards. Linebacker Chris D'Appolonia leads the team with 51 tackles, and defensive lineman Tunmise Adeleye has four sacks.

Nico: Eight hundred eighty-seven yards. Hatcher is a lake-effect storm. You see him coming, and you still can't get out of the way.

What happened last week

SMU beat California 59-20 on Oct. 24. Jennings went 16 of 23 for 223 yards and three touchdowns, and Raphael ran 22 times for 104 yards and two scores.

Tatum: Fifty-nine points. I popped so much imaginary confetti I'm still sweeping.

Syracuse won 31-30 in overtime at North Carolina on Oct. 24. Angeli went 20 of 34 for 256 yards and two touchdowns. Ahmad Miller carried 30 times for 125 yards and a score, and Hatcher caught four passes for 103 yards and a touchdown.

Nico: That's a foot of snow of a WIN! They heard me in Utica.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Syracuse has had three different quarterbacks throw the most passes in a game this season: Angeli, Amari Odom and Malachi Nelson. Angeli did it last week, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Rhett Lashlee was hired at SMU on Nov. 30, 2021. His Mustangs played in the 2024 ACC championship game and lost 34-31 to Clemson on a field goal at the end. This year they're second in the ACC, and they've won all five games at home in University Park.

Fran Brown was hired at Syracuse on Nov. 28, 2023, and his first team went 10-3 in 2024. This year's Orange score 31.6 points a game, and they've already won two overtime thrillers, 42-41 at UConn and 31-30 at North Carolina.

Tatum: Coach Brown's sideline outfit is a very confident orange. I give it an A-minus.

Nico: An A-minus? Tatum, that's the nicest thing a Dallas person has ever said to me.

Player storylines

The big matchup is Hatcher against an SMU defense that held Boston College to 16 points and Virginia to 13. On the other side, the Syracuse big guys up front will try to slow Raphael. SMU gains 4.4 yards a carry and Syracuse allows 4.2, while the Orange gain 3.8 and SMU allows 3.8, so the ground game could be a grind. And watch Jennings early. He threw 33 of 39 for 439 yards against Missouri State.

What's happening on campus

The JMA Wireless Dome opened in 1980 and seats 49,057. Folks call it "The Loud House," and a Halloween noon kickoff indoors means nobody has to worry about lake-effect snow on the costumes. Syracuse is the only FBS school in New York in a Power Four conference.

Tatum: A dome! Nico, my hair thanks you.

Anything else fun and true

SMU has a Heisman Trophy winner, Doak Walker in 1948, and the Pony Express backfield of Eric Dickerson and Craig James is still legendary in Dallas. Syracuse has had its ups and downs, from 10-3 in 2024 to 3-9 last season. These two met last season, and SMU won 31-18.

Nico: Tatum, whatever happens, you're welcome at my mom's table for Sunday dinner. We say grace, then we share the salt potatoes.

Tatum: Sugar, I'll bring the sweet tea. Pony up or sit down.

My call: SMU Mustangs 32, Syracuse Orange 26.

Boston College (4-3, 2-2 ACC) at Duke (5-2, 2-2 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Wallace Wade Stadium, Durham, N.C., CW.

Your hosts are Siobhan Dunleavy, a Boston College grad student and former debate champion who argues every play like a moot-court case, and Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, a Duke pre-everything overachiever with a degree for every occasion.

Siobhan: All rise! The Honorable Siobhan Dunleavy presiding. Also prosecuting. Also on the jury.

Harrison: Objection, your honor. That's a conflict of interest. I wrote a paper on it. Footnotes available upon request.

Players to watch

Boston College quarterback Mason McKenzie has thrown the most passes in all seven Eagle games, and he's also the team's leading rusher. He's 107 of 185 for 1,363 yards, eight touchdowns and seven interceptions, and he has 614 rushing yards and five rushing scores. Javarius Green leads the receivers with 26 catches for 286 yards. On defense, linebacker Anthony Palano has 61 tackles and end Demetrius Ballard has 4.5 sacks.

Duke quarterback Walker Eget has thrown the most passes in all seven Blue Devil games. He's 122 of 197 for 1,440 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. Running back Nate Sheppard is the workhorse, with 875 yards and nine touchdowns on 153 carries. Jonah Burton leads the receivers with 21 catches for 298 yards. Linebacker Nick Morris Jr. has 44 tackles, and end Kevin O'Connor has four sacks.

Harrison: Eight hundred seventy-five yards. Sheppard's carries deserve their own peer-reviewed journal.

What happened last week

Boston College won 49-27 at Georgia Tech on Oct. 24. McKenzie ran 16 times for 170 yards and two touchdowns and threw for 101 yards and another score.

Siobhan: Objection overruled, we WON! I banged the gavel so hard it needs a cast.

Duke won 19-16 at Virginia on Oct. 23. Eget went 14 of 25 for 211 yards, Sheppard ran for a touchdown, and Burton caught four passes for 59 yards.

Harrison: A three-point win on the road. I'll accept that grade with gratitude.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. McKenzie and Eget have each thrown the most passes in every game for their teams this season, so check the teams' pregame notes before kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Bill O'Brien was named Boston College's 37th head coach on Feb. 9, 2024. He went 15-9 at Penn State in 2012 and 2013, won four AFC South titles with the Houston Texans, and coached Heisman winner Bryce Young as Alabama's offensive coordinator.

Manny Diaz was hired at Duke on Dec. 7, 2023. He was head coach at Miami from 2019 to 2021 and defensive coordinator at Penn State in 2022 and 2023. His Duke defense allows 16 points a game this season, and it held Tulane to three points and Stanford to seven.

Siobhan: Two coaches with Penn State on the résumé. I move that they share a pregame handshake.

Harrison: Seconded. Motion carries.

Player storylines

The case to watch is McKenzie against a Duke defense that allows 3.3 yards a carry. If the Duke big guys up front keep him from breaking loose the way he did in Atlanta, the Eagles will have to throw. On the other side, Sheppard gains plenty of yards behind a Duke run game that averages 5.3 yards a carry, and BC allows 4.0. Whoever controls the ground game probably controls the afternoon.

What's happening on campus

Wallace Wade Stadium opened in 1929 and seats 40,004. Duke has won 18 conference championships, eight in the ACC and ten in the Southern Conference, and the program counts 53 All-Americans. A Halloween noon kickoff means expect a few Blue Devil costumes in the stands, which is the easiest costume in Durham.

Siobhan: I'm coming as a Supreme Court justice. Again.

Anything else fun and true

Duke's football rebirth under David Cutcliffe from 2008 to 2021 included the school's first Coastal Division title in 2013. Since then, the Blue Devils have stacked four straight winning seasons: 9-4, 8-5, 9-4 and 9-5. Boston College plays its home games at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill. These two have split their last two meetings: BC won 26-6 in 2020, and Duke won 38-31 in 2022.

Harrison: Siobhan, whatever the verdict, lunch is on me after the game. Grace first, then barbecue.

Siobhan: The court accepts. Objection: sustained.

My call: Duke Blue Devils 29, Boston College Eagles 18.

Halloween Noon at Kinnick: The Polka Comes to Iowa City as No. 25 Wisconsin Meets the Hawkeyes

No. 25 Wisconsin (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) at Iowa (5-2, 2-2 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City, Iowa, Fox.

Your hosts are Lars "Brat" Ellefson, a former Badgers fullback who carries a cheese wedge to every game and talks to a polka beat, and Orrin Kalvelage, an Iowa farm-country Hawkeye who wears the same sweater every week.

Brat: (Oom-pah, oom-pah.) Hiya, Orrin! I brought curds for the whole tailgate. Squeaky fresh.

Orrin: Thank you kindly, Lars. I brought my sweater. It's the same one. It's always the same one.

Players to watch

Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph has thrown the most passes in all seven Badger games, and he's also the team's leading rusher. He's 99 of 173 for 1,256 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions, with 365 rushing yards and four rushing scores. Tyrell Henry leads the receivers with 28 catches for 343 yards. On defense, linebacker Cooper Catalano has 60 tackles and linebacker Sebastian Cheeks has five sacks.

Iowa quarterback Hank Brown has 968 passing yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions, and he has thrown the most passes in six of Iowa's seven games. Jeremy Hecklinski did it in the 41-24 win at Washington. Running back Kamari Moulton leads the team with 541 rushing yards and four scores. Tony Diaz leads the receivers with 29 catches for 386 yards. Linebacker Cam Buffington has 62 tackles, and end Joseph Anderson has four sacks.

Orrin: Sixty-two tackles. Cam Buffington is the kind of linebacker who'd help you fix a fence and then stay for supper.

What happened last week

Wisconsin beat USC 24-7 at Camp Randall on Oct. 24. Joseph went 12 of 14 with a touchdown throw, and Abu Sama III ran 17 times for 71 yards.

Brat: (Oom-pah!) I jumped around so hard my cheese wedge fell off. Twice.

Iowa lost 13-10 at Minnesota on Oct. 24. Brown threw a touchdown throw to Reece Vander Zee, who caught four passes for 69 yards.

Orrin: A three-point loss on the road. We'll be fine. The sweater has been through worse.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Joseph has thrown the most passes in every Wisconsin game, and Brown did for Iowa last week, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Kirk Ferentz is in his 28th season at Iowa, the longest current tenure in FBS, and he's the Big Ten's all-time leader in wins. He's led the Hawkeyes since 1999, and before that he was head coach at Maine from 1990 to 1992. His defense allows 14.3 points a game this season.

Luke Fickell was hired at Wisconsin on Nov. 27, 2022. His Badgers allow 15.3 points a game, and they've already won 24-20 at Penn State and beaten Michigan State 31-3.

Brat: Two coaches who love defense. This game might be decided by a punt. (Oom-pah.)

Orrin: Lars, a good punt is a love letter to your defense.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is the Iowa run game against the Wisconsin defense. The Hawkeyes gain 5.7 yards a carry, and the Badgers allow just 2.8. On the other side, Joseph and the Wisconsin big guys up front face an Iowa defense that allows only 2.4 yards a carry. Somebody's ground game is going to have a long afternoon.

What's happening on campus

Kinnick Stadium seats 69,250, and a Halloween noon kickoff in Iowa City should bring out plenty of black-and-gold costumes. Iowa has won 13 conference championships, 11 in the Big Ten, and has been ranked No. 1 in the AP and Coaches polls 15 times. Wisconsin's home, Camp Randall Stadium, opened in 1917 and is the fourth-oldest stadium in college football.

Orrin: I'm dressing up as myself. In the sweater.

Anything else fun and true

Wisconsin has played in the Big Ten since the conference formed in 1896, and it's one of 26 programs with 700 or more wins. Iowa has been steady as a fence post, with records of 10-4, 8-5, 10-4, 8-5 and 9-4 over the last five seasons. This rivalry is as even as it gets lately. In the last ten regular-season meetings, each team has won five, and Iowa won 37-0 last season.

Brat: Orrin, whatever happens, come by the tailgate after. We'll say grace and have a brat.

Orrin: I'll be there, Lars. Go Hawks.

My call: Iowa Hawkeyes 22, Wisconsin Badgers 17.
