Charts Meet Crabs in College Park: Illinois Brings a Big Win Over Oregon to Maryland on Halloween

Illinois (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) at Maryland (2-5, 0-4 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, SECU Stadium, College Park, Md., FS1.

Your hosts are Margery Vandermolen, a prairie-state numbers whiz who explains football like a beloved teacher, with charts, and Abigail "Abby" Chesapeake, a D.C.-suburb networker who cracks crabs on air and puts Old Bay on everything.

Margery: Good afternoon, class! Orange you glad it's Saturday?

Abby: Margery, sweetie, I'm glad it's Saturday because I brought a whole bushel. Old Bay on that!

Players to watch

Illinois quarterback Katin Houser threw the most passes in the first six Illini games. He's 122 of 184 for 1,440 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions. Michael Clayton II threw the most in the win over Oregon, going 11 of 18 with two touchdown throws. Wide receiver Collin Dixon is the go-to target, with 54 catches for 678 yards and 10 touchdowns. Aidan Laughery leads the rushers with 514 yards. On defense, defensive back Matthew Bailey has 49 tackles.

Maryland quarterback Malik Washington has thrown the most passes in all seven Terrapin games. He's 155 of 261 for 1,615 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions. Chris Durr Jr. leads the receivers with 52 catches for 580 yards. DeJuan Williams leads the rushers with 281 yards and three scores. Linebacker Daniel Wingate has 44 tackles, and linebacker Zion Elee has 3.5 sacks.

Margery: Ten touchdown catches for Dixon. I made a chart, and the column went right off the top of the poster board.

What happened last week

Illinois beat Oregon 21-10 at home on Oct. 24. Laughery ran 13 times for 123 yards and a touchdown, and Dixon caught six passes for 65 yards and a score.

Margery: Oskee-wow-wow! I hugged three strangers and a mascot.

Maryland didn't play last week. Its last game was a 37-30 loss to Rutgers on Oct. 17, when Washington threw for 263 yards and two touchdowns and Durr caught six passes for 104 yards.

Abby: A week off means a week of rest, a week of practice and a week of crab cakes. All three matter.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Houser threw the most passes for Illinois in six games, but Clayton did against Oregon, so watch the teams' pregame notes for who takes the first snap. Washington has thrown the most passes in every Maryland game.

What the coaches are up to

Bret Bielema was named the 26th head coach in Illinois history on Dec. 19, 2020. He's an Illinois native, and one of his early wins was a nine-overtime thriller at Penn State in 2021, the longest game in college football history. His team has already won 38-37 in overtime at Michigan State this year.

Maryland has new leadership this week. Mike Locksley stepped down as head coach last week, and co-defensive coordinator Aazaar Abdul-Rahim was named interim head coach. Abdul-Rahim is a Washington, D.C., native in his second stint with the Terps, and Saturday is his first game in charge. This year's Terps score 28.3 points a game, including a 62-0 win over Hampton and a 38-14 win at UConn.

Abby: Coach Abdul-Rahim is a D.C. guy, and I know everybody in D.C. We should start a networking breakfast.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is Dixon against a Maryland defense that allows 33.3 points a game. On the other side, Washington loves to throw it, and he went 30 of 44 for 359 yards and three touchdowns against Virginia Tech. Both teams run the ball well, too. Illinois gains 5.2 yards a carry and Maryland gains 4.5, so the big guys up front on both sides will be busy.

What's happening on campus

SECU Stadium opened in 1950 and seats 51,802. The Mighty Sound of Maryland band will be on hand, and if you visit, ask somebody about Testudo, the diamondback terrapin who's at the heart of campus tradition. A Halloween noon kickoff should mean plenty of turtle shells in the stands.

Abby: I'm going as a crab. Obviously. Seasoned.

Anything else fun and true

Illinois is a founding member of the Big Ten and claims five national championships, from 1914 to 1951. On Oct. 18, 1924, Harold "Red" Grange scored four touchdowns against Michigan in the first 12 minutes of the Memorial Stadium dedication game. These two teams have split their last four meetings, and Illinois won 24-6 last year. Back in 2018, Maryland won a wild one, 63-33.

Margery: Abby, after the game, I'm making you a chart of everything I learned today.

Abby: And I'm sprinkling Old Bay on it. Then we'll say grace and eat. Old Bay on that!

My call: Illinois Fighting Illini 33, Maryland Terrapins 27.

display.story_text:
Cmdr. Annabel Merriweather, retired, rings a ship's bell at Gillette Stadium and announces, "All hands, we are underway." Declan Moriarty-Chen adjusts his sweater vest and replies, "I would posit, Commander, that your ship is sailing into a hurricane."

No. 5 Notre Dame (6-1) at Navy (2-5), Saturday at 12:00 p.m. ET on ABC at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, a neutral site. DraftKings has Notre Dame Fighting Irish −30.5 with a total of 56.5. My card: Navy Midshipmen +30.5, Over 56.5, and a final of Notre Dame Fighting Irish 43, Navy Midshipmen 15.

Declan speaks for Notre Dame, thesis in hand. "Proposition one: CJ Carr has 16 touchdown passes and one interception. Proposition two: we score 41.1 points a game and allow 13.4. Proposition three: we beat Stanford 58-7 and Purdue 49-10. And we had a week off after BYU."

The Commander speaks for Navy, steady at the helm. "Young man, Jackson Gutierrez ran 26 times for 228 yards and three touchdowns against North Texas. He has 869 rushing yards and 12 rushing scores. Coleman Cauley has 58 tackles. We run the option and take the clock with us. Anchors aweigh."

Why Navy? Because nobody has blown out the Midshipmen this season. Navy's losses came by eight at Florida Atlantic, four at UAB, five at Air Force, four at UTSA and ten to North Texas. The option keeps the ball on the ground, and Navy runs for 5.7 yards a carry. Long drives mean fewer possessions. My final has Notre Dame by four touchdowns, and that keeps Navy inside 30.5.

The worry is history. Notre Dame beat Navy 51-14 in 2024 and 49-10 last season, and both of those would have cleared 30.5 easily. Notre Dame's run defense allows 2.4 yards a carry, and the Irish have 16 takeaways. If Carr gets short fields off Navy turnovers, this gets out of hand.

Why the Over? Five of Navy's seven games have gone past 56.5 total points, including 49-39 last week and 38-34 at UTSA. Navy's defense allows 29.1 points a game. Notre Dame scores 41.1, and it has hit 49 or more three times. DraftKings had this total at 52.5 on Monday, and it has climbed since. The market sees it too. My 43-15 adds up to 58, a point and a half over 56.5.

Now the room. The Formula has Notre Dame 43-14, takes Navy +30.5 and the Over. Next Man Up has Notre Dame 42-15, also Navy and the Over. Follow The Money saw the market move toward the Irish, so it takes Notre Dame −30.5, but it likes the Over too. In The Trenches says the run-game gaps cancel, and Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up started it: "Two of us say Irish by four touchdowns and change. That's Navy."

Follow The Money held firm: "The money says more. I'm sailing with the Irish."

The Formula smiled: "At least we all agree on the Over. The Commander can ring the bell for that."

Bottom of the card: an option team that hasn't lost by more than ten, a Notre Dame offense that scores in bunches, and three Overs in the room. The Commander keeps her ship afloat. Give me the Midshipmen and the Over.

Notre Dame Fighting Irish 43, Navy Midshipmen 15. Navy Midshipmen cover the 30.5. Over 56.5.

Anchors Aweigh in Foxborough: No. 5 Notre Dame and Navy Renew a Classic at Gillette Stadium

No. 5 Notre Dame (6-1, independent) at Navy (2-5, 1-4 American). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough, Mass. (neutral site), ABC.

Your hosts are Declan Moriarty-Chen, a sweater-vested Notre Dame grad-student type who can recite the Irish schedule back to the leather-helmet era, and Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather, a Navy fan and former surface warfare officer who reads the option like a nautical chart.

Declan: I would posit, Commander, that this is one of the great traditions in college football.

Commander: You would posit correctly, young man. Welcome aboard. Mind the ship's bell. It's loud.

Players to watch

Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr has thrown the most passes in all seven Irish games. He's 129 of 193 for 1,639 yards, 16 touchdowns and just one interception. Jordan Faison leads the receivers with 34 catches for 451 yards and four scores, and Jonaz Walton leads the rushers with 426 yards. On defense, linebacker Drayk Bowen has 38 tackles and defensive lineman Boubacar Traore has 3.5 sacks.

Navy quarterback Jackson Gutierrez is the engine of the option. He has 869 rushing yards and 12 rushing touchdowns on 150 carries, and he's thrown for 692 yards and seven touchdowns on just 64 attempts. Tight end Jordan Collins has turned six catches into 212 yards and three scores. On defense, linebacker Coleman Cauley has 58 tackles and linebacker MarcAnthony Parker has four sacks.

Commander: Six catches, 212 yards. Jordan Collins is a submarine. You never see him until he surfaces in the end zone.

What happened last week

Notre Dame had the week off. Its last game was a 28-24 loss at BYU on Oct. 17, when Carr threw for 261 yards, Nolan James Jr. ran for a touchdown, and Jaden Greathouse caught eight balls for 125 yards.

Declan: A rare stumble. My thesis defense that week was a long one.

Navy lost 49-39 to North Texas on Oct. 24. Gutierrez ran 26 times for 228 yards and three touchdowns, and he threw a touchdown, too.

Commander: Steady as she goes. Two hundred twenty-eight yards is still a fine day at sea.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Carr has thrown the most passes in every Notre Dame game, and Gutierrez has done it in every Navy game since the opener, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Marcus Freeman was hired at Notre Dame on Dec. 3, 2021. His teams went 9-4, 10-3, 14-2 and 10-2 over the last four seasons, and this year's Irish score 41.1 points a game while allowing 13.4. They've forced 16 turnovers and lost just two.

Brian Newberry was hired at Navy on Dec. 19, 2022. Last season his Midshipmen went 11-2, won the Liberty Bowl 35-13 and finished No. 23 in the final AP poll. They also won the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy for the second straight season, beating Air Force 34-31 and Army 17-16.

Declan: Eleven wins and a trophy named for the Commander-in-Chief. I concede the point.

Player storylines

This game is a chess match between the Navy option and a Notre Dame defense that allows only 2.4 yards a carry. Navy gains 5.7 yards a carry, so something has to give. The Irish big guys up front will try to keep Gutierrez from turning the corner. On the other side, Carr has been nearly perfect with the ball, and Navy's defense allows 29.1 points a game.

What's happening on campus

This one's played away from both campuses, at Gillette Stadium outside Boston, and a Halloween noon kickoff in New England should bring plenty of sailors and leprechauns to the stands. Back in Annapolis, Navy usually plays at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, which seats 34,000. Notre Dame Stadium, built in 1930, seats 80,795, and visitors never miss "Touchdown Jesus."

Commander: I'm coming as a lighthouse. Practical and festive.

Anything else fun and true

Notre Dame claims 11 national championships, from 1924 through 1988. The Irish have won eight of the last nine regular-season meetings in this series, including 49-10 last year. Navy's lone win in that stretch was a thriller, 28-27 in 2016. And the Band of the Fighting Irish and the Navy midshipmen in the stands make this one of the most respectful scenes in the sport.

Declan: Commander, whatever happens, I'd be honored to say grace with you after the game.

Commander: The honor is mine, young man. Anchors aweigh.

My call: Notre Dame Fighting Irish 43, Navy Midshipmen 15.

Reina Valdés-Kowalski is wearing a full Gasparilla pirate hat in the Raymond James lot, waving a foam cutlass. Ozella Birchfield, Birmingham born and steel-family proud, walks up in a welder's apron and says, "Honey, that sword's plastic. Ours are forged."

UAB (4-3) at South Florida (5-2), Saturday at 12:00 p.m. ET on ESPNU at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa. It's an American game, and both teams are coming off an open week. DraftKings has South Florida Bulls −8.5 with a total of 42.5. My card: South Florida Bulls −8.5, Over 42.5, and a final of South Florida Bulls 30, UAB Blazers 16.

Ozella speaks for UAB, and she plays it like opening night. "Forged, not given! We beat East Carolina 30-17 in overtime. Ryder Burton threw for 262 yards and CJ Smith caught eight balls for 119. Muaaz Byard has 69 tackles, and Marlin Dean has five sacks."

Reina speaks for South Florida, cutlass raised. "Arrr, Ozella, we beat Kent State 29-2. Michael Van Buren Jr. hasn't thrown an interception all season. D.J. Crowther has 518 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. And our defense allows 15.1 points a game. Pirate-approved!"

Why South Florida? The Bulls have the best defense on the field. It held Florida International to nine, Bowling Green to six and Kent State to two. UAB's offense scores 23.3 points a game, and on the road it has struggled: a 42-23 loss at Illinois, a 21-14 loss at Louisiana and a 38-13 loss at Memphis. Burton has five interceptions. Last season South Florida won this matchup 48-18. My final has the Bulls by two touchdowns, and that clears the 8.5.

The worry is the South Florida offense when it stalls. The Bulls scored 13 in a loss to Temple and 14 at Bowling Green. The run games are about even, with both teams near four yards a carry. If USF settles for field goals, UAB can hang around the way it did in a 24-20 win over Navy.

Why the Over? The last three meetings in this series went 56-35, 35-25 and 48-18, and every one of them sailed past 42.5. South Florida has scored 24 or more in four games, and UAB has scored 23 or more in five. Both offenses are rested. My 30-16 adds up to 46, three and a half points over 42.5.

Now the room. The Formula has South Florida 28-16, takes the Bulls −8.5 and the Over. Next Man Up has South Florida 31-15, same side, same Over. Follow The Money saw the market slide toward UAB and the total drop, so it takes UAB +8.5 and the Under. In The Trenches finds no gap worth a call, and Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up started it: "Two of us have the Bulls by two touchdowns. Follow The Money, you're with the dragon?"

Follow The Money shrugged: "The total fell. I don't argue with a falling number."

The Formula answered: "Then argue with the last three meetings. All of them went Over."

Bottom of the card: the better defense at home, a UAB team that hasn't won on the road, and a total too low for this series. Reina gets her pirate parade. Give me the Bulls and the Over.

Pirates and Dragons on Halloween: UAB Visits South Florida as Two Rested Teams Meet in Tampa

UAB (4-3, 2-1 American) at South Florida (5-2, 1-2 American). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa, Fla., ESPNU.

Your hosts are Ozella Birchfield, a Birmingham native, steel-family granddaughter and community-theater actor, and Reina Valdés-Kowalski, a boat-show model turned Bulls roster maven who can't go five minutes without a Gasparilla pirate bit.

Reina: Ahoy, Ozella! Welcome to Tampa. Mind the cannon fire. It's ceremonial.

Ozella: Darling, I'm from Birmingham. We were making steel when your pirates were still drawing maps. Forged, not given!

Players to watch

UAB quarterback Ryder Burton has thrown the most passes in all seven Blazer games. He's 91 of 167 for 1,184 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions. Rod Robinson II leads the rushers with 436 yards, and CJ Smith leads the receivers with 350 yards on 19 catches. On defense, linebacker Muaaz Byard has a team-high 69 tackles and linebacker Marlin Dean has five sacks.

South Florida quarterback Michael Van Buren Jr. has thrown the most passes in all seven Bulls games. He's 115 of 179 for 1,266 yards and six touchdowns, and he hasn't thrown an interception in any of them. Running back D.J. Crowther has 518 yards and seven touchdowns, and Bryson Rodgers leads the receivers with 30 catches for 334 yards. Defensive back Ayden Jackson has 38 tackles, and end Michael Williams II has four sacks.

Reina: Not one interception in seven games. Van Buren guards that ball like buried treasure.

What happened last week

Both teams had the week off. UAB's last game was a 30-17 overtime win over East Carolina on Oct. 15. Burton threw for 262 yards and two touchdowns, and Smith caught eight balls for 119 yards.

Ozella: Overtime! I gave a standing ovation so long the ushers asked me to sit.

South Florida's last game was a 29-2 win over Kent State on Oct. 17. Van Buren went 22 of 27 for 193 yards and a touchdown, and Cameron Seldon caught a scoring throw.

Reina: Two points allowed. The defense walked the plank, and Kent State fell off it.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Burton and Van Buren have each thrown the most passes in every game for their teams, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Both head coaches are in their first season. Brian Hartline was hired at South Florida on Dec. 3, 2025, and his Bulls allow just 15.1 points a game. They've won at Army and at Bowling Green and beaten Kent State 29-2.

Alex Mortensen was hired at UAB on Dec. 5, 2025, two days after Hartline. His Blazers like to run the ball, and they've already won three home games over FBS teams: UL Monroe, Navy and East Carolina.

Ozella: Two first-year coaches. It's like opening night at the community theater. Everybody's nervous and everybody's brilliant.

Player storylines

The matchup to circle is Burton against a South Florida defense that held Florida International to nine points and Bowling Green to six. On the other side, Crowther and the Bulls big guys up front face a UAB defense that allows 4.4 yards a carry. Both teams run for about four yards a carry, so expect a ground battle.

What's happening on campus

Raymond James Stadium opened in 1998 and seats 65,828. A Halloween noon kickoff in Tampa means sunshine, pirate hats and Rocky the Bull leading the cheers. UAB fans will bring the spirit of Blaze the dragon and the UAB Marching Blazers from Protective Stadium, which opened in Birmingham in 2021.

Reina: I'm dressing up as a pirate. Which is what I wear every week.

Ozella: I'm coming as Lady Macbeth. I've played her twice.

Anything else fun and true

South Florida has climbed fast. From 2021 through 2025, the Bulls went 2-10, 1-11, 7-6, 7-6 and 9-4. UAB went 9-4 in 2021, and this year's Blazers have already matched last season's four wins. These two have met three times since 2023. UAB won a wild one 56-35 in 2023, and South Florida won 35-25 in 2024 and 48-18 last season.

Ozella: Reina, after the game, I'm taking you to dinner. We'll say grace and you can tell me pirate stories.

Reina: Deal, matey. Pirate-approved!

My call: South Florida Bulls 30, UAB Blazers 16.

Corwin Dahlquist is pouring imaginary syrup over a Waldo Stadium program and calling it "a full stack forecast." Darcy Fenwick, Bowling Green's old club hockey goalie, taps her stick on the bleachers and says, "Save it, Corwin. We beat you the last two times we played."

Bowling Green (2-6) at Western Michigan (5-3), Saturday at 12:00 p.m. ET on CBSSN at Waldo Stadium in Kalamazoo. The Broncos are 3-1 in MAC play. Michigan (4-3) at Rutgers (2-5), Saturday at 12:30 p.m. ET on BTN at SHI Stadium in Piscataway. It's a Big Ten game, and both teams are 1-3 in league play. DraftKings has Michigan Wolverines −14 with a total of 46.5. My card: Rutgers Scarlet Knights +14, Over 46.5, and a final of Michigan Wolverines 30, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 22.

Vinny speaks for Rutgers, sub knife in hand. "Gus, buddy, KJ Duff has 45 catches for 774 yards and nine touchdowns. Antwan Raymond just ran 18 times for 150 yards at Northwestern. We won 37-30 at Maryland. Exit 9 never lies."

Why Rutgers? Because Michigan doesn't blow anybody out. The Wolverines score 20.3 points a game, and their four wins came 13-12, 17-10, 52-17 and 21-18. Only UTEP lost to them by more than a touchdown. Michigan scored six points in regulation and overtime combined against Indiana, and Tommy Carr threw the most passes in that one, not Bryce Underwood. Michigan's run game gains 3.7 yards a carry. My final has Michigan by a touchdown and change.

The worry is the Rutgers defense. It allows 33.3 points a game and 5.8 yards a carry, and Northwestern beat it 42-14 last week. Rutgers has also been flipping between Dylan Lonergan and AJ Surace at quarterback. And history isn't kind: Michigan beat Rutgers 78-0 in 2016 and 52-0 in 2019.

Why the Over? Every Rutgers game this season has gone past 46.5. Duff and Lonergan can throw it, and the Rutgers defense gives up points too. DraftKings had this total at 47.5 on Monday, and it ticked down to 46.5. My 30-22 adds up to 52, comfortably over 46.5.

Maize Meets the Turnpike: Michigan Visits Rutgers in Piscataway on Halloween

Michigan (4-3, 1-3 Big Ten) at Rutgers (2-5, 1-3 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12:30 p.m. ET, SHI Stadium, Piscataway, N.J., BTN.

Your hosts are Gus Hartwell, a Michigan engineering-school stats savant in a maize sweater who labels his data with fight-song lyrics, and Vinny Scolari, an Exit 9 Jersey guy who gives directions by Turnpike exit.

Vinny: Gus! Welcome to Exit 9! You found the place okay?

Gus: Vincent, I brought a laminated map, three backup routes and a spreadsheet titled "Champions of the West."

Vinny: Fuhgeddaboudit. Just follow the smell of the six-foot sub.

Players to watch

Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood leads the team in passing at 72 of 124 for 924 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions, though Tommy Carr threw the most passes against Indiana last week. Running back Jordan Marshall leads the rushers with 319 yards and four touchdowns. JJ Buchanan is the top receiver with 33 catches for 539 yards and four scores. On defense, linebacker Troy Bowles has 55 tackles and end John Henry Daley has four sacks.

Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan leads the team at 74 of 127 for 1,066 yards, 10 touchdowns and six interceptions. AJ Surace threw the most passes against Northwestern last week. Running back Antwan Raymond has 648 yards and six touchdowns, and receiver KJ Duff has been a highlight machine with 45 catches for 774 yards and nine touchdowns. Defensive back Chris Joines leads the tacklers with 34, and Rondo Porter has 2.5 sacks.

Vinny: Nine touchdowns for KJ Duff, Gus. That's more touchdowns than there are exits between here and the shore. Almost.

What happened last week

Michigan lost 13-6 in overtime to Indiana at home on Oct. 24. Carr was 20 of 32 for 167 yards, and Buchanan caught six balls for 57 yards.

Gus: Victors. valiant. later. I spent Sunday in the library.

Rutgers lost 42-14 at Northwestern on Oct. 24. Raymond was the bright spot with 18 carries for 150 yards and a touchdown.

Vinny: I was around Exit 7A after that one. Maybe 7. But Raymond? Exit 9 all day.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Underwood threw the most passes in Michigan's first six games and Carr did against Indiana, while Lonergan and Surace have traded that role for Rutgers, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Kyle Whittingham was named Michigan's 22nd head coach on Dec. 26, 2025, after 21 seasons at Utah, where he went 177-88 with eight seasons of 10 or more wins. His Wolverines are built on defense, allowing 15.7 points a game.

Greg Schiano returned to Rutgers on Nov. 30, 2019, for his second stint. His team is the least penalized in FBS at 28.7 penalty yards a game.

Vinny: Discipline, baby. I'd yell that from the top of the Driscoll Bridge.

Gus: Coach Whittingham would approve. He'd also ask you to come down safely.

Player storylines

The big story is Raymond against a Michigan defense that allows only 2.8 yards a carry. Something has to give. On the other side, Buchanan and the Michigan offense want to get rolling after a long day against Indiana. Michigan's big guys up front will try to push around a Rutgers defense that gives up 5.8 yards a carry. And Duff will be looking for touchdown number 10.

What's happening on campus

SHI Stadium is listed at 52,454, and a Halloween kickoff in Piscataway should bring plenty of scarlet costumes. Gus notes that Michigan Stadium's record crowd is 115,109, set against Notre Dame on Sept. 7, 2013.

Gus: I'm dressing as a spreadsheet. Very scary for opponents.

Vinny: I'm dressing as the Turnpike. Very scary for everybody.

Anything else fun and true

The very first college football game was played in New Brunswick on Nov. 6, 1869, and Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4. Michigan played its first game on May 30, 1879, and has more wins than any program in college football. Three Wolverines have won the Heisman: Tom Harmon in 1940, Desmond Howard in 1991 and Charles Woodson in 1997.

Vinny: So Gus, the birthplace of football is hosting the winningest program. Saturday's got history all over it.

Gus: Agreed, Vincent. Win or lose, I'll split that sub with you. We'll say grace first.

Vinny: Six feet, Gus. Everybody eats.

My call: Michigan Wolverines 30, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 22.

Winnie Pocklington stands at the gate of S.B. Ballard Stadium in a paper crown, proclaiming each arriving fan a knight of the realm. Mercy Holderby walks up in green scrubs under her Marshall jacket and says, "Winnie, I'm off shift for exactly one game." Winnie bows. "Then the court grants you safe conduct, nurse. Mostly."

Marshall (4-3) at Old Dominion (2-6), Saturday at 1 p.m. ET on ESPN+ at S.B. Ballard Stadium in Norfolk. It's a Sun Belt game: Marshall is 1-2 in league play, Old Dominion 1-4. DraftKings has Marshall Thundering Herd −2.5 with a total of 45.5. My card: Old Dominion Monarchs +2.5, Under 45.5, and a final of Old Dominion Monarchs 25, Marshall Thundering Herd 20.

Mercy speaks for Marshall, honest as always. "We Are. We beat South Alabama 20-13 last time out. Caleb Clark-Glover has 51 tackles. Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw has 25 catches for 335 yards. And we beat Old Dominion 48-24 last year."

Winnie speaks for Old Dominion, crown tilted. "Hear ye! Javen Gibson has five sacks. Lucas Struck has 61 tackles. We went to Boone and beat App State 10-3. Our defense allows 26.8 points a game, and it keeps this kingdom in games. Long live the Monarchs."

Why Old Dominion? Because Marshall's defense is the weakest piece on the field. The Herd allows 30.7 points a game and 5.3 yards a carry, and its turnover margin sits at minus-9. Even Marshall's wins have been tight: 28-26, 30-24, 36-35 and 20-13. Old Dominion's defense can steal a game, as App State found out. With the home crowd and 2.5 points, the Monarchs are my side, and my final has them winning outright.

The risk is the Old Dominion offense. It scores 15.5 points a game and was shut out 26-0 at Louisiana Tech last week. Three different quarterbacks have thrown the most passes in a game this season. The Monarchs have also struggled to protect the quarterback. And Marshall has won eight of the nine meetings since 2016.

Why the Under? Old Dominion scored 17 points or fewer in five of its eight games, and five of its games stayed under 45.5. Marshall's last game finished 20-13. The total ticked down from 46.5 to 45.5 during the week, and I'm with the move. My 25-20 adds up to 45, under 45.5.

Now the room, and it likes the Monarchs. The Formula has Old Dominion 25-23 and takes the Monarchs, though its total lands Over. Next Man Up has Old Dominion 25-18, same side, with the Under. Follow The Money skips the side and takes the Under. In The Trenches has no pick, since the run games cancel out.

The Royal Court Welcomes the Herd: Marshall Visits Old Dominion in Norfolk

Marshall (4-3, 1-2 Sun Belt) at Old Dominion (2-6, 1-4 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 1 p.m. ET, S.B. Ballard Stadium, Norfolk, Va., ESPN+.

Your hosts are Mercy Holderby, a Huntington nurse and the daughter of two Marshall grads, and Winnie Pocklington, an Old Dominion fan who treats every first down like a knighthood.

Winnie: Hear ye, hear ye! The court welcomes the lady from Huntington!

Mercy: Thank you, Winnie. I brought a first-aid kit, a thermos of coffee and the loudest "We Are" in Virginia.

Winnie: The court approves of all three. Especially the coffee.

Players to watch

Marshall has used two quarterbacks. Carlos Del Rio-Wilson leads the team at 90 of 140 for 1,041 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions, and he threw for 413 yards against Gardner-Webb. Zion Turner threw the most passes in each of the last two games. Judah Price leads the rushers with 237 yards, and Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw leads the receivers with 25 catches for 335 yards and four scores. Defensive back Caleb Clark-Glover has 51 tackles, and Kelvon McBride has two sacks.

Old Dominion's top passer is Quinn Henicle, who is 54 of 98 for 656 yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions. Ryan Huff and Jaxon Potter have also thrown the most passes in a game this year. Devin Roche leads the rushers with 382 yards, and TJ Johnson leads the receivers with 17 catches for 265 yards. On defense, Javen Gibson has five sacks and safety Lucas Struck has 61 tackles.

Winnie: Five sacks for Sir Javen Gibson. I've knighted him five times. He's running out of shoulders.

What happened last week

Marshall beat South Alabama 20-13 at home on Tuesday, Oct. 20. Turner was 21 of 33 for 181 yards, Khalil Wilkins ran eight times for 69 yards, and Toby Payne caught seven balls for 69 yards.

Mercy: Twenty to thirteen. I'll take a win with my whole heart, every single time.

Old Dominion lost 26-0 at Louisiana Tech on Oct. 24. Potter was 18 of 34 for 154 yards, and Leon Haughton Jr. caught four balls for 45 yards.

Winnie: The crown was polished. The court reconvened on Monday. We move on.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Turner threw the most passes in Marshall's last two games, and Potter did for Old Dominion last week, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Tony Gibson is in his second season at Marshall. He's a 1994 Glenville State graduate and was previously defensive coordinator at West Virginia and NC State.

Ricky Rahne was hired at Old Dominion on Dec. 7, 2019. Last year his Monarchs went 10-3, and this year the defense has forced 12 turnovers.

Mercy: Coach Gibson knows defense. We just need it to show up for four quarters.

Winnie: Coach Rahne's defense shows up. The offense is still finding its robes.

Player storylines

Marshall's offense gains 4.4 yards a carry, and Old Dominion's defense allows only 3.5. That's the matchup to watch. Old Dominion's big guys up front have had a rough year, allowing 32 sacks in seven games, so protecting whoever plays quarterback is job one. Gibson and the Monarch defense will want to pressure Turner, and Clark-Glover will be busy in the Marshall secondary.

What's happening on campus

S.B. Ballard Stadium in Norfolk is listed at 20,118 seats, and a Halloween afternoon by the harbor should bring plenty of blue-and-silver costumes and a few royal crowns. Marshall's home, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, is one of two Division I stadiums named for a woman.

Winnie: I'll be dressed as a queen. It's not a costume. It's a lifestyle.

Mercy: I'll be in green scrubs. Also not a costume.

Anything else fun and true

Old Dominion's first team, in 1930, was the William & Mary Norfolk Division Braves. The modern Monarchs were founded in 2009 and joined the Sun Belt in 2022. Marshall's first game against another college was a 15-0 win over Shelton College on Nov. 24, 1903, and the 2014 Herd went 13-1. These two have met often lately: Marshall won 42-35 in 2024 and 48-24 in 2025, and Old Dominion won 38-14 in 2016.

Mercy: Winnie, whatever happens, I'll treat you to dinner afterward. We'll say grace first.

Winnie: The court accepts. Long live the Monarchs, and God bless the Herd.

My call: Old Dominion Monarchs 25, Marshall Thundering Herd 20.

Pull up a pine."

Wilson can throw it, too: he had 280 yards in Stillwater, and Williams caught nine balls for 135. Both offenses should find room. My 28-23 adds up to 51, over 47.5.

Now the room, and it mostly agrees with me. The Formula has K-State 28-24 and takes the Wildcats and the Over. Next Man Up has K-State 28-22, same side, same Over. In The Trenches backs K-State too. Follow The Money goes the other way, Colorado and the Under, because the market moved toward the Buffs.

Coastal Carolina (2-5, 1-2 Sun Belt) at Georgia State (4-3, 1-2 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 2 p.m. ET, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta, ESPN+.

Your hosts are Goldie Seabrook, a Conway native from a shrimp-boat family who writes like the tide, and Malik Overstreet, a Georgia State fan who knows every MARTA stop and every Panther third-down tendency.

Malik: Goldie! Welcome to the big city. How was the drive?

Goldie: Long, Malik. I hit traffic on the Connector and thought about turning the car into a boat.

Malik: That's the Connector at rush hour. Welcome to my world.

Players to watch

Coastal quarterback Deuce Bailey has thrown the most passes in every game. He's 109 of 204 for 1,638 yards, 16 touchdowns and four interceptions. Dominic Lee-Knicely leads the rushers with 452 yards and three scores, and Colton Hinton leads the receivers with 297 yards and four touchdowns on 13 catches. On defense, linebacker Marcellius Pulliam has 67 tackles and end Ibrahim Diawara has five sacks.

Georgia State quarterback Cameran Brown threw the most passes in each of the first six games. He's 110 of 166 for 1,356 yards, 14 touchdowns and five interceptions, and he threw six touchdowns against Old Dominion. Ayden Pereira threw the most passes last week. Lanear McCrary Jr. leads the rushers with 399 yards and four touchdowns, and Rodshaun Dorsey leads the receivers with 24 catches for 418 yards and eight scores. Linebacker Xavier Esqillion has seven sacks, and Jaydon Hood has 45 tackles.

Goldie: Sixteen touchdown throws for Deuce Bailey, Malik. That's a full net of shrimp.

What happened last week

Coastal had an open date last week. Its last game was a 35-32 loss to App State on Oct. 16, when Bailey threw for 298 yards and three touchdowns, Lee-Knicely ran 18 times for 90 yards, and Robby Washington caught five balls for 118 yards and a score.

Goldie: Low tide. But we had a whole week to rest and get ready.

Georgia State lost 38-32 at Arkansas State on Oct. 24. Pereira threw two touchdowns, Qwantavius Wiggins ran eight times for 99 yards and a score, and Dorsey caught three balls for 85 yards and a touchdown.

Malik: I blamed the traffic on 75/85. Then I moved on.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Bailey has thrown the most passes in every Coastal game, while Brown did for Georgia State in its first six games and Pereira did last week, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Ryan Beard leads Coastal Carolina, and CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2025. His defense has 15 sacks, 37 tackles for loss and 14 takeaways.

Dell McGee leads Georgia State, and CFBD dates his hire to Feb. 23, 2024. His offense holds the ball 32:34 a game and runs for 206 yards a game.

Malik: Coach McGee's offense moves like the HOV lane. Smooth and fast.

Goldie: Coach Beard's defense comes in like the tide. Steady and strong.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is the Georgia State ground game against a Coastal defense that allows 4.8 yards a carry. Coastal's big guys up front will need to slow McCrary and Wiggins. On the other side, Bailey and his receivers want to keep throwing deep, while Esqillion hunts for sack number eight. Georgia State is 3-0 at home this season, so Coastal will have to bring its best.

What's happening on campus

Center Parc Stadium sits about ten minutes from Georgia State's downtown campus and is listed at 25,000 seats. A Halloween afternoon in Atlanta should bring plenty of blue-and-white costumes, and Coastal fans will bring their teal.

Malik: I'm dressing as a MARTA train. I'll arrive on time.

Goldie: I'm dressing as a shrimp boat. I'll arrive whenever the tide says.

Anything else fun and true

Georgia State football was founded in 2010. Coastal plays at Brooks Stadium in Conway, built in 2003, and its teal turf is the tradition Goldie would show you first. These two have met in every season since 2017, and Coastal has won five of those nine games, including a 51-0 win in 2020 and a 40-27 win in 2025. Georgia State won 42-40 in 2021 and 30-17 in 2023.

Goldie: Malik, win or lose, the shrimp are on me after the game. We'll say grace first.

Malik: Deal, Goldie. Let's ride.

My call: Georgia State Panthers 33, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 25.

Bart: Overtime on the road. We battled. I graded the Memphis tiger's costume, and it was brushed.

Teddy: Our ground game is our Rocky montage. We'll see whose works best.

The matchup to watch is Mason and the Temple ground game against an ECU defense that allows 3.3 yards a carry. Temple's big guys up front will need to win in the trenches. On the other side, Engleman wants another big day, and Sides is coming off a big night at Memphis. ECU won the last three meetings, so Temple has some motivation.

Except for the 1999 Miami game, the Pirates have played every home game at Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium since 1963, and CFBD lists it at 50,000 on natural grass. A Halloween afternoon in Greenville should bring plenty of purple-and-gold costumes, and Bart's tricorn hat is coming out for this one. Temple plays home games at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, listed at 69,879.

Teddy: I'm dressing as Hooter the Owl. Nobody insult Hooter.

Bart: Teddy, nobody has insulted Hooter.

Anything else fun and true

East Carolina played its first season in 1932 and has won seven conference championships and eleven bowl games. The Pirates went 9-4 last year. Temple went 5-7 last season, and its fight song is "Fight! Temple Fight!" These two have met often: ECU won 49-46 in 2022, 56-34 in 2024 and 45-14 in 2025, while Temple won 49-6 in 2018.

Bart: Teddy, whatever happens, the barbecue's on me after the game. We'll say grace first.

Teddy: Deal, Bart. That's Temple Made, and that's Pirate kind.

Cardinal Meets Cardinals: Stanford Visits Louisville on Halloween

Stanford (4-4, 2-3 ACC) at Louisville (4-3, 3-2 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:15 p.m. ET, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville, Ky., ACC Network.

Your hosts are Ignatius "Iggy" Yamamoto-Ross, the founder of three failed apps and one great Cardinal model, and Bianca Thornberry, a Louisville derby-party hostess who rates every game's hat-worthiness.

Bianca: Welcome to Louisville, Iggy! Hold your hats.

Iggy: Thanks, Bianca. Quick question. Is it confusing that we're both Cardinals?

Bianca: Not at all, darling. We have an S on the end. And a much bigger hat budget.

Iggy: Noted. I'll put it in the deck.

Players to watch

Louisville quarterback Lincoln Kienholz has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 121 of 180 for 1,844 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Isaac Brown leads the rushers with 568 yards and four scores, and Lawayne McCoy leads the receivers with 513 yards and four touchdowns. Linebacker T.J. Capers leads the defense with 53 tackles, Clev Lubin has five sacks, and defensive back Kaleb Beasley has five interceptions.

Stanford quarterback Davis Warren has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 163 of 271 for 1,933 yards, 11 touchdowns and two interceptions. Micah Ford leads the rushers with 679 yards and eight touchdowns, and Caden High leads the receivers with 30 catches for 440 yards. Safety Jay Green leads the team with 49 tackles.

Iggy: Micah Ford is pure product-market fit. Four touchdowns against Elon tied a Stanford single-game record.

Bianca: Kaleb Beasley has five interceptions, darling. That's a five-hat secondary.

What happened last week

Stanford beat NC State 31-28 at home on Friday, Oct. 23. Warren went 22 of 37 for 303 yards and four touchdowns, Ford ran 22 times for 150 yards, and High caught nine balls for 103 yards and a score. It was Stanford's second straight win, after a 34-7 victory over Elon.

Iggy: Two wins in a row. We're officially trending.

Louisville had an open date. Its last game was a 34-26 win at Syracuse on Oct. 17, when Kienholz threw for 310 yards and ran for two touchdowns, and McCoy caught five balls for 93 yards.

Bianca: Rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub. I spent mine shopping for feathers.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Kienholz has thrown the most passes for Louisville in every game, and Warren has done the same for Stanford, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jeff Brohm leads Louisville, and CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 7, 2022. His teams went 10-4, 9-4 and 9-4 the last three seasons. This year's Cardinals score 38.7 points a game, run the ball well, and have 12 takeaways against six giveaways.

Tavita Pritchard is in his first season as Stanford's head coach, and CFBD records his hire date as Nov. 28, 2025. He's a Stanford alum who played quarterback on the 2007 team that upset USC, and he coached quarterbacks for the Washington Commanders from 2023 to 2025.

Iggy: Founder returns to the company. Best origin story in the deck.

Bianca: That's a lovely story, Iggy. I'd wear a hat for it.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is the Louisville ground game against a Stanford defense that has struggled to stop the run. Brown and Kienholz both carry the ball, and Louisville's big guys up front like to push people around. On the other side, Ford is coming off a 150-yard game, and Warren has thrown for more than 300 yards in three games. Stanford won the only recent meeting, 38-35 in 2024, so Louisville has a memory to fix.

What's happening on campus

L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium was built in 1998 and has a listed capacity of 60,000. The Marching Cards will be there, and so will "Fight! UofL." Halloween in Louisville means red costumes, and at least one very large red hat. If you visit, ask somebody about the Cardinal Bird.

Iggy: I'm dressing as a cardinal. Singular. On brand.

Bianca: Then I'll dress as a whole flock.

Anything else fun and true

Stanford has fielded teams nearly every year since 1892, and it played rugby instead of football from 1906 to 1917. The teams were known as the "Indians" from 1930 to 1972, and they've been the "Cardinal" since the 1982 season. A 1975 student vote to become the "Robber Barons" wasn't approved. Stanford Stadium was built in 2006 and seats 50,424.

Bianca: Whatever happens, Iggy, there's a derby pie waiting after the game. We'll say grace first.

Iggy: Deal, Bianca. Ship it. Go Card.

My call: Louisville Cardinals 42, Stanford Cardinal 19.

Arizona State (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) at No. 8 BYU (6-1, 3-1 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo, Utah, Fox.

Your hosts are Skylar Vanterpool, an Arizona State fan whose motto is "Hydrate and Dominate," and Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi, a BYU superfan and Provo trail guide whose dad jokes are so clean they sparkle.

Bryce: Oh my heck, Skylar! Welcome to Provo. That's Y Mountain right there.

Skylar: It's beautiful, Bryce. Also, you're at altitude. Drink some water.

Bryce: Why did the Sun Devil drink so much water in Provo? Because it heard the Cougars were a thirsty bunch.

Skylar: Hydrate, Bryce. And maybe workshop that one.

Players to watch

BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 116 of 184 for 1,514 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions, and he ran for two scores and caught another against Notre Dame. LJ Martin leads the rushers with 344 yards, and freshman Legend Glasker leads the receivers with 28 catches for 498 yards. Linebacker Cade Uluave leads the defense with 45 tackles, and Tausili Akana has 3.5 sacks.

Arizona State receiver Reed Harris is the headliner, with 47 catches for 800 yards and eight touchdowns. Cutter Boley leads the team in passing at 1,360 yards and 13 touchdowns, but Mikey Keene has thrown the most passes the last two games. Cardae Mack leads the rushers with 400 yards and six scores. Linebacker Owen Long leads the defense with 63 tackles, and Julian Hugo has four sacks.

Skylar: Reed Harris catches deep balls like I catch rays. Effortlessly.

Bryce: Glasker's numbers are like my jokes, Skylar. They just keep landing.

What happened last week

BYU lost 39-31 in overtime at UCF on Oct. 24. Bachmeier threw for 257 yards and two touchdowns, and Kyler Kasper caught six balls for 129 yards and a score. It was the Cougars' first loss of the season.

Bryce: That one stung. But you climb back up the trail one step at a time.

Arizona State beat Kansas State 28-17 at home on Oct. 24. Mack ran 26 times for 159 yards and four touchdowns, Keene threw for 160 yards, and Harris caught six balls for 147 yards.

Skylar: Four touchdowns for Cardae Mack! I cannonballed into the kiddie pool. Twice.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Bachmeier has thrown the most passes for BYU in every game. For Arizona State, Boley did it in the first five games and Keene in the last two, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Kalani Sitake played fullback for BYU under LaVell Edwards and became head coach in 2016. He's the first Tongan head coach in college football, and he entered the Polynesian Football Hall of Fame in 2025. His teams went 11-2 and 12-2 the last two seasons, and this year's defense allows 18.6 points a game.

Kenny Dillingham became Arizona State's 26th head coach on Nov. 27, 2022, and took the Sun Devils to the 2024 Big 12 championship, beating Iowa State 45-19 in the title game. His offense loves to throw it, and Harris is the proof.

Bryce: Coach Sitake was a fullback. He still runs downhill.

Skylar: Coach Dillingham coaches with so much energy, he must run on electrolytes.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Harris against a BYU defense that doesn't allow much. On the other side, the Cougars want their big guys up front to get Martin and the run game going against an Arizona State defense that has given up yards on the ground. These two split the last two meetings: BYU won 27-17 in 2021, and Arizona State won 28-23 in 2024.

What's happening on campus

LaVell Edwards Stadium is named for the coach who won 19 conference titles and the 1984 national title, and CFBD lists it at 63,470 seats. A Halloween afternoon under the mountains should bring plenty of royal blue in the stands, along with some very creative costumes. Arizona State's home, Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, is listed at 65,870.

Skylar: I'm dressing as a cactus. A hydrated one.

Bryce: I'm dressing as a trail map. You can find yourself on me.

Anything else fun and true

BYU started playing college football in 1922, has won 23 conference championships and the 1984 national championship, and joined the Big 12 on July 1, 2023. Arizona State beat Michigan 22-15 in the Rose Bowl on Jan. 1, 1987, and earlier this season it beat Kansas 24-17 at Wembley Stadium in London.

Bryce: Whatever happens, Skylar, dinner's on me. We'll say grace first.

Skylar: Deal, Bryce. I'll bring the water.

Your hosts are Fitz Calloway, a hoops-first Lawrence native who converts every football stat into basketball points, and Ryder Galloway, a Stockyards cowboy turned finance guy who explains defenses as cattle drives.

Ryder: Howdy, Fitz, and welcome to Fort Worth! Not Dallas. Never Dallas.

Fitz: Thanks, Ryder. I brought a basketball. Old habits.

Ryder: This is a football game, partner.

Fitz: Sure. But a touchdown is two and a half three-pointers, and nobody can tell me otherwise.

Players to watch

TCU quarterback Jaden Craig has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 162 of 240 for 2,066 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions. Jeremy Payne leads the rushers with 429 yards, and Ed Small leads the receivers with 38 catches for 514 yards. On defense, Koron Hayward has 4.5 sacks, and linebacker Hudson Hooper leads the team with 41 tackles.

Kansas quarterback Isaiah Marshall has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 105 of 196 for 1,506 yards, 11 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Dylan Edwards leads the rushers with 531 yards and four scores, and Nik McMillan leads the receivers with 25 catches for 466 yards and five touchdowns. Linebacker Trey Lathan leads the defense with 48 tackles, and Leroy Harris III has 3.5 sacks.

Ryder: Hayward gets after a quarterback like a flank rider after a stray. Yeehaw.

Fitz: McMillan has five touchdown catches on just 25 grabs. That's a fast break, Ryder.

Kansas beat Baylor 25-24 on Homecoming in Lawrence on Oct. 24. Edwards carried 30 times for 156 yards, Marshall threw two touchdowns, and McMillan caught a scoring ball. It was KU's 114th Homecoming, and the parade on Jayhawk Boulevard was back for the first time in seven years.

Sonny Dykes was hired at TCU on Nov. 29, 2021, and in his first season he took the Frogs to the national championship game. This year his defense is the story. TCU allows only 13.9 points a game, and every one of its losses has been close.

Lance Leipold has led Kansas since 2021. Before that he won six Division III national championships at Wisconsin-Whitewater and reached 100 wins faster than any coach in NCAA history, in his 106th game. His 2023 team went 9-4. This year his offense runs the ball well, behind Edwards and the big guys up front.

Fitz: Coach Leipold wins everywhere he goes. That's a Hall of Fame jump shot.

Minnesota (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) at No. 4 Indiana (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, Ind., CBS.

Your hosts are Torvald "Tor" Engebretsen, a Minnesota ski-hill Gopher who owns enough coats to lend one out, and Mallory Penhallow, a former Miss Monroe County runner-up who runs a 40-tab efficiency model.

Mallory: Welcome to Bloomington, Tor! Hello, Hoosier Nation!

Tor: Thank you, Mallory. I brought cocoa, and a spare coat in case you get chilly.

Mallory: That's very sweet. I'll wear it over the sash.

Tor: And I should mention we're bringing home a bronze pig. Well, it's already home. We won it Saturday.

Players to watch

Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 116 of 187 for 1,741 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception. Turbo Richard leads the rushers with 711 yards and six scores, and Charlie Becker leads the receivers with 42 catches for 726 yards and eight touchdowns. On defense, Tobi Osunsanmi has nine sacks, and linebacker Isaiah Jones leads the team with 61 tackles.

Minnesota quarterback Drake Lindsey has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 141 of 222 for 1,472 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions. TJ Thomas leads the rushers with 325 yards, and Javon Tracy leads the receivers with 39 catches for 420 yards. Linebacker Maverick Baranowski leads the defense with 51 tackles, and TJ Bush Jr. has four sacks.

Mallory: Nine sacks for Tobi Osunsanmi, Tor. It's the explosives, darling.

Tor: Maverick Baranowski has 51 tackles. In Minnesota, we call that a good catch.

What happened last week

Minnesota beat Iowa 13-10 at home on Oct. 24, on Homecoming, and took back Floyd of Rosedale, the bronze pig trophy introduced in 1935. Lindsey threw for 137 yards, and Tracy caught seven balls for 45 yards. The defense did the heavy lifting, holding Iowa to 10 points.

Tor: Floyd is back in Minneapolis. I may have hugged a pig. A bronze one. Respectfully.

Indiana won 13-6 in overtime at Michigan on Oct. 24. Hoover went 8 of 18 for 81 yards, Richard ran 19 times for 68 yards, and the defense held Michigan to six points. It came one week after a 19-15 loss to Ohio State.

Mallory: Grace in defeat one week, grit on the road the next. Full pageant wave.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hoover has thrown the most passes for Indiana in every game, and Lindsey has done the same for Minnesota, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Curt Cignetti was hired at Indiana on Nov. 30, 2023. In 2025, the Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship. This year's team allows only 12.0 points a game.

P.J. Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017, after coaching Western Michigan from 2013 to 2016. He played receiver at Northern Illinois and coached receivers for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. His defense is the strength this year, stingy against the throw and good on third down.

Tor: Coach Fleck rows the boat. We all row together.

Mallory: Coach Cignetti said it best: "It can be done." I have it on a pillow.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Becker and Hoover against a Minnesota defense that allows only 159.7 passing yards a game. On the other side, the Gophers need their big guys up front to open running room against an Indiana defense that allows very little on the ground. Minnesota won the two recent meetings in this series, 38-31 in 2018 and 35-14 in 2021, so the Gophers have some happy memories. Indiana wants to stay near the top of the Big Ten race.

What's happening on campus

A Halloween afternoon in Bloomington means cream and crimson costumes in the stands at Memorial Stadium, and a CBS crowd watching at home. Minnesota fans just finished Homecoming week in Minneapolis, so their voices may still be a little hoarse. Back home, the Gophers play at Huntington Bank Stadium, listed at 50,850 seats.

Tor: I'm dressing as Floyd of Rosedale. Bronze paint and everything.

Mallory: I'm dressing as Miss Congeniality. Wait, that's the sash. I'm giving it to you, Tor, with love.

Anything else fun and true

Minnesota started playing football in 1882 and has been in the Big Ten since the league began in 1896 as the Western Conference. The Gophers claim seven national championships. Indiana's 2025 team was the first to win 16 games without a loss since Yale in 1894, and quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman.

Tor: Whatever happens, Mallory, the cocoa's on me afterward. We'll say grace first.

Mallory: Deal, Tor. And keep the coat warm for me.

My call: Indiana Hoosiers 34, Minnesota Golden Gophers 11.

Footnotes and Fashion: No. 20 Northwestern Visits Oregon on Halloween

No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten) at Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Autzen Stadium, Eugene, Ore., Peacock.

Your hosts are Ezra Lindqvist, a Northwestern data journalist who footnotes his own jokes, and Nix Wyatt-Aldana, a Eugene sneaker-and-uniform designer who reviews jerseys and route trees with equal ferocity.

Nix: Welcome to Autzen, Ezra! Before we begin, I have to review your outfit.

Ezra: I was afraid of that.

Nix: Purple quarter-zip, pumpkin pin for Halloween. Seven out of ten. The pin is carrying you.

Ezra: Footnote: the pin was my mother's idea, and she will be thrilled.

Players to watch

Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 117 of 164 for 1,617 yards, 12 touchdowns and just one interception. Caleb Komolafe leads the rushers with 551 yards and five scores, and Griffin Wilde leads the receivers with 39 catches for 615 yards. Linebacker Braydon Brus leads the defense in both tackles, with 62, and sacks, with four.

For Oregon, Jordon Davison leads the rushers with 422 yards and seven touchdowns, and Dakorien Moore leads the receivers with 34 catches for 417 yards. Dylan Raiola threw the most passes last week, and Lanning has said Brock Thomas and Akili Smith Jr. are in the mix too. On defense, Matayo Uiagalelei has six sacks, and Koi Perich leads the team with 46 tackles.

Ezra: Chiles has one interception in seven games. I checked it three times.

Nix: Uiagalelei rushing the quarterback is pure runway, darling. Ten out of ten.

Ezra: I've already filed my formal correction to everyone who doubted us. It's eleven pages.

Oregon lost 21-10 at Illinois on Oct. 24. Raiola completed 27 of 41 for 246 yards, Davison ran 14 times for 92 yards and the Ducks' touchdown, and Dakorien Moore caught nine balls.

Nix: Honest review? Somebody tripped on the runway. We get back up, we fix the hem.

Moore suffered a concussion at USC on Sept. 26 and has missed three games since. Before the injury he was 69 of 99 for 926 yards and nine touchdowns. Raiola and Thomas have started the last three games. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and Chiles has thrown the most passes for Northwestern every week, so check the teams' pregame notes.

Nix: We miss Dante. Get well, kid. You're always on the team.

Lanning also made a change on his staff. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was dismissed Sunday, and assistant coach Jay Johnson will coordinate the offense. Lanning was hired on Dec. 11, 2021, and his 2024 team went 13-1 and 9-0 in the Big Ten, winning the league title in its first season.

David Braun became Northwestern's interim coach in 2023, was named the permanent head coach that November and was the consensus Big Ten Coach of the Year. His team runs the ball and protects it, with only two turnovers lost all season.

Oregon has played football since 1894, joined the Big Ten in 2024 and went 13-2 last season. Marcus Mariota became Oregon's first Heisman Trophy winner in 2014. Northwestern opened this season with two games at lakefront Martin Stadium, right on Lake Michigan, before moving into the new Ryan Field.

Trail Shoes and Double Scoops: Colorado State Visits Utah State on Halloween

Colorado State (3-4, 1-2 Pac-12) at Utah State (2-5, 1-2 Pac-12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Maverik Stadium, Logan, Utah, USA Net.

Your hosts are Ansel Rimrock, a Colorado State fan who spends his mornings on the foothill trails, and Hyrum Tolleson, a Utah State fan from a Cache Valley dairy who's been up before the sun since he was 8.

Hyrum: Well, hello there, neighbor, and welcome to Logan. Double scoop of Aggie Ice Cream?

Ansel: Hyrum, it's Halloween morning.

Hyrum: Exactly. It's a holiday. Ice cream is the treat, and nobody has to play a trick.

Ansel: Fair enough. Mountain air, thick defense, and one scoop. Just one.

Players to watch

Colorado State quarterback Hauss Hejny threw the most passes in the first two games and again last week. He's 71 of 104 for 952 yards, 13 touchdowns and two interceptions. K'saan Farrar threw the most in the four games in between. Mel Brown leads the rushers with 454 yards on just 52 carries, and RJ Vick leads the receivers with 24 catches for 367 yards. Linebacker Oumar Diomande leads the defense with 67 tackles.

Utah State quarterback Grady Brosterhous has thrown the most passes in six straight games. He's 99 of 178 for 1,120 yards, seven touchdowns and six interceptions. Javen Jacobs leads the rushers with 435 yards, and Eli Wood leads the receivers with 37 catches for 479 yards and five touchdowns. Safety Brevin Hamblin leads the defense with 58 tackles, and Jordan Pendleton has 2.5 sacks.

Ansel: Mel Brown runs like he's coming downhill on a switchback. Every carry.

Hyrum: Eli Wood is a fine young man. Catches everything, says thank you after.

What happened last week

Colorado State beat San Diego State 56-49 at home on Oct. 24. Hejny threw for 333 yards and three touchdowns, Durell Robinson ran for two scores, and Tommy Maher caught six balls for 108 yards and two touchdowns.

Ansel: A long climb with a big view at the top. I'll take it.

Utah State lost 20-17 at Texas State on Oct. 24, on Homecoming night in San Marcos. Brosterhous threw for 206 yards, and Anthony Garcia caught eight balls for 87 yards.

Hyrum: Three points. That one stung like a cold barn in January. We milk the cows and go again.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hejny threw the most passes for Colorado State last week, and Brosterhous has done it for Utah State in six straight games, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jim Mora was hired at Colorado State on Nov. 26, 2025, and this is his first season. His offense can move the ball and takes care of it, with only four turnovers all season. The defense is the work in progress, and Mora has kept his team swinging, as last week's shootout showed.

Bronco Mendenhall leads Utah State, with a hire date of Dec. 6, 2024. His Aggie defense has kept games close, including a 16-14 loss at Washington and a 17-16 win over Washington State. The offense is the piece he's still building.

Ansel: Coach Mora has been around. Calm on the switchbacks.

Hyrum: Coach Mendenhall works like a dairy farmer. Early mornings, no complaints.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Colorado State's run game against a Utah State defense that has been steady all season. Brown has been breaking long runs, and the Aggies' big guys up front need to keep him in front of them. On the other side, Brosterhous and Wood need to find the end zone against a Rams defense that has had a hard time. Utah State won five of the eight meetings from 2016 through 2025, but Colorado State won the last one, 42-37 in 2024.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Cache Valley, and Maverik Stadium, home since 1968, is listed at 25,513 seats. The field is named for Merlin Olsen, the Pro Football Hall of Famer who played at Utah State. This is Colorado State's first season in the Pac-12, and the Rams play their home games at Canvas Stadium, opened in 2017 and listed at 36,500.

Hyrum: I'm dressing as a dairy cow. Very traditional.

Ansel: I'm dressing as a trail marker. Follow me, folks.

Anything else fun and true

Utah State football started in 1892, one of the oldest programs in the western United States, and the Aggies have won 13 conference championships across four leagues, most recently in 2021, when they went 11-3. Colorado State spent 49 seasons, from 1968 to 2016, at Sonny Lubick Field at Hughes Stadium before moving to Canvas.

Hyrum: Whatever happens, Ansel, the ice cream's on me. We'll say grace first.

Ansel: Deal, Hyrum. Make it a double after all.

My call: Utah State Aggies 34, Colorado State Rams 27.

UTEP (1-6, 0-3 Mountain West) at North Dakota State (6-2, 3-2 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Fargodome, Fargo, N.D., MW+.

Your hosts are Neto Galindo, a UTEP fan and Sun Bowl ironworker's kid who grades effort by chile heat, and Inga Halvorsen, a North Dakota State fan and agricultural economist who has tracked every Bison title since she was a girl.

Inga: Oh, for cute, you made it to Fargo! Welcome, Neto.

Neto: Thanks, Inga. I brought green chile from El Paso. It's Halloween, so I figured I'd bring the scariest thing I own.

Inga: And I brought tater tot hotdish. I bring hotdish either way, hon.

Neto: Then let's make it Hatch-hot hotdish. Neighbors share.

Players to watch

North Dakota State quarterback Nathan Hayes has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 123 of 196 for 1,470 yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Myles Mitchell leads the rushers with 393 yards, and Jackson Williams leads the receivers with 32 catches for 503 yards. Linebacker Donovan Woolen leads the defense with 55 tackles, and Kelton McCaslin has four sacks.

For UTEP, Raymond Moore III has thrown the most passes the last two games and leads the team in rushing with 414 yards. EJ Colson Jr. threw the most in the first five games and leads in passing with 628 yards and seven touchdowns. Kam Thomas leads the receivers with 270 yards, linebacker Isaiah Bogerty leads the defense with 42 tackles, and Sterling Miles has 3.5 sacks.

Inga: Against Nevada, Jackson Williams caught a missed field goal in the end zone and ran it back 100 yards. That young man deserves extra hotdish.

Neto: Raymond Moore III runs like a five-alarm chile. Effort grade: Hatch-hot.

What happened last week

North Dakota State lost 21-16 at New Mexico on Oct. 24, on Homecoming weekend in Albuquerque. Hayes threw for 198 yards and two touchdowns, and Williams caught four balls for 71 yards. It was the first meeting on record between the schools.

Inga: Oh, yah, that's a tough one. I made a second hotdish on the bus.

UTEP had an open week. The Miners last played on Oct. 17, losing 24-11 to San José State at the Sun Bowl. Moore threw for 195 yards, and Thomas caught four balls for 96 yards.

Neto: A week off to rest the legs and sharpen the effort. We'll be fresh.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hayes has thrown the most passes for North Dakota State every week, and Moore has done it for UTEP the last two games, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Tim Polasek leads North Dakota State, with a hire date of Dec. 17, 2023. His team plays Bison football: run it, defend it, don't give it away. The Bison allow 12.5 points a game, they've taken the ball away 14 times, and they shut out Fordham 38-0 and Wyoming 28-0.

Scotty Walden leads UTEP, with a hire date of Dec. 4, 2023. His offense runs the ball on most plays, and his team's best day came Sept. 12, a 51-10 win over Texas Southern. The open week gave his staff extra time to prepare.

Inga: Coach Polasek is Fargo through and through. Practical, like a good snow shovel.

Neto: Coach Walden is building it brick by brick, like my dad on a Sun Bowl job site.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is North Dakota State's defense against Moore, who can hurt you with his legs. The Bison's big guys up front have been tough to run on all season. On the other side, Hayes wants a clean day after five interceptions in the two losses, and UTEP's defense will try to force him into more mistakes. This is the first meeting between these schools in our records from 2016 through 2025.

What's happening on campus

Halloween in Fargo means bundling up, and the Fargodome, opened in 1992 and listed at 18,700 seats, keeps everybody warm and loud inside. UTEP fans call the Sun Bowl home, built in 1963 and listed at 51,500, with the Sound of the Southwest band and mascot Paydirt Pete.

Neto: I'm dressing as Paydirt Pete. Pickaxe and all.

Inga: I'm dressing as a casserole dish. Very warm, very Fargo.

Anything else fun and true

North Dakota State has won 18 national championships, including 10 FCS titles between 2011 and 2024, and 39 conference championships. The Bison went 14-1, 12-3, 11-4, 14-2 and 12-1 in their last five Missouri Valley seasons. UTEP's fight song is "El Paso Fight."

Inga: Whatever happens, Neto, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Neto: Deal, Inga. Share the chile, and the hotdish.

Cafecito in Lynchburg: FIU Visits Liberty on Halloween

FIU (3-4, 1-2 Conference USA) at Liberty (6-1, 3-0 Conference USA). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Williams Stadium, Lynchburg, Va., CBSSN.

Your hosts are Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, an FIU fan from Sweetwater who learned football from her abuela with cafecito and dominoes, and Gideon Fairweather, a Lynchburg youth pastor who coaches middle-school football on the side.

Gideon: Welcome to Lynchburg, Lourdes! Game day here feels like a family reunion with a marching band.

Lourdes: Gracias, Gideon. I brought cafecito and my abuela's dominoes.

Gideon: Dominoes? On Halloween?

Lourdes: The dominoes are the players, the sugar packets are the defense. It's the scariest playbook in Miami.

Players to watch

Liberty quarterback Deshawn Purdie has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 80 of 133 for 1,226 yards and nine touchdowns, and he hasn't thrown an interception all season. Kam Davis leads the rushers with 583 yards and five scores, and Makai Jackson leads the receivers with 23 catches for 540 yards and five touchdowns. Linebacker Derrell Farrar leads the defense with 39 tackles, and Brenton Williams has three sacks.

FIU quarterback JJ Kohl has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 131 of 227 for 1,637 yards, 10 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Devonte Lyons leads the rushers with 383 yards, and Maguire Anderson leads the receivers with 36 catches for 568 yards. DeeJay Holmes Jr. has five sacks, and DeAndre Boykins leads the team with 37 tackles.

Gideon: Zero interceptions for Purdie. I preach a whole sermon on patience, and that young man is living it.

Lourdes: DeeJay Holmes Jr. gets to the quarterback like my abuela gets to the last pastelito. Fast.

What happened last week

Liberty won 34-6 at Kennesaw State on Thursday, Oct. 22. Purdie threw for 176 yards and a touchdown, and Davis ran for a score. Kennesaw State had won the last three meetings, so this one meant plenty.

Gideon: Grace and grit, Lourdes. Grace and grit.

FIU lost 26-23 to Middle Tennessee at home on Tuesday, Oct. 20, a "Paws at the Pit" night. Kohl threw three touchdowns, Lyons ran 19 times for 115 yards, and Kyle McNeal caught a scoring ball. The week before, the Panthers lost 27-24 at Jacksonville State.

Lourdes: Two three-point losses in a row. My abuela needed two coladas. Then she said, "Mija, next week."

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Purdie has thrown the most passes for Liberty every week, and Kohl has done the same for FIU, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jamey Chadwell has led Liberty since the 2023 season, after head coaching stops at North Greenville, Delta State, Charleston Southern and Coastal Carolina. His first Liberty team went 13-1. This year's Flames run the ball and play defense, allowing 14.0 points a game.

Willie Simmons is in his second year at FIU. In his first season, the Panthers went 7-6 and made their first bowl trip since 2019. Before that, he won a black college national championship and a SWAC title at Florida A&M in 2023. He played quarterback at Clemson and The Citadel.

Gideon: Coach Chadwell builds a team the way I build a youth group. Steady, with a lot of snacks.

Lourdes: Coach Simmons wins everywhere he goes. ¡Vamos!

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Davis and Liberty's big guys up front against an FIU defense that allows only 16.3 points a game. On the other side, Kohl needs to find Anderson against a Liberty defense that has been stingy all season. These teams have met four times since 2020. Liberty won three, but FIU won the most recent one, 34-27 last season.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween afternoon in Lynchburg, and Williams Stadium, built in 1989 and listed at 25,000, should be full of Flames fans, plus a costume or two. FIU's Pitbull Stadium, opened in 1995, is listed at 20,000, and its Homecoming is still to come later this fall.

Lourdes: I'm dressing as a domino. Double six. The best one.

Gideon: I'm dressing as a middle-school water bottle. That's what those kids care about most.

Anything else fun and true

Liberty moved from FCS to FBS and became a full member in 2019. In 2020 the Flames entered the AP poll for the first time, at No. 25, and they joined Conference USA in 2023. FIU shared the 2010 Sun Belt championship and plays Florida Atlantic every year in the Shula Bowl.

Gideon: Whatever happens, Lourdes, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Lourdes: Deal, Gideon. I'll bring the cafecito.

My call: Liberty Flames 27, Florida International Panthers 12.

Pearls and an Optimism Counter: Southern Miss Visits UL Monroe on Halloween

Southern Miss (2-5, 1-2 Sun Belt) at UL Monroe (1-6, 1-2 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Malone Stadium, Monroe, La., ESPN+.

Your hosts are Dee Broussard, a Southern Miss fan and former sorority president who calls everybody "sugar" and means it, and Darnell Vidrine, a UL Monroe fan and overnight Delta radio host who keeps an optimism counter running all season.

Darnell: Good evening, good morning, good whatever-time-it-is! Welcome to Monroe, Dee.

Dee: Thank you, sugar. Is that the famous optimism counter?

Darnell: Set to 100, like every week. But this week, Dee, I didn't have to reset it. We WON.

Dee: Well, bless it. Congratulations, Darnell. Truly.

Players to watch

Southern Miss quarterback Landry Lyddy has thrown the most passes in the last five games. He's 101 of 170 for 1,196 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions. Steven Robinson leads the rushers with 577 yards and eight scores, and Mario Sanders leads the receivers with 40 catches for 569 yards and five touchdowns. Linebacker Mathis Haygood leads the defense with 63 tackles, and Jameer Lewis has four sacks.

UL Monroe quarterback Aidan Armenta has thrown the most passes in the last four games. He's 96 of 153 for 1,121 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. Austin Carlisle, who threw the most passes in the second and third games, leads the team in rushing with 237 yards, and Marcellus Jackson leads the receivers with 32 catches. Linebacker Noah Flemmings leads the defense with 65 tackles, and Kevontay Wells has three sacks.

Dee: Steven Robinson runs like he's late for a formal. Eight touchdowns, sugar.

Darnell: Noah Flemmings has 65 tackles. I can FEEL it every time he hits somebody.

What happened last week

UL Monroe won its first game of the season, 21-14 at Troy on Oct. 24, on Troy's Military Appreciation day. Armenta went 13 of 22 for 147 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions.

Darnell: I KNEW IT! I may have sniffled on the air. Okay, I definitely sniffled.

Southern Miss beat Louisiana 35-31 on Homecoming at "The Rock" on Oct. 24. Jamarice Wilder ran 13 times for 154 yards and a touchdown, and Sanders caught six balls for 77 yards.

Dee: Homecoming win at home. To the top, y'all! I pointed skyward so hard I lost an earring.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Lyddy has thrown the most passes for Southern Miss in five straight games, and Armenta has done it for UL Monroe in four straight, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Blake Anderson is in his first season at Southern Miss, with a hire date of Dec. 11, 2025. His team throws it well and just got a big day from the run game, too. The defense is the work in progress, but the Golden Eagles found a way against Louisiana.

Bryant Vincent leads UL Monroe, with a hire date of Dec. 5, 2023. Two of his team's early losses were one-score games, 26-20 at UAB and 38-35 to SE Louisiana, and last week his defense held Troy to 14 points.

Dee: Coach Anderson walked in and got to work. I respect a man with a plan.

Darnell: Coach Vincent keeps the faith. He's a counter-reset kind of coach.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is the Southern Miss run game against a UL Monroe defense that has had a hard time stopping the run. Robinson and Wilder will test the Warhawks' big guys up front. On the other side, Armenta wants another clean day after throwing for 362 yards at South Alabama earlier this season. Southern Miss won four of the six meetings since 2017, including 49-21 last season, but UL Monroe won 38-21 in 2024.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Monroe, and Malone Stadium, opened in 1978 and listed at 27,617 seats, gets the home crowd back after last week's trip to Troy. Southern Miss fans just celebrated Homecoming at The Rock, which wears a new name this fall, Renasant Stadium. The nickname isn't going anywhere.

Dee: I'm dressing as a string of pearls. Elegant, timeless, a little bit sparkly.

Darnell: I'm dressing as a 2 a.m. radio show. Everybody's welcome to call in.

Anything else fun and true

UL Monroe football dates to 1931. The school's teams were the Northeast Louisiana Indians for a long stretch and became the Warhawks in 2006, and the program moved up to what is now FBS in 1994. Southern Miss went 7-6 last season, a lovely bounce back after a 1-11 year in 2024.

Darnell: Whatever happens, Dee, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Dee: Deal, sugar. I'll bring the sweet tea.

My call: Southern Miss Golden Eagles 32, UL Monroe Warhawks 26.
