Chili and Slalom Gates: No. 6 Utah Visits Cincinnati on Halloween

No. 6 Utah (7-0, 4-0 Big 12) at Cincinnati (5-2, 2-2 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:45 p.m. ET, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati, ESPN.

Your hosts are Aspen Mortensen, a Utah fan and former ski racer who reads defenses like slalom gates, and Lionel "Skyline" Abernathy, a Cincinnati engineering co-op kid who ranks everything in chili ways.

Skyline: Welcome to Nippert, Aspen! Two Saturdays, two top-10 visitors. That's a five-way schedule.

Aspen: Thanks, Skyline. I'll warn you now, there will be avalanche puns.

Skyline: I can handle puns. Can your defense handle Cole Tabb?

Aspen: Our defense eats gates for breakfast. Send it, no fear.

Players to watch

Utah quarterback Devon Dampier has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 136 of 198 for 1,616 yards, 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, and he ran for 150 yards and two scores last week. Wayshawn Parker leads the rushers with 644 yards and eight touchdowns, and Braden Pegan leads the receivers with 34 catches for 459 yards and six scores. Linebacker Trey Reynolds leads the defense with 44 tackles, and Karson Kaufusi has two sacks.

Cincinnati quarterback JC French IV has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 127 of 183 for 1,510 yards, 13 touchdowns and only two interceptions. Cole Tabb leads the rushers with 621 yards and nine scores on just 65 carries, and JV Gibson leads the receivers with 29 catches for 385 yards. Linebacker Jonathan Thompson leads the defense with 60 tackles, and Patrick Bauer has three and a half sacks.

Aspen: Dampier runs like he's on a fresh powder day. Nobody catches him.

Skyline: Nine touchdowns for Tabb on 65 carries. That's onions AND beans.

What happened last week

Utah beat Houston 21-13 at home on Oct. 24, the Utes' first win ever over the Cougars. Dampier threw for 204 yards and ran for 150 more with two touchdowns.

Aspen: Five losses to Houston, then finally a win. Every ski run has a bottom, and we made it to the lodge.

Cincinnati beat No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24 on Homecoming in front of a sold-out Nippert crowd. French threw four touchdowns, and Tabb ran 16 times for 173 yards and a score. It was only the third top-10 win in Nippert Stadium history.

Skyline: Five-way. Extra onions. I'm still smiling.

Injuries and availability

The official Big 12 availability report hasn't been posted yet. Utah coach Morgan Scalley said starting offensive lineman Kelvin Obot, who was hurt at Colorado and missed the Houston game, has no timetable and is getting a second opinion. Cincinnati coach Scott Satterfield said the team is close to getting starting nose tackle Josh Hough back after he missed last week, and starting center Taran Tyo, who left last week's game, likely won't have an answer until late in the week. Check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Morgan Scalley is in his first season as Utah's head coach after taking over in December 2025. He played defensive back for the Utes from 2001 to 2004, joined the staff in 2007 and spent 10 seasons as defensive coordinator. After the Colorado win he said, "It's not always pretty, but we did enough."

Scott Satterfield became Cincinnati's 43rd head coach on Dec. 5, 2022. His offense runs the ball well and almost never gives it away.

Aspen: Coach Scalley has been a Ute for a long time. He knows every gate on this course.

Skyline: Coach Satterfield has us at a five-way. I'm not downgrading anything this week.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Tabb and the Cincinnati big guys up front against a Utah defense that allows only 14.6 points a game. On the other side, Dampier and Parker face a Bearcats defense that just slowed down Texas Tech. These teams met for the first time last season, on Nov. 1 in Salt Lake City, where College GameDay was in town, and Utah won 45-14.

What's happening on campus

For the first time in program history, Cincinnati is hosting ranked opponents in back-to-back weeks, and it all happens on Halloween. Football has been played on the Nippert site since 1901, which Cincinnati calls the second-oldest playing site in college football.

Aspen: I'm dressing as an avalanche. Big, fast and loud.

Skyline: I'm dressing as a five-way. Onions and beans included.

Anything else fun and true

Utah football began in 1892 and has played on the current site of Rice-Eccles Stadium since 1927. The Utes have won two BCS bowls, the 2005 Fiesta Bowl and the 2009 Sugar Bowl. Cincinnati became the first team from outside the Power Five to make the College Football Playoff in the 2021 season, when the Bearcats played Alabama in the Cotton Bowl.

Skyline: Whatever happens, Aspen, chili's on me. We'll say grace first.

Aspen: Deal, Skyline. I'll bring the fry sauce.

My call: Utah Utes 33, Cincinnati Bearcats 25.

Virginia (4-4, 2-3 ACC) at No. 14 Wake Forest (6-1, 4-1 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:45 p.m. ET, Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, Winston-Salem, N.C., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Prescott Ashby-Lowell, a fourth-generation Wahoo in a game-day bow tie who refuses to say "campus," and Eloise Brightman-Rowe, a Wake Forest grad and debate-team darling who rolls the Quad and politely roasts bad tackling.

Eloise: Welcome to Winston-Salem, Prescott! Resolved: Wake Forest is the best place to spend Halloween.

Prescott: I'll accept the premise, Eloise, with one amendment. The Grounds are a close second.

Eloise: Two minutes for rebuttal.

Prescott: I only need one. Go 'Hoos.

Players to watch

Wake Forest quarterback Gio Lopez has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 140 of 207 for 1,947 yards, 17 touchdowns and just one interception. Carlos Hernandez leads the receivers with 49 catches for 720 yards and four scores, and Ty Clark III leads the rushers with 328 yards and four touchdowns. Linebacker Vincent Firenze leads the defense with 49 tackles, and Langston Hardy has five and a half sacks.

Virginia quarterback Beau Pribula has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 119 of 183 for 1,369 yards, 13 touchdowns and two interceptions. Jekail Middlebrook leads the rushers with 513 yards and four scores, and Da'Shawn Martin has five touchdown catches. Matthew Fobbs-White has four sacks, and cornerback Jacobie Henderson leads the team with 40 tackles.

Eloise: One interception all season. Gio Lopez would win any debate about ball security.

Prescott: Mr. Fobbs-White has four sacks. Mr. Jefferson would've charted every one.

What happened last week

Wake Forest had an open date. The Demon Deacons' last game was a 41-7 win at Cal on Oct. 17, when Lopez threw four touchdowns and Dominick Barry caught four balls for 102 yards and three scores. Their only loss this season came against Miami, 33-20.

Eloise: The open week was for rest, film and a little extra Quad rolling.

Virginia lost 19-16 to Duke at Scott Stadium on Friday, Oct. 23. Middlebrook ran 24 times for 117 yards and a touchdown, and John Rogers caught five balls for 65 yards.

Prescott: A close one. I straightened my bow tie and went home to think.

Injuries and availability

The official ACC availability report hasn't been posted yet. Virginia coach Tony Elliott said starting safety Brandyn Hillman and safety Ethan Minter are day-to-day, and he confirmed that Pribula remains the starting quarterback. Hernandez was banged up in the Cal game, and Wake Forest used the open week to heal, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jake Dickert leads Wake Forest, with a hire date of Dec. 18, 2024. His team scores 37.4 points a game, and the defense has 18 sacks. The Demon Deacons beat Louisville on the road and have won their last three ACC games by at least 24 points.

Tony Elliott has led Virginia since being hired Dec. 10, 2021. Before that he coached at Clemson from 2011 to 2021, finishing as associate head coach and offensive coordinator, and he won the 2017 Broyles Award as the top assistant in college football. He also played wide receiver at Clemson. Last season his Cavaliers went 11-3.

Eloise: Coach Dickert's team has won four straight since the Miami game. That's a winning argument.

Prescott: Coach Elliott built an 11-win season. I had it framed.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Lopez and Hernandez against a Virginia defense that allows 19.6 points a game. On the other side, Middlebrook and Virginia's big guys up front need to keep Hardy away from Pribula. Wake Forest won four of the five meetings since 2016, including 16-9 last season, but Virginia won a 31-30 thriller in 2024.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Winston-Salem, and Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, built in 1968 and listed at 31,500 seats, gets the Demon Deacons back after the open week. The Spirit of the Old Gold & Black will play "O' Here's to Wake Forest," and rolling the Quad is the tradition every Deacon fan shows visitors first.

Prescott: I'm dressing as Mr. Jefferson. Bow tie, of course.

Eloise: I'm dressing as a rolled tree. Very festive, very white.

Anything else fun and true

Virginia football started in 1887, and Scott Stadium sits next to the university's Academical Village, part of a World Heritage Site. In 1915 Virginia became the first Southern program to beat Yale, winning 10-0 at the Yale Bowl. Before Duke, all three of Virginia's losses came away from Scott Stadium.

Eloise: Whatever happens, Prescott, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Prescott: Splendid, Eloise. I'll bring the bagels.

My call: Wake Forest Demon Deacons 30, Virginia Cavaliers 19.

Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz is sketching a game-week roadmap on a whiteboard outside CEFCU Stadium when Paloma Begaye-Ortiz walks up holding two foil-wrapped burritos. "Red or green?" Paloma asks. Tessa studies them like a product spec. "Can I A/B test both?" Paloma laughs. "Both, Tessa. Always both."

New Mexico (6-1, 3-0 Mountain West) visits San José State (4-4, 2-2 Mountain West) Saturday at 4 p.m. ET on MW+ at CEFCU Stadium in San Jose. DraftKings has New Mexico Lobos −14.5 with a total of 42.5. My card: New Mexico Lobos −14.5, Over 42.5, and a final of New Mexico Lobos 31, San José State Spartans 15.

Paloma speaks for New Mexico. "We beat North Dakota State 21-16 last week, and Kiefer Sibley ran for 91 yards and a touchdown. Scottre Humphrey has nine rushing touchdowns, Brett Karhu has five sacks, and Mercury Swaim has 43 tackles. Our defense allows 11.3 points a game. Red or green? BOTH!"

Tessa speaks for San José State. "Rollback. We lost 28-13 at Nevada, and our quarterback spot is a work in progress. Daniel Rolovich got hurt early, and Luke Weaver came back late. Weaver has 11 touchdown throws. Carson Clark has 47 catches, Jayland McGlothen has six sacks and Dylan Lee has 71 tackles. And we've won the last four meetings."

Why New Mexico? Because the Lobos defend and run the ball. New Mexico allows 11.3 points a game, and its only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma. San José State scored 13 points at Nevada and 13 against Wyoming, and it's sorting out its quarterbacks. My final has the Lobos winning by 16.

The risk is the New Mexico passing game. Toa Fa'avae threw for 92 yards last week and 59 at Hawai'i, with interceptions in both, and the Lobos won those games 21-10 and 21-16. McGlothen can get after the quarterback, and the Spartans have won the last four meetings, including 35-28 last season. If New Mexico can't throw, this stays close.

Why the Over? New Mexico can score in a hurry: 38 against Central Michigan, 70 against Mercyhurst, 42 at New Mexico State and 61 against UTEP. The last five meetings between these teams finished 48-41, 32-21, 38-21, 52-24 and 35-28. My 31-15 adds up to 46, over 42.5.

Now the room. The Formula has New Mexico 31-15, sides with New Mexico, and likes the Over. Next Man Up has New Mexico 30-15, sides with New Mexico, and likes the Over. Follow The Money sits out both, since the spread and the total haven't budged. In The Trenches sits out: the New Mexico run game and the San José State run game each have a matchup they like, so they cancel out.

The Formula opened: "New Mexico's defense wins this by more than two scores."

Next Man Up agreed: "And the Lobos score enough for the Over."

Follow The Money shrugged: "Nothing moved. I'm watching."

Bottom of the card: a New Mexico defense that takes the ball away, a San José State team sorting out its quarterbacks and a Halloween crowd in San Jose. Give me the Lobos and the Over.

Balloons and Product Launches: New Mexico Visits San José State on Halloween

New Mexico (6-1, 3-0 Mountain West) at San José State (4-4, 2-2 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4 p.m. ET, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose, Calif., MW+.

Your hosts are Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, a New Mexico fan who flies a hot-air balloon in the Balloon Fiesta every October, and Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, a San José State fan and tech product lead who treats game week like a launch.

Tessa: Welcome to San Jose, Paloma! I've got the roadmap, the standup and the retro all scheduled.

Paloma: Thanks, Tessa. I brought green chile. Red, too. Both!

Tessa: Can I A/B test them?

Paloma: You can, but the answer is always both.

Players to watch

New Mexico quarterback Toa Fa'avae has thrown the most passes in the last six games. He's 49 of 87 for 790 yards, five touchdowns and four interceptions. Scottre Humphrey leads the rushers with 453 yards and nine scores, and tight end Cade Keith leads the receivers with 20 catches for 265 yards. Brett Karhu has five sacks, and linebacker Mercury Swaim leads the defense with 43 tackles.

San José State's Luke Weaver threw the most passes in each of the first six games and leads the team with 1,620 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions. Jabari Bates leads the rushers with 586 yards, and freshman Carson Clark leads the receivers with 47 catches for 551 yards and five scores. Jayland McGlothen has six sacks, and linebacker Dylan Lee leads the team with 71 tackles.

Paloma: Humphrey runs like a balloon catching a thermal. Up and up.

Tessa: Carson Clark has 47 catches as a freshman. That's a feature I'd demo to anybody.

What happened last week

New Mexico beat North Dakota State 21-16 on Homecoming in Albuquerque on Oct. 24, during a Pack Week that honored the Route 66 centennial. Kiefer Sibley ran 13 times for 91 yards and a touchdown, and Keith caught five balls.

Paloma: Too much heat for a while, then we soared. Red or green? BOTH!

San José State lost 28-13 at Nevada on Oct. 24. Viliami Teu ran for a touchdown, and Dominique McKenzie caught two balls for 60 yards.

Tessa: Rollback. I opened a bug ticket on the bus ride home.

Injuries and availability

No official Mountain West availability report has been posted for this game yet. San José State's quarterback spot is the big question. Freshman Daniel Rolovich started the last two games, but he was hurt in the first quarter at Nevada, and Weaver came back in the fourth quarter to lead a late scoring drive. Who starts Saturday hasn't been announced, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jason Eck leads New Mexico, with a hire date of Dec. 16, 2024. His defense allows 11.3 points a game and had taken the ball away 21 times through six games. The Lobos' only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma.

Ken Niumatalolo was hired at San José State on Jan. 21, 2024. Before the UTEP game he went with Rolovich because, as he put it, the staff "just felt like we needed a spark." He also said of the freshman, "He's got a big arm. He's big and strong and can run. He's not afraid."

Paloma: Coach Eck builds a defense the way I pack a balloon basket. Nothing loose.

Tessa: Coach Niumatalolo ships fixes fast. I respect that.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Humphrey and the New Mexico big guys up front against a Spartans defense that allows 22.5 points a game. On the other side, whoever plays quarterback for San José State has to find Clark against a Lobos defense that loves taking the ball away. San José State has won the last four meetings, including 35-28 last season, and the Spartans are looking for an eighth straight home win over the Lobos.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in San Jose, and San José State is hosting Trick or Treat with the Spartans and Youth Spirit Day. Families can trick-or-treat before kickoff, and local youth dance and cheer groups will perform on the field at halftime. CEFCU Stadium opened in 1933 as Spartan Stadium and is listed at 30,456 seats.

Paloma: I'm dressing as a hot-air balloon. Cherry and silver, of course.

Tessa: I'm dressing as a software update. Nobody knows when I'll arrive.

Anything else fun and true

San José State first played a regular season in 1898, and the Spartans count Pro Football Hall of Famers Bill Walsh and Dick Vermeil among their alumni. New Mexico's University Stadium opened in 1960, and last season the Lobos went 9-4.

Tessa: Whatever happens, Paloma, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Paloma: Deal, Tessa. I'll bring the green chile.

My call: New Mexico Lobos 31, San José State Spartans 15.

Snowboards and Storyboards: Nevada Visits No. 7 UCLA on Halloween

Nevada (3-4, 2-2 Mountain West) at No. 7 UCLA (7-0, 5-0 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4:15 p.m. ET, Rose Bowl, Pasadena, Calif., BTN.

Your hosts are Ridge Corbell, a Nevada fan, Tahoe ski patroller and snowboarder whose motto is "Send It," and Kenzie Rhee, a UCLA fan and Westwood film-school producer who storyboards every drive.

Kenzie: Welcome to Pasadena, Ridge! Sunshine, mountains in the distance and an unbeaten team. I'd greenlight it.

Ridge: Thanks, Kenzie. Those mountains have no snow on them, but I'll allow it.

Kenzie: This week's logline: "Mountain team visits the movie set."

Ridge: And the mountain team sends it. Strap in.

Players to watch

UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach has thrown the most passes in the last two games. He went 22 of 33 for 264 yards in his first start against Wisconsin and 18 of 31 for 198 yards and a touchdown against Michigan State. Wayne Knight leads the rushers with 627 yards and 12 touchdowns, and Semaj Morgan leads the receivers with 31 catches for 383 yards. Linebacker Sammy Omosigho has five and a half sacks, and Jalen Woods leads the defense with 59 tackles.

Nevada's Luke Duncan threw the most passes last week, going 18 of 29 for 178 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers. Carter Jones leads the team with 654 passing yards. Nevada's top running back has 582 yards and five touchdowns, and Gary Givens III leads the receivers with 19 catches for 305 yards. Linebacker EJ Smith leads the defense with 76 tackles, and Dylan LaBarbera has four sacks.

Kenzie: Wayne Knight has 12 rushing touchdowns. That's a franchise, darling.

Ridge: EJ Smith has 76 tackles. That dude never stops carving.

What happened last week

UCLA beat Michigan State 28-10 on Homecoming at the Rose Bowl, where the Bruins honored their 1966 Rose Bowl team. Anthony Woods ran 14 times for 112 yards and a touchdown, and Brian Rowe Jr. caught three balls for 74 yards and a score.

Kenzie: Homecoming, a callback to 1966 and a win. And. scene.

Nevada beat San José State 28-13 on Homecoming at Mackay Stadium. Duncan threw two touchdowns, and Marshaun Brown caught five balls for 52 yards and a score.

Ridge: Sick! I mimed a backflip. Nobody got hurt.

Injuries and availability

The official availability reports haven't been posted yet. UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is out for the season after a knee injury in the Oregon game. For Nevada, starting quarterback Carter Jones (arm) and AJ Bianco (ankle) both missed last week, and coach Jeff Choate said it was too early to say who will start. Check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Bob Chesney is in his first season at UCLA, with a hire date of Dec. 6, 2025. He's a Dickinson College graduate who was head coach at Salve Regina, Assumption, Holy Cross and James Madison, and at Holy Cross he won five straight Patriot League titles. He's the first UCLA coach to begin his tenure 6-0, and the Bruins have kept on winning.

Jeff Choate was hired at Nevada on Dec. 4, 2023. This week he said his goal is to keep the game close: "Let's just drag this thing into deep water and find out who's gonna swim in the fourth quarter."

Kenzie: Coach Chesney walked onto the set and made a blockbuster. Breakout debut.

Ridge: Coach Choate wants deep water. I'm a snow guy, but I'm in.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Nevada's run game against a UCLA defense that allows 15.3 points a game. Duncan, if he plays, has a story all his own: he spent his first three college seasons at UCLA. On the other side, Knight and UCLA's big guys up front face a Nevada defense that has had trouble stopping the run. This is just the 10th time Nevada has played a top-10 team since moving up to the top level of college football.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween at the Rose Bowl, listed at 88,565 seats, one week after UCLA's Homecoming. Back in Reno, Nevada fans just celebrated Homecoming Week and the football program's 130th birthday, since the team was founded on Oct. 24, 1896, as the Sagebrushers.

Kenzie: I'm dressing as a director's chair. Very supportive.

Ridge: I'm dressing as a snowboard. Pasadena needs a little winter.

Anything else fun and true

UCLA has been ranked in the AP top 10 at least once in every decade since the poll began in the 1930s, and the Bruins won the 1954 Coaches' Poll national title under Red Sanders. Nevada's Mackay Stadium field sits 4,610 feet above sea level, and Chris Ault, Frank Hawkins and Buck Shaw are in the College Football Hall of Fame.

Ridge: Whatever happens, Kenzie, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Kenzie: Deal, darling. I'll bring dessert.

My call: UCLA Bruins 34, Nevada Wolf Pack 14.

display.story_text:
Hank Palouse drives a combine and keeps a shoebox of game tapes in the cab. Kai Delgado-Sorensen surfs Ocean Beach most mornings. Two teams that need a win, and two new quarterbacks.

Washington State (1-7) at San Diego State (3-5), Saturday at 7:00 p.m. ET on CBSSN at Snapdragon Stadium in San Diego. It's a Pac-12 game. DraftKings has San Diego State Aztecs −2.5 with a total of 48.5. Action Network opened San Diego State −2.5 with a total of 48.5. My card: Washington State Cougars +2.5, Over 48.5, and a final of San Diego State Aztecs 27, Washington State Cougars 25.

Hank speaks for Washington State. "Cougs never quit. We lost 16-17 at Utah State, and that tape's still in my shoebox. Owen Eshelman threw for 289 yards and two scores at Oregon State in his first extended look. Branden Ganashamoorthy has 30 catches. Kirby Moore says Darrius Clemons and Jeremiah Bernard are day-to-day. Wave the flag."

Kai speaks for San Diego State. "Brah, Stone Saunders threw for 369 yards at Colorado State in his first college start. Jaylon Hawkins caught six for 164. We still lost 49-56, because our defense gave up 56. Sean Lewis named Stone the starter again. Sione Hala has 83 tackles. Gnarly honesty: we need this one."

Here is the part that matters. San Diego State allows 36.1 points a game. It gave up 66 at Oregon State and 56 at Colorado State. Washington State scores only 18.9, but it doesn't need a big night to keep this close. The Cougars allow 27.6, and they have lost by one point already this year.

Why Washington State? In The Trenches likes the Cougars. San Diego State runs for 4.3 yards a carry against a Washington State defense that allows 5.0, which is below what the Aztecs should get. The Formula has a one-point game, 28-27. A two-and-a-half point spread in a coin-flip game is worth taking.

The worry is real. Washington State is still looking for its first win over an FBS team this season. Eshelman ran 23 times for 33 yards against Boise State and threw no touchdowns. Next Man Up has San Diego State 25-22, a three-point final that would beat me by a half point.

Why the Over/Under? San Diego State's last game had one hundred five points. The Formula has 55 and likes the Over. Next Man Up has 47. Follow The Money has nothing because nothing moved. Saunders and Hawkins can make plays, and this Aztec defense gives up points. My 27-25 adds up to 52, three and a half over the over/under 48.5.

Now the room. The Formula has San Diego State 28-27 and likes the Over. Next Man Up has San Diego State 25-22. Follow The Money has no side and no total. In The Trenches likes Washington State. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

The Formula: "One point either way. Take the points."

Next Man Up: "No official report. Saunders and Eshelman are both new."

In The Trenches: "The Aztecs haven't run it well. The Cougars can hold up."

Bottom of the card: a late field goal decides it, and the Cougars stay inside the number. Kai trades Hank a fish taco for a look at the shoebox.

San Diego State Aztecs 27, Washington State Cougars 25. Washington State Cougars cover the 2.5. Over 48.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Cougars and Aztecs Meet Under the San Diego Lights

Washington State (1-7, 0-4 Pac-12) at San Diego State (3-5, 2-2 Pac-12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:00 p.m. ET (4:00 p.m. Pacific), Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego, CBSSN.

Your hosts are Hank Palouse, a Washington State fan who drives a combine and keeps a shoebox of game tapes in the cab, and Kai Delgado-Sorensen, a San Diego State fan who surfs Ocean Beach most mornings.

Kai: Welcome to sunshine, Hank. You can leave the combine at home.

Hank: Brought the shoebox, though. Cougs never quit.

Players to watch

Washington State quarterback Owen Eshelman has started the last two games. Caden Pinnick, who started the first six, has thrown for 952 yards. Wide receiver Branden Ganashamoorthy leads the team with 30 catches for 401 yards and three touchdowns, and Kirby Vorhees has 275 rushing yards. On defense, linebacker Keith Brown has 60 tackles, and defensive tackle Jirah Leaupepetele has 2.5 sacks.

San Diego State quarterback Stone Saunders, a redshirt freshman and Kentucky transfer, gets his second straight start. Running back Javion Kinnard leads the team with 526 rushing yards. Wide receiver Jaylon Hawkins has 322 receiving yards and three touchdowns. Linebacker Sione Hala has 83 tackles, and linebacker Djibril Rahman has 3.5 sacks.

Kai: Hala's in on every play. That's a surfer who never gets out of the water.

What happened last week

Washington State lost 31-10 at home to Boise State. Eshelman completed 21 throws for 191 yards and ran the ball 23 times. Ganashamoorthy and Daniel Blood played all 76 snaps on offense.

San Diego State lost 56-49 at Colorado State in a wild one. The 105 combined points were the most in a game in San Diego State's Division I history. Saunders went 23 of 33 for 369 yards and two touchdowns in his first college start. Hawkins caught six balls for a career-high 164 yards and scored a touchdown for the fifth straight game. Lucky Sutton ran for 98 yards and two scores, and Kinnard added two more on just 10 carries.

Hank: One hundred sixty-four yards for Hawkins. That one's going in the shoebox, even if he's not ours.

Injuries and availability

No official Pac-12 availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Coach Kirby Moore said wide receiver Darrius Clemons (ankle) and safety Jeremiah Bernard (shoulder) are day-to-day and set to return to practice this week. For San Diego State, Jayden Denegal remains day-to-day.

What the coaches are up to

Moore is in his first season at Washington State. He wants sharper practices this week. "We talk about deliberate practice," he said. "That really starts with bringing great energy, having verbal combat, doing your assignment, making sure you're not thinking out there, that you're just reacting."

Sean Lewis is in his third season at San Diego State. He named Saunders the starter on Monday. "Stone will start this week," Lewis said. "So, he'll get the bulk of the one reps as we go forward."

Kai: Clear call from the coach. Gnarly.

Player storylines

Saunders came into his first start with just 15 career throws. His 369 yards were the most ever by an Aztec quarterback making his first start on the road, going back to 1969. He also became the first Aztec to throw for 300 yards since Jalen Mayden in the 2022 Hawai'i Bowl.

Ganashamoorthy has played 503 snaps this season, the most of any wide receiver in the Pac-12. Washington State's only win so far came 48-7 over Duquesne, and the Cougars lost 17-16 at Utah State. They're looking for their first win over an FBS team.

Hank: One-point loss. I've watched it twice. Still hurts.

What's happening on campus

Snapdragon Stadium opened in 2022 and seats 35,000. San Diego State began playing football in 1921 and has won 21 conference championships.

Washington State is in Pullman, where the first Cougar team took the field in 1894. Home is Martin Stadium, which opened in 1972 on ground that dates back to 1892, when it was called Soldier Field.

Anything else fun and true

The Aztecs went 9-4 last year and are trying to get to a bowl game for a second straight season. They have won two close home games this year, 31-29 over Texas State and 26-23 over Fresno State.

Hank: Ganashamoorthy, five hundred and three snaps. That young man has earned a nap.

Kai: Bring him to the beach after, Hank. Respect.

My call: San Diego State Aztecs 27, Washington State Cougars 25.

Mississippi State (4-3) at Texas (5-2), Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin. It's an SEC game. DraftKings has Texas Longhorns −20.5 with a total of 50.5. But Fluff Bothwell ran 17 times for 111 yards against Oklahoma, and Anthony Evans III has 53 catches. Parker Puckett has the job now. One ring of the cowbell for him."

Caro speaks for Texas. "Darling, we beat Ole Miss 34-27, and Raleek Brown ran 23 times for 157 yards. Colin Simmons has 10.5 sacks, but he is an asset under repair with a high ankle sprain. Our defense played well without him. Still, we lost 24-27 to Oklahoma and 24-27 to Florida. We don't win big very often."

Here is the part that matters. Texas has not been a blowout team. It beat Ohio State 24-23, Tennessee 20-17 and Ole Miss 34-27. Only Texas State and UTSA were blowouts, 59-7 and 30-6. The offense can stall, and Arch Manning has seven interceptions. Twenty and a half is a lot to ask of this team.

Bothwell is the plan. Lebby's offense still scored 15 against Oklahoma, all after halftime, and last year the Bulldogs lost only 38-45 to Texas.

display.fanatic_story:
Halloween Night in Austin: Mississippi State Visits Texas

Mississippi State (4-3, 2-3 SEC) at No. 11 Texas (5-2, 2-2 SEC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 p.m. Central), DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, Texas, ESPN.

Your hosts are Wade Pettus, a poultry-science grad who charts Air Raid concepts on feed-store receipts and trusts his cowbell on third down, and Caro Whitfield, a Texas fan, former rodeo queen and ex-consultant who values players like assets.

Caro: Welcome to Austin, darling. Hook 'em.

Wade: Thank you, ma'am. I'll ring once for you. Politely. (ding.)

Players to watch

Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor was 104 of 159 for 1,460 yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions, but he is out for the season. Parker Puckett takes over. Running back Fluff Bothwell has 514 yards and three touchdowns, and wide receiver Anthony Evans III leads the team with 53 catches for 647 yards. On defense, linebacker Tyler Lockhart has 48 tackles, and Jaray Bledsoe has 2.5 sacks.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning is 124 of 196 for 1,507 yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Running back Raleek Brown has 422 yards and five touchdowns. Wide receiver Ryan Wingo has 33 catches for 456 yards and four touchdowns. On defense, Colin Simmons has 10.5 sacks, and Jelani McDonald has 54 tackles.

Caro: Ten and a half sacks. Darling, that is a premium asset.

What happened last week

Mississippi State lost 23-15 to Oklahoma at home. Taylor started but left in the first half. Puckett went 17 of 24 for 158 yards and a touchdown, Bothwell ran for 111 yards, and Sanfrisco Magee had three catches for 65 yards and a touchdown.

Texas beat Ole Miss 34-27. Brown ran 23 times for 157 yards, and Wingo caught seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown. Manning threw for 212 yards.

Wade: One hundred fifty-seven for Brown. My cowbell is processing it quietly.

Injuries and availability

No official SEC availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Mississippi State announced that Taylor will miss the rest of the season with a foot injury that needs surgery, and he is expected to make a full recovery. "Missing the rest of this season is hard to accept, but I know God has a plan," Taylor said. For Texas, Simmons hurt his ankle against Florida and missed the Ole Miss game.

Caro: Praying for a full recovery for both of those young men.

What the coaches are up to

Jeff Lebby is in his third season at Mississippi State. "Nobody wants to be on that field more than Kamario," he said. "He's the ultimate teammate and competitor." Lebby is also weighing Puckett and AJ Swann at quarterback.

Steve Sarkisian is in his sixth season at Texas. He loved how his defense played without Simmons. "Nobody was just waiting for Colin to make a play," he said. "It was all 11 guys playing really well collectively together." He also said, "Believe me, we want Colin back as bad as anybody else."

Player storylines

Taylor had huge games in wins over Minnesota, South Carolina and Missouri, and he says he is all in with his teammates. "Starkville is home," he said. Puckett now gets his chance. For Texas, McDonald played his best game of the year against Ole Miss, according to Sarkisian Brown carried the load with 23 carries and will try to do it again.

What's happening on campus

DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium opened in 1924 and is listed at 100,119 seats. Texas began playing football in 1893 and claims national titles from 1963, 1969, 1970 and 2005.

Mississippi State plays at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field, the second-oldest stadium in FBS, dating to 1914, with room for 61,337. The Bulldogs won the SEC championship in 1941, and their fans bring the cowbells everywhere.

Anything else fun and true

These teams have met the last two years. Texas won 35-13 in 2024 and 45-38 in 2025.

Mississippi State started this season 4-0, with wins over UL Monroe, at Minnesota, at South Carolina and over Missouri. After Saturday, the Bulldogs play three straight home games.

Wade: I wrote Puckett's first road start on a receipt. I'm keeping it.

Caro: Keep it, darling. Receipts are good business. Hook 'em.

My call: Texas Longhorns 35, Mississippi State Bulldogs 19.

Wendell Quist charts the flight of every punt, and lately the Georgia Tech numbers have only gone one direction. Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci has his homemade whistle and a Pitt team that needs a win just as badly. Halloween night on the North Shore.

Georgia Tech (2-5) at Pittsburgh (5-3), Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. It's an ACC game. DraftKings has Pittsburgh Panthers −7.5 with a total of 54.5. My card: Pittsburgh Panthers −7.5, Over 54.5, and a final of Pittsburgh Panthers 36, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 21.

Wendell speaks for Georgia Tech. "Alberto Mendoza is 153 of 215 for 1,714 yards. That's a good arc. The trouble is the other side. Boston College ran for three hundred ninety-nine yards on us in a 27-49 loss. Coach Brent Key called it embarrassing and said, 'It's on coaching, so that's on me.'"

Yinz speaks for Pitt. "How's it goin', n'at? We lost Mason Heintschel for the season at Virginia Tech, and we've lost three since. But Holden Geriner is our guy now, Coach Narduzzi said so. Cataurus Hicks caught five for 149 at Miami. And Georgia Tech can't stop the run. That's a whole lotta yinz."

Here is the part that matters. With Heintschel, Pitt started 5-0, beating Miami (Ohio) 59-14, UCF 12-7, Syracuse 27-13 and Bucknell 59-0 at home and winning 35-33 at Virginia Tech. The losses since came against North Carolina, at Boston College and at Miami. Georgia Tech allows 30.3 points a game. Its last two were losses of 24-34 at Virginia Tech and 27-49 at home. The Yellow Jackets have a long list of injured players, and their best run defender, Tawfiq Thomas, was out against Boston College.

Why Pitt? The Formula and Next Man Up both like the Panthers. Pitt's freshman back Damon Ferguson Jr. has 477 yards, and the Panthers have run it well in ACC play. Geriner was steadier at Miami, 18 of 32 for 268 yards. That defense is hurting.

The worry is In The Trenches, which likes Georgia Tech. Pitt has given up some points lately, and without Heintschel the offense has been uneven. Georgia Tech beat Duke 28-25, so this group can still play.

Why the Over/Under? Georgia Tech allows 30.3 a game and scores 26.7. Pitt scores 31.6. The Formula has 55, Next Man Up has 58, and Follow The Money likes the Over because the total moved from 52.5 to 54.5. My 36-21 adds up to 57, two and a half over the over/under 54.5.

Now the room. The Formula has Pittsburgh 33-22 and likes Pitt and the Over. Next Man Up has Pittsburgh 38-20 and likes Pitt and the Over. Follow The Money has no side and likes the Over. In The Trenches likes Georgia Tech and has no total. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up: "No official report yet. Georgia Tech's injury list is long."

The Formula: "Thirty-three to twenty-two. Pitt clears it."

Follow The Money: "The total climbed two points. I go with it."

Bottom of the card: Pitt runs the ball, Geriner keeps it clean, and the slide ends at home. Yinz blows the whistle. Wendell recalculates.

Pittsburgh Panthers 36, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 21. Pittsburgh Panthers cover the 7.5. Over 54.5.

Halloween Night on the North Shore: Georgia Tech Visits Pitt

Georgia Tech (2-5, 1-3 ACC) at Pittsburgh (5-3, 2-3 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:30 p.m. ET, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh, ESPN2.

Your hosts are Wendell Quist, a Georgia Tech aerospace engineer who models the trajectory of every punt, and Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci, a steel-town linebacker who grades every tackle from "yinz" to "yikes" with a homemade whistle.

Yinz: How's it goin', n'at? Welcome to Pittsburgh, Wendell.

Wendell: Thank you, Yinz. I brought my calculator and a warm coat.

Players to watch

Georgia Tech quarterback Alberto Mendoza is 153 of 215 for 1,714 yards, 10 touchdowns and six interceptions. Running back Justice Haynes has 515 yards and four touchdowns, and wide receiver Jordan Allen leads the team with 42 catches for 517 yards. On defense, safety Tae Harris has 45 tackles, and Noah Carter has three sacks.

Pitt's season leader at quarterback is Mason Heintschel, with 1,304 yards, 14 touchdowns and one interception, but he is out for the year. Holden Geriner is the starter now. Running back Damon Ferguson Jr., a freshman, has 477 yards and four touchdowns. Wide receiver Cataurus Hicks has 31 catches for 649 yards and five touchdowns. On defense, Cruce Brookins has 55 tackles, and Jaeden Moore has 4.5 sacks.

Yinz: Brookins with 55 tackles. That's a whole lotta yinz.

What happened last week

Georgia Tech lost 49-27 at home to Boston College. Mendoza threw for 186 yards and a touchdown, Haynes ran for a score, and Dalen Penson had a career day with five catches for 88 yards and a touchdown. Boston College ran for 399 yards.

Pitt lost 52-23 at No. 1 Miami. Geriner went 18 of 32 for 268 yards and a touchdown, and Hicks caught five passes for 149 yards and a score. Ferguson ran for a touchdown too.

Wendell: One hundred forty-nine yards for Hicks. That's a long flight path.

Injuries and availability

The official ACC availability report had not been posted as of Tuesday. Pitt coach Pat Narduzzi announced in early October that Heintschel was injured at Virginia Tech and will miss the rest of the season. "We're heartbroken for Mason, but he's a resilient young man," Narduzzi said. Pitt running back Ja'Kyrian Turner was listed out for the Miami game. Georgia Tech has been hit hard by injuries; Carter, defensive tackle Tawfiq Thomas, cornerback Daiquan White and safety Savion Riley were all listed out for the Boston College game.

Yinz: Prayers for everybody on that list, from both sides.

What the coaches are up to

Brent Key has led Georgia Tech since 2022. After the Boston College game he took the blame. "It's on coaching, so that's on me. I'll take full responsibility," he said. He also told his team, "I want to play. I want to compete."

Narduzzi has led Pitt since December 2014. He named Geriner his starter after the Miami game. Earlier this season he said, "We have a team that can win an ACC championship with Mason or without Mason."

Player storylines

Geriner is a fifth-year player who has waited a long time for this chance, and he looked steadier at Miami. Ferguson is a freshman who has become Pitt's top runner, and veteran La'Vell Wright adds four rushing touchdowns of his own. For Georgia Tech, Mendoza threw for 335 yards at Virginia Tech two weeks ago, and Penson is coming off his best game.

What's happening on campus

Pitt plays at Acrisure Stadium on the North Shore, listed at 68,400. Pitt won the 1976 national title, when Tony Dorsett won the Heisman Trophy, and won its first ACC title in 2021.

Georgia Tech plays at Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field in Midtown Atlanta and claims national titles from 1917, 1928 and 1990.

Anything else fun and true

Last year Pitt won 42-28 in Atlanta in a night game with a lot riding on it. Georgia Tech won the 2022 meeting 26-21.

Georgia Tech's best win this season was 28-25 over Duke, which was unbeaten at the time.

Wendell: I ran the numbers on a Halloween comeback. The curve points up.

Yinz: My whistle says "yinz" tonight, Wendell. Happy Halloween.

My call: Pittsburgh Panthers 36, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 21.

Javi "The Breeze" Castillo is scouting Chapel Hill in linen and sunglasses. Ainsley Pemberton, former debutante and kinesiology PhD, has already offered him a sweater. The No. 1 team in the country comes to Kenan Stadium on Halloween night.

Miami (7-0) at North Carolina (4-3), Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill. It's an ACC game. DraftKings has Miami Hurricanes −14.5 with a total of 52.5. Action Network opened Miami −14.5 with a total of 50.5. My card: Miami Hurricanes −14.5, Over 52.5, and a final of Miami Hurricanes 35, North Carolina Tar Heels 20.

Javi speaks for Miami. "It's all about the U, baby! Darian Mensah has 22 touchdown passes and one interception. Malachi Toney caught 16 balls for 194 yards and three scores against Pitt. Even Bill Belichick says he can't find a weak point in Toney's game. Number one in the sun, Canes get it done."

Ainsley speaks for North Carolina. "Darling, we lost 30-31 to Syracuse in overtime, and it stung. Billy Edwards Jr. opened that game with eleven straight completions. Xavier Lewis has 7 sacks and Derek McDonald has 71 tackles. We won at Pitt and at Duke. We know how to keep a game close."

Here is the part that matters. Miami scores 49.0 points a game and has not been held under 33. North Carolina scores 24.4. The Tar Heels kicked three field goals against Syracuse, and Jordan Shipp said they have to turn those into touchdowns. Against this defense, field goals won't keep pace.

Why Miami? The Formula and Next Man Up both have Miami 35-20, a 15-point final. That's only a half point past the spread, so neither card gets excited, and Follow The Money sees no move on the side. I'll take the Canes anyway. Miami won at Clemson 41-13, where Carolina lost 20-28, and Mensah has thrown one interception all year.

The worry is the Belichick factor. Carolina allows only 20.9 a game, and Belichick will build a plan for Toney. In The Trenches shows a Carolina run game at 3.9 yards a carry against a Miami defense that allows 2.4, but Miami runs for 5.6 against a defense that allows 3.9. Those cancel out. A slow, careful game could land the Heels inside two scores.

Why the Over/Under? The Formula has 55 and Next Man Up has 55. Follow The Money likes the Over after the total climbed from 50.5 to 52.5. Miami scored 52 against Pitt and 43 against Florida State. My 35-20 adds up to 55, two and a half over the over/under 52.5.

Now the room. The Formula has Miami 35-20 and no strong feeling on either side or total. Next Man Up has Miami 35-20 and likes the Over. Follow The Money has no side and likes the Over. In The Trenches has nothing this week. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up: "No official report. Mensah and Toney are the whole show."

Follow The Money: "Two points up on the total. I go with the move."

In The Trenches: "Both run games point in different directions."

Bottom of the card: Miami pulls away late. Javi offers Ainsley a cafecito. She offers him the sweater again.

display.fanatic_story:
No. 1 Comes to Chapel Hill: Miami Visits North Carolina

No. 1 Miami (7-0, 5-0 ACC) at North Carolina (4-3, 2-2 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:30 p.m. ET, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, ABC.

Your hosts are Javi "The Breeze" Castillo, a former Miami defensive back who scouts in linen and sunglasses, and Ainsley Pemberton, a North Carolina fan, former debutante and kinesiology PhD.

Javi: It's all about the U, baby! Number one in the sun, Canes get it done!

Ainsley: Welcome to Chapel Hill, darling. Do you need a sweater?

Players to watch

Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has completed 166 of 204 throws for 2,151 yards, 22 touchdowns and just one interception. Wide receiver Malachi Toney has 66 catches for 952 yards and 11 touchdowns. Running back Javian Mallory has 444 yards and seven touchdowns on only 59 carries. On defense, Marquise Lightfoot has five sacks, and linebacker Mohamed Toure has 35 tackles.

North Carolina quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. has thrown for 1,531 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions. Wide receiver Jordan Shipp has 41 catches for 543 yards. Benjamin Hall leads the running backs with 283 yards. On defense, Xavier Lewis has seven sacks, and linebacker Derek McDonald has 71 tackles.

Javi: Toney in the end zone, mi amigo, that's a done zone!

What happened last week

Miami beat Pittsburgh 52-23. Mensah went 31 of 37 for 387 yards and four touchdowns, and Toney caught 16 balls for 194 yards and three scores. Mallory ran for two touchdowns.

North Carolina lost 31-30 to Syracuse in overtime at Kenan Stadium. Edwards opened the game with 11 straight completions and finished with season highs of 27 completions and 271 yards. Shipp had eight catches for 102 yards and a touchdown, and Demon June ran 25 yards for the team's longest rushing score of the year. McDonald, a Syracuse transfer facing his old team, made a career-high 16 tackles.

Ainsley: Sixteen tackles against his old school, darling. That's good manners and good football.

Injuries and availability

No official ACC availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Mensah and Toney have no reported injury concerns.

What the coaches are up to

Mario Cristobal is in his fifth season at Miami. Last season the Canes reached the national championship game, losing 27-21 to Indiana on Jan. 19, 2026.

Bill Belichick is in his second season at North Carolina. After the Syracuse game he said, "They made a couple more plays than we did today, and that was the difference in the game." On Monday he talked about Toney. "He's good at everything," Belichick said. "He's even a good blocker." He added, "At his age, that's pretty impressive. I don't see any weak points in his game."

Javi: When Coach Belichick says that, you frame it, hermano.

Player storylines

Toney is going for his third straight game with more than 150 receiving yards. On3's Heisman poll has him third, right behind his own quarterback, Mensah.

For Carolina, Shipp said the Tar Heels moved the ball well but need to finish drives. "We need to turn those field goals into touchdowns," he said. Rece Verhoff made all three of his field goals against Syracuse, with a long of 39 yards. Tight end Jelani Thurman caught a career-best seven passes.

What's happening on campus

This is North Carolina's 100th season playing in Kenan Stadium, which opened in 1927 and seats 50,500. The Tar Heels have won five ACC titles and played in 37 bowl games. Saturday continues a homestand for Carolina.

Miami claims five national championships: 1983, 1987, 1989, 1991 and 2001. The Canes are No. 1 in both the AP and Coaches polls.

Anything else fun and true

Miami has scored at least 33 points in every game this season, including 77 against Florida A&M. The Canes won 43-35 in overtime against Florida State.

Carolina won close road games at Pittsburgh, 21-17, and at Duke, 24-20. The Tar Heels and Syracuse have now played nine times, and Carolina still leads that series 5-4.

Ainsley: Halloween in Chapel Hill, darling. Kenan is lovely by moonlight.

Javi: I'll bring the sunglasses anyway. Canes get it done.

My call: Miami Hurricanes 35, North Carolina Tar Heels 20.

display.story_text:
Halloween night at the Coliseum, and Ohio State shows up with a quarterback who has never started a college game. Buck Holloway runs routes in the press box hallway. Sterling Ashworth-Vance narrates everything like a movie trailer.

Ohio State (6-1) at USC (6-2), Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles. It's a Big Ten game. DraftKings has Ohio State Buckeyes −6.5 with a total of 51.5. Action Network's opening number was Ohio State −7.5. My card: Ohio State Buckeyes −6.5, Over 51.5, and a final of Ohio State Buckeyes 34, USC Trojans 23.

Buck speaks for Ohio State. "That's a Columbus problem! Julian Sayin is out with the elbow he hurt at Indiana. He had 19 touchdown passes and four interceptions. Ryan Day hasn't picked between Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair. But Jeremiah Smith has 52 catches for 984 yards and 12 scores, and the bye week got most of our hurt defenders back."

Sterling speaks for USC. "In a world where a team ran for minus seventeen yards in Madison... that was us, Buck. We lost 7-24 at Wisconsin. But Jayden Maiava has 2,302 yards and 19 touchdowns. We beat Washington here, and Oregon beat us here, so I won't oversell it. Eight of the last ten meetings belong to us. Roll credits."

Here is the part that matters. Ohio State allows 13.4 points a game. Its worst offensive night was 19 points at Indiana, and the defense still won that game. USC's run game just disappeared. If the Trojans can't run, Maiava has to throw into a defense that gave Indiana 15.

Why Ohio State? The Formula and Next Man Up both back the Buckeyes. Day says the front is a "full arsenal" again, with Austin Siereveld back from illness. A young quarterback with a healthy line and Smith outside can manage this. USC's defense allows 25.0 a game.

The worry is real. Next Man Up made no quarterback change because there's no official report yet. That's a hole in its number, and Sayin's absence is the biggest news in this game. Follow The Money backs USC after the spread came down from 7.5 to 6.5, and In The Trenches also likes the Trojans.

Why the Over/Under? Ohio State scores 39.3 a game. USC scores 32.8. The Formula has 55 and Next Man Up has 58. Follow The Money likes the Under after the total fell from 55.5 to 51.5, and I won't pretend the quarterback news doesn't matter. My 34-23 adds up to 57, five and a half over the over/under 51.5.

A Border Rivalry on Halloween Night: Missouri Visits Arkansas

No. 23 Missouri (5-2, 2-2 SEC) at Arkansas (3-4, 1-3 SEC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:45 p.m. ET (6:45 p.m. Central), Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, Ark., SEC Network.

Your hosts are Delphine Arceneaux-Moss, a Missouri journalism-school style reporter who breaks obvious news with a fake ticker sound, and Bubba Fayette-Dorsey, an Ozark grade-school science teacher who calls the Hogs before every stat.

Delphine: Show me the tape! Breaking news, Bubba: it is Halloween, and there is a trophy on the field.

Bubba: Woooo, Pig! Breaking news back at you, Delphine. It's our house tonight.

Players to watch

Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons, an Ole Miss transfer, is 132 of 209 for 1,773 yards, 14 touchdowns and two interceptions. Running back Jamal Roberts leads the SEC in rushing with 867 yards and eight touchdowns on 167 carries. Wide receiver Cayden Lee has 47 catches for 678 yards and five touchdowns. On defense, Daeden Hopkins has seven sacks, and linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez has 76 tackles.

Arkansas quarterback KJ Jackson is 131 of 215 for 1,444 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions. Wide receiver Chris Marshall has 43 catches for 633 yards, second in the SEC in both. Braylen Russell leads the running backs with 205 yards. On defense, linebacker Ja'Quavion Smith has 48 tackles, and Quincy Rhodes Jr. has three sacks.

Bubba: Woooo, Pig! Seven sacks for Hopkins. Our quarterback should keep his eyes up.

What happened last week

Both teams had the week off on Oct. 24.

Missouri's last game was a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. Simmons threw for 339 yards, and Donovan Olugbode caught nine passes for 127 yards. The Tigers got into the red zone three times and came away with three points.

Arkansas' last game was a 31-21 win at Vanderbilt on Oct. 17, its first SEC win in two years. Jackson went 21 of 31 for 251 yards and ran for a touchdown. Antonio Jordan, a Warren, Ark., native, had career highs with five catches for 74 yards.

Delphine: Breaking news: the Hogs are feeling good.

Injuries and availability

No official SEC availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Silverfield said Marshall, who hurt his leg at Vanderbilt, is expected to play. Arkansas center Caden Kitler, a team captain, is listed as the starter, though Kash Courtney started at Vanderbilt. Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said wide receiver Blair is back from a hamstring injury and will be fully available. Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy has been sidelined since an offseason accident.

What the coaches are up to

Drinkwitz grew up in Alma, Ark., and has led Missouri since 2020. "I think the SEC is better when Arkansas is good," he said last fall.

Ryan Silverfield became the 35th head coach in Arkansas history the morning after last year's game. He coached Memphis against Missouri in 2023. "We know that they're going to be sound and well-coached," he said. He praised the Missouri wide zone running game and said it gets stronger in the fourth quarter.

Player storylines

Simmons faced his old school, Ole Miss, two weeks ago, and he keeps it simple. "It's just another game for me," he said. Roberts has carried the load with Hardy out. For Arkansas, Jordan showed he can make plays when Marshall is out, and now the Hogs may have both.

What's happening on campus

Razorback Stadium opened in 1938 and seats 80,000. Fans will call the Hogs, the band is known as the Best in Sight and Sound, and the fight song is "Arkansas Fight." Arkansas claims a 1964 national title.

Missouri plays at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, with Faurot Field and Marching Mizzou. The fight song is "Every True Son, Fight Tiger," and the Tigers claim a 1960 national title. This is the first SEC night game Arkansas has hosted since Oct. 19, 2024.

Anything else fun and true

The winner takes home the rivalry trophy. Missouri won the last four meetings, including 31-17 last year in Fayetteville. Arkansas last won in 2021, 34-17. Eight of the 16 games in the series were decided by one score. Only one first-year Arkansas coach has beaten Missouri: Glen Rose, 7-6 in St. Louis in 1944.

Delphine: Breaking news: Silverfield would like to be the second.

Bubba: Woooo, Pig! And the Hogs would love to call that one.

My call: Missouri Tigers 27, Arkansas Razorbacks 21.

Halloween Night in Memphis: Army Marches Into the Bluff City

Army (5-2, 4-1 American) at Memphis (6-2, 3-1 American). Saturday, Oct. 31, 8:00 p.m. ET (7:00 p.m. Central), Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis, Tenn., ESPNU.

Your hosts are Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke, a retired Army logistics officer who reads every option play like a supply chain, and Otis Delaney-Crum, a Memphis blues guitarist who sings bass in his gospel choir.

Otis: Well, hello there, friends. Welcome to Memphis, Captain. I'll hum you a riff when we score.

Thaddeus: Attention on deck. I've got my boots shined, Otis. Mission brief: run the ball, protect the ball.

Otis: Brother, that's not a song. That's a march.

Players to watch

Army quarterback Cale Hellums is the engine of the option. He has 159 carries for 840 yards and 16 rushing touchdowns, and he has completed 39 of 69 throws for 422 yards and three touchdowns. Brady Anderson leads the team with 10 catches for 163 yards. On defense, linebacker Elijah Walton has 52 tackles and linebacker Victor Afolabi has three sacks.

Memphis quarterback Marcus Stokes is 150 of 224 for 2,161 yards, 21 touchdowns and six interceptions. Running back Jaylin Carter has 128 carries for 833 yards and eight touchdowns. Tight end Hunter Tipton leads the receivers with 30 catches for 409 yards and five touchdowns. On defense, Elijah Kinsler has 5.5 sacks and linebacker Mike Montgomery has 58 tackles.

Thaddeus: Sixteen rushing touchdowns from the quarterback. Outstanding.

What happened last week

Army won 38-35 at Tulsa on Friday night, Oct. 23, for its third win in a row. The Black Knights trailed 35-28 in the fourth quarter. Hellums tied it with a 1-yard run with 1:50 left, and Dawson Jones kicked a 50-yard field goal as time ran out. Jones also made one from 51, and the school says he's the first Army kicker to make two field goals of 50 or more in one game. Hellums ran for 121 yards and three touchdowns, and Godspower Nwawuihe ran 12 times for 135 yards, including a 66-yard touchdown.

Memphis beat East Carolina 41-34 in overtime on Thursday, Oct. 22. Stokes threw for 320 yards and accounted for all five touchdowns, three throwing and two running. Jemyri Davis caught seven balls for 91 yards and two scores. The win made Memphis bowl-eligible for the 13th straight season.

Otis: Five touchdowns from one young man. That drive had a backbeat.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report had been posted for this game as of Tuesday. Early injury pages show no reported injuries for either team. Watch for the official report closer to kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Jeff Monken has led Army since 2014, and he coached Georgia Southern before that. After the Tulsa win, he said the Black Knights still need to improve, especially after a rough third quarter. Offensive coordinator Cody Worley even called a trick play at Tulsa, a 45-yard throw from slotback Zach Mundell to Anderson.

Charles Huff is in his first season at Memphis after coaching Southern Miss and Marshall. His offense moves the ball on the ground and through the air, and Stokes has thrown at least two touchdowns in all but one game.

Player storylines

Hellums scored twice on fourth-and-1 at Tulsa, including a 41-yard run on the opening drive. Army went 3-for-4 on fourth down that night. For Memphis, Stokes threw for 384 yards at Boise State and 318 at Charlotte.

What's happening on campus

Memphis has a long football story that began in 1912, and the Tigers have been bowl-eligible every year since 2014. Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium opened in 1965 and seats 58,325.

At West Point, the Black Knights keep one big date circled every year, the Navy game.

Anything else fun and true

The two teams have not played each other in the regular season in the last 10 years. Army beat Tulane 20-17 on Oct. 10, and Memphis lost 31-17 at Tulane six days later, so Tulane is the one shared opponent so far.

Army's defense had two sacks, five tackles for loss, an interception and a blocked punt at Tulsa, and Walton made 10 tackles.

Otis: Captain, you bring the march, and I'll bring the blues.

Thaddeus: Copy that, Otis. And beat Navy.

Otis: Go Tigers Go.

My call: Memphis Tigers 31, Army Black Knights 28.

Halloween on the Blue Turf: Texas State Visits Boise State

Texas State (4-3, 2-1 Pac-12) at No. 20 Boise State (6-1, 3-0 Pac-12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 10:00 p.m. ET (8:00 p.m. Mountain), Albertsons Stadium, Boise, Idaho, CW.

Your hosts are Yesenia Calderwood, a Texas State fan who floats the San Marcos River with a sun hat and a radio, and Thatcher Bluestem, a Boise State fan whose car, pancakes and opinions are all blue.

Thatcher: Paint it blue! Welcome to Boise, Yesenia. Bring sunglasses. The field looks even bluer in person.

Yesenia: Eat 'em up, Cats! I brought a sun hat, Thatcher. It's going to be cold, isn't it?

Players to watch

Texas State quarterback Brad Jackson is 133 of 194 for 1,606 yards, 14 touchdowns and five interceptions, and he's a runner too. The school says he has 26 career rushing touchdowns. Running back Torrance Burgess Jr. has 118 carries for 889 yards and five touchdowns. Wide receiver Chris Dawn Jr. leads the team with 36 catches for 396 yards and four touchdowns. On defense, Jayden Bradley has 47 tackles and Tymere Jackson has 2.5 sacks.

Boise State quarterback Maddux Madsen is 124 of 189 for 1,445 yards and 14 touchdowns. The school says he has gone seven straight games without an interception, the first Bronco starter to do that since the team joined the top level of college football in 1996. Running back Dylan Riley has 140 carries for 963 yards and eight touchdowns. Freshman receiver Rasean Jones has 29 catches for 437 yards. Linebacker Boen Phelps leads the defense with 41 tackles, and linebacker Jayden Virgin-Morgan has three sacks.

Thatcher: Seven games, no interceptions. That's bluer than a cloudless October sky.

What happened last week

Texas State beat Utah State 20-17 at homecoming on Oct. 24. Jacob Bonilla kicked a 37-yard field goal with less than two minutes left, after making one from 51 earlier. Jaylen Jenkins returned a kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown, and Jackson ran for a score. A week earlier, the Bobcats set a school record with 716 yards in a 66-27 win over Colorado State.

Boise State won 31-10 at Washington State. Riley ran 13 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns, and Madsen threw a touchdown to Cam Bates. It was Boise State's first win ever in Pullman and its sixth win in a row.

Yesenia: A 100-yard kickoff return at homecoming. Now that's going with the flow.

Injuries and availability

The official Pac-12 availability report hadn't been posted as of Tuesday and usually comes out on game day. Unofficial notes don't list Madsen, Riley or Jackson. Texas State's Cole Snodgrass is listed as out.

What the coaches are up to

G.J. Kinne has 27 wins at Texas State, which ties him for second among Bobcat coaches at the Division I level. His teams are 17-7 at home. After the Utah State game he called the offense a bad dream, so expect him to want a better night.

Spencer Danielson won his 30th game at Boise State last week, the eighth Bronco head coach to get there. Boise State has started 3-0 in league play in each of his three full seasons. His teams love to run the ball and keep it away from the other side.

Player storylines

Madsen moved into fourth in Boise State history with 631 career completions and has 64 career touchdown throws. He's 17-1 as a starter in league games. For Texas State, Jackson and Burgess give the Bobcats two runners who can break a long one.

What's happening on campus

The blue turf at Albertsons Stadium is one of the most famous fields in the country, and the stadium seats 36,387. Boise State is now bowl-eligible for the 29th season in a row. The school says only Georgia has a longer active run.

Last week a Bronco player carried the Dan Paul Hammer onto the field in Pullman, a Boise State tradition.

Anything else fun and true

This is the first meeting between Texas State and Boise State. Both schools are new to the Pac-12 this season. The Bobcats come from the warm Hill Country, and the Broncos come from the foothills, so a Halloween night in Boise will be a change of scenery for Yesenia.

Texas State drew 18,587 fans for homecoming last week. Boise State has scored 30 or more points in six straight games for the first time since 2023.

Yesenia: First meeting, new conference, blue grass. I'm floating into the unknown, Thatcher.

Thatcher: And we'll paint it blue, Yesenia. Every inch.

My call: Boise State Broncos 38, Texas State Bobcats 26.

Brad Jackson has 14 touchdown passes, and Torrance Burgess Jr. has 889 rushing yards. Go with the flow, y'all."

Thatcher speaks for Boise State. "Paint it blue! Maddux Madsen still has zero interceptions. Seven games, friends. Dylan Riley has 963 rushing yards, and he ran for 128 and two touchdowns at Washington State. That's six straight wins,."

Northern Illinois (0-7) at UNLV (4-3), Saturday at 10:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. It's a Mountain West game. DraftKings has UNLV Rebels −23.5 with a total of 53.5. Nola speaks for Northern Illinois. "I'm calm. Very calm. We were tied with Hawai'i in the second quarter, and then the crop got hailed on. DeAree Rogers caught eight balls for 115 yards and two touchdowns. Telly Johnson Jr. has 502 rushing yards. The roots are still in the ground."

Action Network's opening number was UNLV −24.5, and it has come down a point. Both The Formula and Next Man Up like the Huskies. My final has UNLV by twenty.

display.fanatic_story:
Halloween Night on the Strip: Northern Illinois Visits UNLV

Northern Illinois (0-7, 0-3 Mountain West) at UNLV (4-3, 2-1 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 10:30 p.m. ET (7:30 p.m. Pacific), Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas, CBSSN.

Your hosts are Nola Brandvik, a Northern Illinois agricultural scientist from DeKalb who thinks about the Huskies like a corn crop, and Vegas Monroe-Kalani, a former headliner dancer who calls every UNLV game a show and rates the opening act.

Vegas: The show starts Saturday night. Welcome to Las Vegas, Nola.

Nola: Thank you. I'm calm. Very calm. I brought a sweater. It's October.

Players to watch

Northern Illinois quarterback Taron Dickens is 138 of 210 for 1,364 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions. Running back Telly Johnson Jr. has 95 carries for 502 yards and four touchdowns. Wide receiver DeAree Rogers leads the team with 57 catches for 537 yards and four touchdowns. On defense, Jack Murray has 49 tackles and Avery Jones has two sacks.

UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold is 108 of 182 for 1,386 yards, 10 touchdowns and two interceptions. The school says he leads the league with 16 total touchdowns, 10 throwing and six running. Running back Jai'Den Thomas has 112 carries for 543 yards and three touchdowns. Wide receiver Kayden McGee has 16 catches for 330 yards and four touchdowns. Safety Jake Pope leads the defense with 63 tackles, Tre Fulton has 3.5 sacks and Mumu Bin-Wahad has three interceptions.

What happened last week

Northern Illinois lost 56-21 at home to Hawai'i on Oct. 24. The game was tied at 14 in the second quarter before Hawai'i scored 35 points in a row. Rogers caught eight balls for 115 yards and two touchdowns, of 49 and 25 yards. Dickens threw for 171 yards, and Johnson ran for 63.

UNLV had an open date on Oct. 24, its second bye of the season. The Rebels' last game was a 41-31 loss at Air Force on Oct. 17. McGee caught five balls for 99 yards and two touchdowns that day, and Arnold ran for a score.

Nola: After the Hawai'i game I stared at my cornfield photo for 30 seconds. It helped.

Injuries and availability

The official Mountain West availability report hadn't been posted as of Tuesday and usually comes out on game day. Unofficial notes from mid-October list UNLV receiver DeAngelo Irvin Jr. as out. McGee was listed as questionable that week but played at Air Force. Dickens was listed as questionable before the Hawai'i game and played.

What the coaches are up to

Rob Harley was the Huskies' defensive coordinator until he was promoted to interim head coach when Thomas Hammock resigned on Feb. 18 to return to the NFL. After the Hawai'i game, Harley said, "We have to find a way, and it starts with me first, to find a way to increase the consistency with the base stuff that we do."

Dan Mullen is in his second season at UNLV after being hired on Dec. 12, 2024. The Rebels are 7-2 at home under Mullen. This week he talked about tackling and getting healthy after the break.

Player storylines

Rogers is on a roll for the Huskies. Arnold, an Auburn transfer, didn't throw his first interception of the season until the North Dakota State game on Oct. 10. That came after 142 straight throws without one.

What's happening on campus

UNLV is throwing a Halloween party at Allegiant Stadium. The Rebel Village Fan Zone in Lot C is free, and a band called The Lucky Devils plays before the game.

Halloween is also Nevada Day, the day Nevada became the 36th state in 1864. UNLV last played on Halloween in 2020, when it hosted Nevada in the first game ever played at Allegiant Stadium.

Northern Illinois is in its first season in the Mountain West as a football-only member, so this trip is all new.

Anything else fun and true

The Huskies have won all five meetings with UNLV, the latest 38-30 in 2015. UNLV is still looking for its first win in the series.

UNLV says it has already played in five different time zones this season and is the only school in the top level of college football scheduled to do that in 2026. The Rebels are 2-7 all-time on Halloween, and their last Halloween win was 35-31 over San Jose State in 1992.

Vegas: Saturday night, under the lights, on Halloween. That's my kind of opening act.

Nola: Knee-high by the Fourth of July. Or by Halloween. I'll take either.

My call: UNLV Rebels 35, Northern Illinois Huskies 15.

Now the room. The Formula has Oregon State 30-27, takes Fresno State and the Under. Next Man Up has Oregon State 29-26, takes Fresno State and likes the Under. The Formula: "Three points. Halloween treat for the home team."

Next Man Up: "Crandall back at corner helps Oregon State, but the Bulldogs still have the defense."

Halloween Night in the Valley: Oregon State Visits Fresno State

Oregon State (5-2, 3-0 Pac-12) at Fresno State (4-3, 1-2 Pac-12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 11:00 p.m. ET (8:00 p.m. Pacific), Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno, Calif., USA Net.

Your hosts are Juniper Ostrowski, an Oregon State forestry PhD who charts treetop weather and red-zone efficiency and corrects everyone's tree metaphors, and Rosalind "Roz" Ayala, a Fresno State fan and raisin-grower's daughter who calls herself the Valley Girl, from a different valley.

Roz: Not that Valley, babe! Welcome to Fresno on Halloween night.

Juniper: Measure twice, kick once! I packed a costume. I came as a Douglas fir.

Roz: Of course you did.

Players to watch

Oregon State quarterback Braden Atkinson is 189 of 273 for 2,604 yards, 24 touchdowns and just two interceptions. The Oregonian says he has thrown 129 straight throws without an interception, and the school record is 182 by Matt Moore. Wide receiver Jesse Legree has 46 catches for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns. Running back AJ Newberry has 431 yards. On defense, linebacker Aiden Sullivan has 53 tackles and linebacker Takari Hickle has six sacks.

Fresno State quarterback Jayden Mandal is 123 of 195 for 1,393 yards, eight touchdowns and one interception, and he has run for two scores. Rayshon Luke leads the rushers with 333 yards, and Josiah Freeman leads the receivers with 32 catches for 445 yards. Linebacker K'vion Thunderbird has 61 tackles, and defensive back Simeon Harris has three interceptions.

Juniper: Legree with 14 touchdowns is a giant sequoia. Tall, strong and impossible to miss.

What happened last week

Both teams had an open date on Oct. 24. Oregon State's last game was a 48-30 home win over Washington State on Oct. 17, when Atkinson threw for 347 yards and three touchdowns and Newberry ran for 105 yards and caught five balls for 120 more.

Fresno State lost 26-23 at San Diego State that same night. Bryson Donelson ran for a touchdown.

Injuries and availability

The official Pac-12 availability report usually posts on game day. The Oregonian reports that Oregon State cornerback TJ Crandall, who missed the Washington State game with a concussion, is good to go. Receiver Adonis McDaniel, who tore his Achilles in the winter, is expected to make his season debut. For Fresno State, Luke was listed as questionable with a concussion after the San Diego State game, so watch for his status on Saturday.

What the coaches are up to

JaMarcus Shephard is 5-2 in his first season at Oregon State. He was hired on Nov. 28, 2025. Matt Entz is 13-7 at Fresno State and won two FCS national championships at North Dakota State.

Roz: Coach Entz knows big games. Two national titles is a lot of raisins.

Juniper: That is not how raisins work.

Player storylines

McDaniel and Atkinson both came to Corvallis from Mercer. If McDaniel plays, two old teammates get to share a big Saturday night again.

Mandal is in his first season as a starter, and he has protected the ball all year with just one interception in seven games. He has also caught a 21-yard ball this year, so keep an eye on trick plays.

The Beavers have won five straight and have not trailed in any of them. Last year's meeting went the other way, a 36-27 Fresno State win in Corvallis.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Fresno, and the Bulldogs haven't played on Oct. 31 since 2009. Fresno State is 7-4-1 on Halloween, including 5-0-1 at home. Oregon State is 4-9-1 on Halloween, so Juniper might want to keep that Douglas fir costume handy for luck.

Fresno State plays on Jim Sweeney Field, and Valley Children's Stadium seats 41,031. Oregon State's home, Reser Stadium, seats 43,363.

Anything else fun and true

Oregon State sits first in the Pac-12 at 3-0 in league games, and the Beavers have 17 sacks and nine takeaways. Fresno State's defense is second in the league in scoring, according to The Oregonian.

Juniper: A good defense is like an old-growth forest. You don't get through it quickly.

Roz: And a good offense is like a raisin. Sweet, a little wrinkly, and gone before you know it.

Juniper: I'm writing that down for the podcast.

My call: Oregon State Beavers 30, Fresno State Bulldogs 27.
